cleaned_devanagari_text:
प्रकरणम् १ ]    हिन्दी टीका सहित    ( ३ )

तृतीयामें द्वितीया-उक्त कर्म और गमनसम्बन्धी कृत्य, शिल्प, सीमन्त, चूडा, अन्नप्राशन, गृहकर्म[?] भी शुभ होते हैं । रिक्ता ४।९।१४ में अग्निकर्म, मारणकर्म, बन्धन, कृत्य, शस्त्र, विष, अग्निदाह, घात आदि विषयक कृत्य शुभ और मंगलकृत्य अशुभ होते हैं । पञ्चमीमें समस्त शुभकृत्य सिद्धि देते हैं, परन्तु ऋण (कर्जा) इसमें न देना; देनेसे नाश हो जाता है । षष्ठीमें तैलाभ्यंग, पितृकर्म और दन्तकाष्ठके विना सभी मंगल-पौष्टिक कर्म करने, तथा संग्रामोपयोगी शिल्प, वास्तु, भूषण, वस्त्र भी शुभ हैं । सप्तमीमें जो जो कृत्य द्वि॰ तृ॰ पं॰ ष॰[?] में कहे हैं वे सिद्ध होते हैं । अष्टमीमें रणोपयोगी कर्म, वास्तुकृत्य, शिल्प, राजकृत्य, लिखनेका काम, स्त्री, रत्न, भूषणकृत्य शुभ होते हैं । दशमीमें जो जो द्वि॰ तृ॰ पं॰ स॰ में कहे हैं वे सिद्ध होते हैं । एकादशीमें व्रत-उपवासादि समस्त धर्मकृत्य, देवताका उत्सव, वास्तुकर्म, सांग्रामिक कर्म, शिल्प शुभ होते हैं । द्वादशीमें समस्त स्थावर-जंगमके कर्म, पुष्टिकारक शुभकर्म सभी सिद्ध होते हैं । त्रयोदशीमें द्वि॰ तृ॰ पं॰ स॰ के उक्त कृत्य शुभदायक होते हैं । पूर्णिमामें यज्ञक्रिया, पौष्टिक, मङ्गल, संग्रामोपयोगी, वास्तुकर्म, विवाह, शिल्प, समस्तभूषणादि सिद्ध होते हैं । अमावास्यामें पितृकर्ममात्र होते हैं, कहीं शाबरोक्त उग्रकर्म भी कहे हैं । अन्य मंगल-पौष्टिकोत्सवादि कृत्य न करने ॥ ३ ॥ (अनुष्टुप्)

तिथीनां संज्ञा, सिद्धियोगाश्च
नन्दा च भद्रा च जया च रिक्ता पूर्णा तिथयोऽधममध्यशस्ताः ।
सितेऽसिते शस्तसमाधमाः स्युः सितज्ञभौमार्किगुरौ च सिद्धाः ॥ ४ ॥

तिथियोंकी तीन आवृत्तिमें नन्दादि पंच संज्ञा क्रमसे हैं, जैसे— १।६।११ । नन्दा,
content_en:
[ṭīkā] (commentary continuing on verse 3) On the third (tṛtīyā) the acts stated for the second, and acts connected with travel, craft-work (śilpa), sīmantonnayana, cūḍākarma (tonsure), annaprāśana and household work[?] are also auspicious. On the Riktā tithis (lunar days) — the 4th, 9th and 14th — acts involving fire, killing rites, binding, abhicāra (harming rites), weapons, poison, arson, striking and the like are auspicious, while festive and auspicious acts are inauspicious. On the fifth all auspicious acts succeed, but a loan must not be granted on it; granting one brings ruin. On the sixth, excepting oil-massage, rites for the ancestors (pitṛ-karma) and use of the tooth-stick, all festive and strengthening (pauṣṭika) acts may be performed; craft-work for war, building (vāstu), ornaments and garments are likewise auspicious. On the seventh, whatever acts are stated for the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 6th[?] succeed. On the eighth, acts of war, building, craft-work, royal business, writing, matters concerning women, gems and ornaments are auspicious. On the tenth, whatever is stated for the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 7th succeeds. On the eleventh all religious acts such as vows and fasts, festivals of the deities, building, martial acts and craft-work are auspicious. On the twelfth all acts concerning immovable and movable property, and all strengthening auspicious acts, succeed. On the thirteenth the acts stated for the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 7th are auspicious. On the full-moon day sacrificial rites, strengthening rites, festive acts, acts for war, building, marriage, craft-work and all ornament-work succeed. On the new-moon day only rites for the ancestors are performed; in some places the fierce rites taught in the Śābara [tantra] are also mentioned. Other festive, strengthening and celebratory acts are not to be done. || 3 || (anuṣṭubh)

[Verse 4 — The names of the tithis, and the siddhi-yogas]
Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Riktā and Pūrṇā [are the names of the tithis]. In the bright fortnight (sita) the [three successive rounds of] tithis are inferior, middling and excellent [respectively]; in the dark fortnight (asita) they are excellent, ordinary and inferior. And they are siddha (accomplishing, i.e. they form siddhi-yogas) on Śukra (Friday), Jña/Budha (Wednesday), Bhauma (Tuesday), Ārki/Śani (Saturday) and Guru (Thursday) respectively. || 4 ||

[ṭīkā] The five designations beginning with Nandā apply in order across the three rounds of the tithis, thus: 1, 6, 11 — Nandā; ...
ocr_review_note: ṭīkā, tṛtīyā clause: 'गृहमे' — expanded as गृहकर्म[?]; गृहारम्भ is an equally possible reading, the akṣaras after गृह are lost. ṭīkā, saptamī clause: 'व०' — read as ष॰ (ṣaṣṭhī)[?] by parallel with the daśamī/trayodaśī clauses, but the abbreviation letter is genuinely unclear. Separately (typo-obvious, corrected silently, not flagged): the verse number printed by OCR as '॥७॥' is ॥४॥ — confirmed by the ṭīkā closing '॥ ४ ॥' in the following chunk and by the verse sequence 3→5.

cleaned_devanagari_text: २।७।१२ । भद्रा, ३।८।१३ । जया, ४।९।१४ । रिक्ता, ५।१०।१५ । पूर्णा संज्ञक हैं । इनके जैसे नाम वैसे ही फल भी हैं । तथा शुक्लपक्षमें पूर्व त्रिभाग (प्रतिपदासे पंचमीपर्यन्त) अधम — अर्थात् इनमें चन्द्रमा क्षीण ही रहता है — द्वितीय त्रिभाग (पंचमीसे दशमीपर्यन्त) मध्यम और अंतिम त्रिभाग (दशमीसे पूर्णिमापर्यन्त) शुभ होते हैं; तथा कृष्णपक्षमें पू॰ त्रि॰ (पंचमीपर्यन्त) शुभ, म॰ त्रि॰ (पंचमीसे दशमीपर्यन्त) मध्यम और अं॰ त्रि॰ (एकादशीसे अमा॰ पर्यन्त) अधम होते हैं । चतुर्थपादका अर्थ यह है कि शुक्रवारके दिन नन्दा १।६।११, बुधको भद्रा २।७।१२, मंगलको जया ३।८।१३, शनिवारको रिक्ता ४।९।१४, गुरुवारके दिन पूर्णा ५।१०।१५ सिद्धि देनेवाली हैं । इसका प्रयोजन यह है कि "सिद्धा तिथिर्हन्ति समस्तदोषान्" इत्यादि — मासशून्य, मासदग्ध, दिनदग्ध आदि दोषोंको हटाकर कार्य सिद्ध कर देती है ॥ ४ ॥ (उपजाति)
content_en:
[ṭīkā] (commentary on verse 4, continued) — 2, 7, 12 are called Bhadrā; 3, 8, 13 Jayā; 4, 9, 14 Riktā; 5, 10, 15 Pūrṇā. Their effects correspond to their names. Further, in the bright fortnight (śukla pakṣa) the first third (from pratipadā up to pañcamī) is inferior — that is, in these the Moon still remains waned; the second third (from pañcamī up to daśamī) is middling; and the last third (from daśamī up to pūrṇimā) is auspicious. In the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇa pakṣa) the first third (up to pañcamī) is auspicious, the middle third (from pañcamī up to daśamī) middling, and the last third (from ekādaśī up to amāvāsyā) inferior.

The sense of the fourth pāda is this: on Friday, Nandā (1, 6, 11); on Wednesday, Bhadrā (2, 7, 12); on Tuesday, Jayā (3, 8, 13); on Saturday, Riktā (4, 9, 14); on Thursday, Pūrṇā (5, 10, 15) — these are the givers of siddhi (accomplishment). The purpose of this is [expressed in the maxim] "siddhā tithir hanti samasta-doṣān" — 'a siddha tithi (lunar day so combined with its vāra, weekday) destroys all doṣas (afflictions)' — that is, it removes doṣas such as māsa-śūnya (month-void), māsa-dagdha (month-burnt) and dina-dagdha (day-burnt), and brings the undertaking to accomplishment. || 4 || (upajāti)

( ४ )    मुहूर्तचिन्तामणि    [ शुभाशुभ-

रव्यादिवारेषु यथाक्रमनिषिद्धतिथिभानि
नन्दा भद्रा नन्दिकाख्या जया च रिक्ता भद्रा पूर्णसंज्ञा हताऽर्कात्[?] ।
याम्यं त्वाष्ट्रं वैश्वदेवं धनिष्ठाऽऽर्यम्णं ज्येष्ठाऽन्त्यं रवेर्दग्धभं[?] स्यात् ॥ ५ ॥

सूर्यादिवारोंमें नन्दादि उक्त तिथि क्रमसे अशुभ (घातक) होती हैं । जैसे रविवारको नन्दा १।६।११, सोमवारको भद्रा २।७।१२, मंगलको नन्दा १।६।११, बुधको जया ३।८।१३, गुरुवारको रिक्ता ४।९।१४, शुक्रवारको भद्रा २।७।१२, शनिवारको पूर्णा ५।१०।१५ । ऐसे ही नक्षत्र भी — जैसे रविवारको भरणी, सोमवारको चित्रा, मंगलको उत्तराषाढा, बुधको धनिष्ठा, गुरुवारको उत्तराफल्गुनी, शुक्रको ज्येष्ठा, शनिवारको रेवती दग्धनक्षत्र होते हैं । उक्त घातक तिथि तथा ये दग्धनक्षत्र शुभकृत्यमें वर्ज्य हैं ॥ ५ ॥ (शालिनीवृत्त)

तिथिचक्रम् ।
| तिथि | स्वामी | संज्ञा[?] | शुक्ल | कृष्ण | सिद्धि | [?] |
| १ | ... | नन्दा | अधम[?] | शुभ | ... | ... |

content_en:
[Verse 5 — The tithis and nakṣatras prohibited, in order, on the vāras (weekdays) beginning with Sunday]
Nandā, Bhadrā, the one called Nandikā (i.e. Nandā again), Jayā, Riktā, Bhadrā, and the one named Pūrṇā — these are hata (struck down, destructive)[?] counting from Arka (Sunday). Yāmya (Bharaṇī), Tvāṣṭra (Citrā), Vaiśvadeva (Uttarāṣāḍhā), Dhaniṣṭhā, Āryamṇa (Uttaraphalgunī), Jyeṣṭhā and the last (Revatī) — these are the dagdha (burnt) nakṣatras (lunar mansions)[?] counting from Ravi (Sunday). || 5 ||

[ṭīkā] On the vāras beginning with Sunday the aforesaid tithis (lunar days), Nandā and the rest, are in order inauspicious (ghātaka, destructive). Thus: on Sunday Nandā (1, 6, 11); on Monday Bhadrā (2, 7, 12); on Tuesday Nandā (1, 6, 11); on Wednesday Jayā (3, 8, 13); on Thursday Riktā (4, 9, 14); on Friday Bhadrā (2, 7, 12); on Saturday Pūrṇā (5, 10, 15). In the same way the nakṣatras also: on Sunday Bharaṇī, on Monday Citrā, on Tuesday Uttarāṣāḍhā, on Wednesday Dhaniṣṭhā, on Thursday Uttaraphalgunī, on Friday Jyeṣṭhā, on Saturday Revatī are the dagdha (burnt) nakṣatras. The aforesaid destructive tithis and these dagdha nakṣatras are to be shunned in auspicious undertakings. || 5 || (śālinī metre)

[ṭīkā] Tithi-cakra (table of the tithis) — columns: tithi | lord | designation[?] | bright fortnight | dark fortnight | siddhi | [?]; first rows give Nandā — inferior[?] — auspicious ..., and for the second tithi Brahmā ... 'accomplishment of the undertaking'[?]. The remainder of the table is not recoverable from this scan.
ocr_review_note: Verse 5 pāda 2: OCR 'बृताकंत्' reconstructed as हताऽर्कात्[?] ('destructive, counting from Sunday') on the strength of the ṭīkā's gloss 'अशुभ (घातक)' and the śālinī syllable count; the printed akṣaras themselves are lost. Verse 5 pāda 4: OCR 'रवेदग्धम स्यात्' — रवेर्दग्धभं[?] adopted; रवेर्दग्धं is equally possible, one syllable is uncertain (the sense, 'the dagdha nakṣatras from Sunday onward', is secure from the ṭīkā). Tithi-cakra table at foot of page: column header 'सला' read as संज्ञा[?]; one header cell ('ओमि') is wholly illegible[?]; cell 'अम' read as अधम[?]; cell 'कार्य॑सायन' read as कार्यसाधन[?]. The table's grid is broken up by the OCR line order and most cells cannot be assigned to a row or column with confidence — the table is therefore rendered only as a skeleton, not reconstructed.

प्रकरणम् १ ]    हिन्दी टीका सहित    ( ५ )

क्रकचादिनिन्द्ययोगाः
षष्ठ्यादितिथयो मन्दाद्विलोमं प्रतिपद्बुधे ।
सप्तम्यर्केऽधमाः षष्ठ्याद्यमाश्च[?] रददावने ॥ ६ ॥

शनिवारसे विपरीत तथा षष्ठीसे सीधे क्रमसे गिननेमें, तथा प्रतिपदाको बुध, सप्तमीको रवि — अधम (शुभकार्यमें वर्जनीय) क्रकचयोग होता है । पंचांगोंमें इसे वारदग्ध लिखते हैं । इनकी सुगमता यह भी है कि, तिथि-वार जोड़नेसे १३ जिस दिन हों वही वा॰ द॰ । जैसे शनिवारकी षष्ठी, शुक्रकी सप्तमी, बृहस्पतिवारकी अष्टमी, बुधकी नवमी, मंगलकी दशमी, चंद्रवारकी एकादशी, रविवारकी द्वादशी; और बुधकी प्रतिपदा, रविकी सप्तमी — ये पृथक् २ ही कही हैं । और षष्ठी, प्रतिपदा, अमावस्याके दिन काष्ठविशेष नीम आदिसे दंतधावन (दातुन) न करना; किसी आचार्यके मतसे नवमी तथा रविवारको भी वर्जित है ॥ ६ ॥ (अनुष्टुप्) ।

कृत्यविशेषे निषिद्धतिथयः
षष्ठ्यष्टमीभूतविधुक्षयेषु नो सेवेत ना तैलं पलं क्षुरं रतम् ।
नाभ्यञ्जने विश्वदशाद्विके तिथौ धात्रीफलैः स्नानममाद्रिगोष्वसत् ॥ ७ ॥

षष्ठीके दिन तैलाभ्यंग, अष्टमीको मांसभोजन, चतुर्दशीको क्षौर, अमावस्याके दिन स्त्रीसंभोग मनुष्य न करे । किसीका मत है कि, मैथुन सभी पर्वदिनोंमें न करना — चतुर्दशी, कृष्णाष्टमी, अमावस्या, पूर्णिमा, सूर्यसंक्रांति ये पर्व होते हैं । उक्त कामोंमें तिथि तत्कालकी मानी जाती है, उदयव्यापिनी नहीं । तथा त्रयोदशी, दशमी, द्वितीयाके दिन तैलाभ्यंग (उबटन) न करना; यह नियम केवल मलापकर्षस्नानमात्रको ब्राह्मणरहित तीन वर्णोंको है । और अमावस्या, सप्तमी, नवमीको आमलेके चूर्णसे स्नान न करना — करनेसे धन एवं संतति क्षीण होती है; अन्य दिनों तिलकल्कसहित आमलेसे स्नान पुण्य देता है । यह वैद्यक शास्त्रसे भी स्नानकी औषधी वर्णकांतिकारक है ॥ ७ ॥ (इन्द्रवंशा) ।

दग्धादियोगचतुष्टयम्
content_en:
[Verse 6 — The reprehensible yogas beginning with Krakaca]
The tithis (lunar days) beginning with the sixth, [reckoned] in reverse order from Manda (Saturn, i.e. Saturday); and pratipadā (the first) on Budha (Wednesday) and saptamī (the seventh) on Arka (Sunday) — [these vāra-tithi combinations] are inferior [and form the Krakaca yoga]. And the sixth, the first and the amā (new-moon day)[?] [are prohibited] for tooth-cleaning. || 6 ||

[ṭīkā] Counting backwards from Saturday and forwards from the sixth [tithi], and further pratipadā on Wednesday and saptamī on Sunday, there arises the inferior Krakaca yoga (to be shunned in auspicious work). In the pañcāṅgas (almanacs) it is written as vāra-dagdha. An easy rule for these is also this: whichever day the tithi and the vāra (weekday), added together, come to 13, that day is vāra-dagdha. Thus: the sixth on Saturday, the seventh on Friday, the eighth on Thursday, the ninth on Wednesday, the tenth on Tuesday, the eleventh on Monday, the twelfth on Sunday; and pratipadā on Wednesday and saptamī on Sunday — these two are stated separately. Also, on the sixth, on pratipadā and on the new-moon day one should not clean the teeth with a particular wood such as nīm; in the opinion of some ācāryas the ninth and Sunday are prohibited as well. || 6 || (anuṣṭubh)

[Verse 7 — Tithis prohibited for particular acts]
On the sixth, the eighth, the bhūta (fourteenth) and the waning-away of the Moon (amāvāsyā, new moon), a man should not resort, respectively, to oil, meat, the razor and sexual union. Nor should anointing [with oil] be done on the viśva (thirteenth), the tenth and the second tithi; and bathing with dhātrī (āmalaka) fruits on the amā (new moon), the adri (seventh) and the go (ninth) is not good. || 7 ||

[ṭīkā] On the sixth a man should not take an oil-massage, on the eighth not eat meat, on the fourteenth not shave, on the new-moon day not have intercourse with a woman. Some hold that intercourse is to be avoided on all parvan days — the fourteenth, the dark-fortnight eighth, the new moon, the full moon and the solar saṃkrānti are the parvans. In these matters the tithi current at the actual moment is taken, not the one prevailing at sunrise. Further, on the thirteenth, tenth and second one should not take an oil-massage (ubṭan); this rule applies only to the mere cleansing bath, and to the three varṇas excluding the brāhmaṇa. And on the new moon, the seventh and the ninth one should not bathe with āmalaka powder — doing so diminishes wealth and progeny; on other days bathing with āmalaka together with sesame paste yields merit. By the medical śāstra too this bathing-drug is held to enhance complexion and lustre. || 7 || (indravaṃśā)

[Verse 9 — the Yamaghaṇṭa yoga, by vāra × nakṣatra]
On the vāras (weekdays) beginning with the Sun, the tithis[?] occur [as stated above]; [and now] Maghā, Viśākhā, Śiva (Ārdrā), Mūla, Vahni (Kṛttikā), Brāhma (Rohiṇī) and Kara (Hasta) — [these nakṣatras, taken] from Arka (Sunday) onward, are called Yamaghaṇṭaka[?]. They are to be shunned in auspicious work, and must without fail be avoided for setting out on a journey. || 9 ||

[ṭīkā] Maghā on Sunday, Viśākhā on Monday, Ārdrā on Tuesday, Mūla on Wednesday[?], Kṛttikā on Thursday[?], Rohiṇī on Friday[?], Hasta on Saturday — these form the Yamaghaṇṭa yoga. All these — Dagdha, the one called Viṣa, Hutāśana and Yamaghaṇṭa — are prohibited in auspicious work, and are especially to be avoided for a journey. For unavoidable undertakings their parihāra (remedial cancellation) is also given in other treatises: that the consideration [holds] chiefly [in the region of] the Vindhya range[?] ... and not in other countries; and further, if a benefic graha stands in a kendra or trikoṇa from the lagna, then their doṣa (affliction) does not apply. And some hold that only the 8 ghaṭīs of the Yamaghaṇṭa are to be avoided. Vasiṣṭha's view is that the four yogas give their evil result by day and not by night. || 9 || (upendra[vajrā])

Prakaraṇa 1 — with the Hindī ṭīkā (commentary) · page (7)

DOṢAS ARISING FROM THE TITHI–NAKṢATRA COMBINATION

(11cd) Likewise censured [in auspicious work] are Sārpa (Āśleṣā) on the twelfth tithi (lunar day), and Vaiśva (Uttarāṣāḍhā) on the first.
(12) Anurādhā on the second, and Pitrya (Maghā) on the fifth; the fixed Uttarā nakṣatras (lunar mansions) on the third, and Rohiṇī on the eleventh.
(13) Svātī and Citrā on the thirteenth; Hasta and Rākṣasa (Mūla) on the seventh; Kṛttikā on the ninth, Pūrvabhādrapadā on the eighth, and Rohiṇī[?] on the sixth.

[ṭīkā] The doṣas (afflictions) belonging to the tithi–nakṣatra combination are stated: Āśleṣā on the twelfth, Uttarāṣāḍhā on the first (pratipadā), Anurādhā on the second, the three Uttarās on the third, Rohiṇī on the eleventh, Svātī and Citrā on the thirteenth, Hasta and Mūla on the seventh, Kṛttikā on the ninth, Pūrvabhādrapadā on the eighth, Maghā on the fifth — these are to be shunned in auspicious undertakings. (11–13)

THE ŚŪNYA (VOID) NAKṢATRAS IN THE MONTHS BEGINNING WITH CAITRA

(14) [In Caitra] Ka (Rohiṇī) and Dasra (Aśvinī); [in Vaiśākha] Tvāṣṭra (Citrā) and Vāyu (Svātī); [in Jyeṣṭha] Vaiśva (Uttarāṣāḍhā) and Ijya (Puṣya); [in Āṣāḍha] Bhaga (Pūrvaphālgunī) and Vāsava (Dhaniṣṭhā); [in Śrāvaṇa] Vaiśva (Uttarāṣāḍhā) and Śruti (Śravaṇa); [in Bhādrapada] Pāśin (Śatabhiṣā) and Pauṣṇa (Revatī); [in Āśvina] Ajapād (Pūrvabhādrapadā); [in Kārtika] Agni (Kṛttikā) and Pitrya (Maghā).
(15) [In Mārgaśīrṣa] Citrā and [Viśākhā?]; [in Pauṣa] Śiva (Ārdrā), Aśvi (Aśvinī) and Arka (Hasta); [in Māgha] Śruti (Śravaṇa) and Mūla; [in Phālguna] Yama (Bharaṇī) and Indra (Jyeṣṭhā). In the months beginning with Caitra these are called the śūnya (void) stars, and they bring destruction of wealth.

THE BURNT (DAGDHA) LAGNAS ON ODD TITHIS

(17) Counting from the beginning of the fortnight, on the odd tithis (lunar days) these lagnas (ascendants) [are void]: Ghaṭa (Kumbha) and Eṇa[?]; Mṛgendra (Siṃha) and Nakra (Makara); Mithuna and Aṅganā (Kanyā); Jhaṣa[?] (Mīna), Karka and Hari (Siṃha); Haya (Dhanus) and Antya (Mīna); Go (Vṛṣa) and Antya (Mīna). The lagna void for a given tithi is inauspicious.

[ṭīkā] Reckoning from the pratipadā (first day of the fortnight), on the odd tithis these lagnas are void: on the first, Makara[?]; on the third, Makara and Siṃha; on the fifth, Mithuna and Kanyā; on the seventh, Dhanus and Karka; on the ninth, Siṃha and Karka; on the eleventh, Dhanus and Mīna. These void lagnas are to be shunned in auspicious works. (17) (Indravajrā)

PARIHĀRA (CANCELLATION) OF THE MALEFIC YOGAS WHEN AN AUSPICIOUS ACT IS UNAVOIDABLE

(18) Nārada [says]: those tithis that are month-void, and likewise those lagnas that are declared void — they are to be shunned in Madhyadeśa [alone]; among other [peoples/regions] they do not vitiate.
(19) The lame (paṅgu), blind (andha) and one-eyed (kāṇa) lagnas, and the month-void rāśis (signs), are to be avoided in Gauḍa and Mālava; in another country they are not censured.

[ṭīkā] Regarding the month-void tithis and the rest that have been stated, Nārada states a qualification: the month-void tithi and the void lagnas that have been described are to be shunned in Madhyadeśa only — in other countries they carry no doṣa (affliction). Likewise the paṅgu, andha and kāṇa lagnas (which are described in the marriage chapter) and the month-void rāśi are to be rejected in the Gauḍa country ([Mārava?][?]) and [a second region — the OCR here reads as either Mālava or, alternatively, Malabar (Kerala); the mūla verse (19, translated above) is unambiguous for Gauḍa and Mālava, so that pairing is retained as the primary reading, but the ṭīkā's own restatement at this exact point is genuinely uncertain and may have specified a different or additional region][?]; in other countries they are not blameworthy. (18–19) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE CENSURABILITY OF THE HASTĀRKA AND SIMILAR YOGAS EVEN THOUGH THEY BESTOW SUCCESS IN AUSPICIOUS WORKS

(20ab) In all undertakings one should reject the Hasta–Arka [combination — Hasta nakṣatra on a Sunday] when it falls on the fifth tithi.

Prakaraṇa 1 — with the Hindī ṭīkā (commentary) · page (9)

[ṭīkā, on verse 20] The Amṛtasiddhi yogas that arise from the vāra (weekday) and nakṣatra (lunar mansion) combination become inauspicious through their conjunction with certain tithis (lunar days). Thus Hasta on a Sunday is a siddhi (success-yielding) combination, but if it falls on the fifth tithi it is contrary. So likewise Aśvinī on a Tuesday when it falls on the seventh, and Mṛgaśira on a Monday when it falls on the sixth. (20) (Anuṣṭubh)

(21) [One should avoid] the Budha–Anurādhā [combination] on the eighth tithi; the Bhṛgu–Revatī [Friday–Revatī] on the tenth; the Guru–Puṣya [Thursday–Puṣya] on the ninth; and the Śani–Rohiṇī [Saturday–Rohiṇī] on the eleventh.

[ṭīkā] Anurādhā on a Wednesday when it falls on the eighth, Revatī on a Friday on the tenth, Puṣya on a Thursday on the ninth, and Rohiṇī on a Saturday on the eleventh become contrary; should such combinations occur, they are to be rejected in every auspicious undertaking. (21) (Anuṣṭubh)

(22) In house-entry (gṛhapraveśa), in journey (yātrā) and in marriage respectively, one should reject the Bhauma–Aśvinī, the Śani–Brāhma (Saturday–Rohiṇī), and the Guru–Puṣya.

[ṭīkā] Although the said Bhauma–Aśvinī and the other Amṛtasiddhi yogas are declared [auspicious] for all undertakings, still Bhauma–Aśvinī must be rejected for house-entry, Śani–Rohiṇī for a journey, and Guru–Puṣya for a marriage. (22) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE TWENTY-EIGHT YOGAS BEGINNING WITH ĀNANDA

(23) Ānanda by name, then Kāladaṇḍa, Dhūmra, Dhātṛ (Prajāpati), Saumya, Dhvāṅkṣa, Ketu (Dhvaja) in order; Śrīvatsa by name, Vajra, Mudgara, Chatra, Mitra, Mānasa, Padma and Lamba.
(24) Utpāta and Mṛtyu indeed, Kāṇa and Siddhi, Śubha, that named Amṛta, Musala and Gada, and those named Mātaṅga, Rakṣas, Cara, Susthira and Pravardhamāna — they yield fruit according to their own names.

[ṭīkā] The names of the Ānandādi yogas: Ānanda 1, Kāladaṇḍa 2, Dhūmra 3, Prajāpati 4, Saumya 5, Dhvāṅkṣa 6, Dhvaja 7, Śrīvatsa 8, Vajra 9, Mudgara 10, Chatra 11, Mitra 12, Mānasa 13, Padma 14, Lambaka 15, Utpāta 16, Mṛtyu 17, Kāṇa 18, Siddhi 19, Śubha 20, Amṛta 21, Musala 22, Gada 23, Mātaṅga 24, Rākṣasa 25, Cara 26, Sthira 27, Vardhamāna 28. These yogas arise according to the nakṣatra and the vāra, and they give fruits corresponding to their names. (23–24) (Śālinī for 23; Upajāti for 24)

आवश्यकतामें दुष्टयोगोंकी वर्ज्यघटीसंख्या कहते हैं कि—ध्वांक्ष, वज्र, मुद्गरको ५ घटी; पद्म, लम्बककी ४ घटी; गदकी ७; धूम्रकी १; काणकी २; मुसलकी २; और राक्षस, मृत्यु, उत्पात, कालदण्डकी समस्त ६० घटी वर्जित हैं। अन्य ग्रन्थोंमें चरयोगकी तीन घटी वर्जित करनी लिखी है ॥ २६ ॥ (शालिनी)

दोषापवादभूता रवियोगाः

सूर्यभाद्वेदगोतक[?]दिग्विश्वनखसम्मिते ।
चन्द्रे रवियोगाः स्युर्दोषसर्वविनाशकाः ॥ २७ ॥

जिस नक्षत्र पर सूर्य हो उससे गिनकर (दिननक्षत्र) जिसपर चन्द्रमा है उस पर्यन्त ४। ९। ६। १०। १३। २० इसमें कोई संख्या हो तो रवियोग होता है; यह सभी कार्यमें शुभ होता है, पूर्वोक्त दोषोंके समूहका नाश करता है ॥ २७ ॥

सिद्धियोगाः

अर्के[?]मूलोत्तरपुष्यदस्रं चन्द्रे श्रुतिब्राह्मशशीज्यमैत्रम् ।
भौमेऽश्व्य[?]बुध्न्यकृशानुसार्पं सौम्ये[?]मैत्रार्ककृशानुसार्पम्[?] ॥ २८ ॥
जीवेऽन्त्यमैत्राश्व्यदितीज्यधिष्ण्यं शुक्रेऽन्त्यमेवाश्व्यदितिश्रवोभम् ।
शनौ श्रुतिब्राह्मसमीरभानि सर्वार्थसिद्धये कथितानि पूर्वैः ॥ २९ ॥

सिद्धियोग कहते हैं कि—रविवारको हस्त, मूल, तीनों उत्तरा, पुष्य, अश्विनी। सोमवा-

Prakaraṇa 1 — with the Hindī ṭīkā (commentary) · page (11)

[ṭīkā, completing verse 25] [On Sunday count from Aśvinī, on Monday] from Mṛgaśira, on Tuesday from Āśleṣā, on Wednesday from Hasta, on Thursday from Anurādhā, on Friday from Uttarāṣāḍhā, on Saturday from Śatabhiṣā. Whatever ordinal number the current day's nakṣatra (lunar mansion) reaches in that count, the yoga of that same number among the aforesaid [28] is to be known. Thus on a Sunday, Aśvinī is Ānanda and Bharaṇī is Kāladaṇḍa; and on a Monday, counting from Mṛgaśira, Hasta comes to 9, so the ninth yoga, Vajra, obtains. The rest are to be known in the same way. Here Abhijit too must be counted, and then the yogas will number 28. (25) (Anuṣṭubh)

PARIHĀRA (CANCELLATION) OF THE MALEFIC YOGAS AMONG THE ĀNANDĀDI WHEN AN ACT IS UNAVOIDABLE

(26) In [Dhvāṅkṣa?], Vajra and Mudgara five nāḍīs (ghaṭīs) are to be shunned; in Padma and Lamba, four; in Gada, seven; in Dhūmra, Kāṇa and Mausala, one and two [respectively]; and in Rākṣasa, Mṛtyu, Utpāta and Kāla[daṇḍa], the whole [duration].

[ṭīkā] The number of ghaṭīs to be shunned in the malefic yogas, when [an act] is unavoidable, is stated: for Dhvāṅkṣa, Vajra and Mudgara, 5 ghaṭīs; for Padma and Lambaka, 4 ghaṭīs; for Gada, 7; for Dhūmra, 1; for Kāṇa, 2; for Musala, 2; and for Rākṣasa, Mṛtyu, Utpāta and Kāladaṇḍa the entire 60 ghaṭīs are to be shunned. In other works it is written that three ghaṭīs of the Cara yoga are to be shunned. (26) (Śālinī)

THE RAVI-YOGAS, WHICH CONSTITUTE THE EXCEPTION TO [ALL] DOṢAS

(27) When, counted from the Sun's nakṣatra, the Moon['s nakṣatra] falls at [a distance] measured by 4, [9], [6], 10 (dik), 13 (viśva) or 20 (nakha), the Ravi-yogas arise, and they destroy all doṣas (afflictions).

[ṭīkā] Counting from the nakṣatra occupied by the Sun up to that occupied by the Moon (the day's nakṣatra), if the count is any of 4, 9, 6, 10, 13, 20, a Ravi-yoga occurs. It is auspicious for every undertaking, and it destroys the whole mass of the doṣas stated above. (27)

THE SIDDHI-YOGAS

(28) On Sunday (Arka): [Hasta?], Mūla, the Uttarās, Puṣya and Dasra (Aśvinī); on Monday (Candra): Śruti (Śravaṇa), Brāhma (Rohiṇī), Śaśin (Mṛgaśira), Ijya (Puṣya) and Maitra (Anurādhā); on Tuesday (Bhauma): Aśvi (Aśvinī), [Ahir]budhnya (Uttarabhādrapadā), Kṛśānu (Kṛttikā) and Sārpa (Āśleṣā); on Wednesday (Saumya): Maitra (Anurādhā), Arka (Hasta), Kṛśānu (Kṛttikā) and Sārpa (Āśleṣā).
(29) On Thursday (Jīva): Antya (Revatī), Maitra (Anurādhā), Aśvi (Aśvinī), Aditi (Punarvasu) and Ijya (Puṣya); on Friday (Śukra): Antya (Revatī) itself, [Bhaga = Pūrvaphālgunī], Aśvi (Aśvinī), Aditi (Punarvasu) and Śravaṇa; on Saturday (Śani): Śruti (Śravaṇa), Brāhma (Rohiṇī) and Samīra (Svātī). These have been declared by the ancients to yield success in every object (sarvārtha-siddhi).

[ṭīkā] The Siddhi-yogas are stated: on Sunday, Hasta, Mūla, the three Uttarās, Puṣya, Aśvinī; on Mon— [continues in the next chunk]

THE UTPĀTA, MṚTYU, KĀṆA AND SIDDHI YOGAS

(30) From Dvīśa (Viśākhā), from Toya (Pūrvāṣāḍhā), from Vāsava (Dhaniṣṭhā), from the Pauṣṇa star (Revatī), from Brāhmī (Rohiṇī), from Puṣya and from Aryaman (Uttaraphālgunī) — by [each successive set of] four stars[?] — on the days beginning with Sunday[?] there arise Utpāta, Mṛtyu, Kāṇa and Siddhi; their fruit is the same as their name.

[ṭīkā] On Sunday, the four nakṣatras (lunar mansions) reckoned from Viśākhā are in order the Utpāta, Mṛtyu, Kāṇa and Siddhi yogas. Thus on a Sunday, Viśākhā is Utpāta, Anurādhā is Mṛtyu, Jyeṣṭhā is Kāṇa and Mūla is Siddhi. In the same way the said four yogas arise on Monday from Pūrvāṣāḍhā, on Tuesday from Dhaniṣṭhā, on Wednesday from Revatī, on Thursday from Rohiṇī, on Friday from Puṣya, and on Saturday from Uttaraphālgunī. Their fruits too are just as their names are. (30) (Śālinī)

[The printed table of the Cara, Dagdha, Mṛtyu, Siddhi, Utpāta and Amṛtasiddhi yogas is fragmented and illegible in the scan — not rendered.]

PARIHĀRA (CANCELLATION) OF THE MALEFIC YOGAS BY DIFFERENCE OF REGION

(31) The evil yogas (kuyogas) born of tithi-and-vāra, those born of tithi-and-nakṣatra, and those born of nakṣatra-and-vāra — and likewise those born of all three — are to be shunned only in Hūṇa[?] [and the regions named]…

[ṭīkā] The parihāra (cancellation) of the malefic yogas is stated: those such as Krakaca (vāra-dagdha) which arise from tithi (lunar day) together with vāra (weekday); and those which arise from tithi together with nakṣatra, as in "Anurādhā on the second" and so forth; and those which arise from nakṣatra together with vāra, as in "Yāmya (Bharaṇī), Tvāṣṭra (Citrā), Vaiśvadeva (Uttarāṣāḍhā), Dhaniṣṭhā, Aryaman (Uttaraphālgunī), Jyeṣṭhā and Antya (Revatī) are the Sun's burnt star" — [continues in the next chunk]

(2) Verse 30 pāda 4 read as 'वारेऽर्कादौ' on the strength of the ṭīkā's weekday sequence, flagged. (3) The six-row yoga table is broken into isolated glyphs and cannot be reconstructed. (4) Verse 31 pāda 3, the list of regions where these kuyogas apply is corrupt; the ṭīkā on page 25 glosses them as Hūṇa (Baṅga), Bengal and Uttarakhaṇḍa (Khāndeś), but the verse's own place-names cannot be restored with confidence. Note: verse 31 is the load-bearing classification of combination-kuyogas into tithi×vāra, tithi×nakṣatra, nakṣatra×vāra and all-three-together classes, and that classification is fully legible.

समस्त शुभकृत्योंमें वर्जित पदार्थ कहते हैं कि, चन्द्रमा तथा (पापग्रह) सूर्य, मंगल, शनि, राहु, केतुसे युक्त लग्न एवं नवांश भी सभी कार्योंमें त्याज्य हैं; तथा मध्याह्न एवम् अर्धरात्रिके मध्य १ घटी अभिजित् मुहूर्त उत्तम होता है, परन्तु इसके ठीक मध्यके (घटीत्र्यंश) २० पल (१० पूर्वके, १० परभागके) भी त्याज्य हैं। ऐसे ही सूर्य-चन्द्रग्रहणसे पूर्व तीन [दिन]; और (उत्पात) प्रकृतिसे विरुद्ध होनेको उत्पात कहते हैं। सो तीन प्रकारके हैं—(१) दिव्य—केतुदर्शन, ग्रहनक्षत्रवैकृत, उल्का, निर्घात, परिवेषादि; (२) अन्तरिक्ष—गन्धर्वनगर, इन्द्रधनुषादि; (३) भौम—पृथ्वीसम्बन्धी भूमिकम्प, वृक्षवैकृत, पशुवैकृत, अग्निजलवैकृतादि हैं। जिस दिन ऐसा कोई उत्पात हो उससे तथा ग्रहणदिनसे ७ दिन पर्यन्त शुभ कृत्य न करना; ऐसे ही केतु (पुच्छतारा) के दर्शनमें भी जानना। और मतांतरसे ग्रहणका नियम—सर्वग्रासमें ७ दिन, त्रिभागमें ६ दिन, अर्धग्रासमें ४ दिन, चौथाई ग्रासमें तीन दिन, और १।२।३ अंगुल ग्रासमें एक दिन मात्र वर्ज्य है। (शुभदोत्पातमें) १ दिन वर्ज्य। शुभदोत्पात—बिजली गिरना, भूकम्प, सन्ध्यासमय, निर्घातशब्द, परिवेष, रजविना अग्निधूम, सूर्यबिम्ब रक्त उदयास्तमें,

Prakaraṇa 1 — with the Hindī ṭīkā (commentary) · page (13)

[ṭīkā, completing verse 31] …and so forth; and those born of all three together — tithi (lunar day), vāra (weekday) and nakṣatra (lunar mansion) — as in "In all undertakings one should reject Hasta–Arka on the fifth tithi," and the like. All these doṣas (afflictions) are to be shunned in the Hūṇa country (Baṅga), in Bengal, and in Uttarakhaṇḍa (Khāndeś); in other countries they are not prohibited. (31) (Anuṣṭubh)

THINGS TO BE REJECTED IN EVERY AUSPICIOUS UNDERTAKING

(32) In every [undertaking] the lagna (ascendant) joined with the Moon and malefics is to be rejected[?], and the bad navāṃśa; [likewise] the middle third [of the abhijit ghaṭī] at midnight and midday…[?]; the three days preceding an eclipse; from an utpāta (portent) [seven] days[?]; a day vitiated by an auspicious-yielding portent[?] — one day; and for six months one should reject a star struck by a planet[?], [a star of a] planetary war[?], and the star of a portent.

[ṭīkā] The things to be rejected in every auspicious undertaking are stated: a lagna, and likewise a navāṃśa, occupied by the Moon together with the malefics (pāpa-grahas) — the Sun, Mars, Saturn, Rāhu and Ketu — are to be avoided in all works. And the one ghaṭī of the abhijit muhūrta at the middle of the day and at midnight is excellent, yet the 20 palas at its exact centre (a third of a ghaṭī — 10 before and 10 after) are also to be avoided. Likewise the three days before a solar or lunar eclipse.
And an utpāta (portent) is what is contrary to nature. It is of three kinds: (1) divine — the sighting of a comet, aberration of planets and stars, meteors, thunderclaps without cloud, haloes and the like; (2) atmospheric — gandharva-cities [mirages], rainbows and the like; (3) terrestrial — earthquakes, abnormalities in trees, in animals, in fire and water, and so on. On the day on which any such portent occurs, and from the day of an eclipse, auspicious acts are not to be performed for seven days; the same is to be understood for the sighting of a comet (a tailed star).
By another opinion the rule for eclipses is: for a total eclipse, 7 days; for a two-thirds eclipse, 6 days; for a half eclipse, 4 days; for a quarter eclipse, 3 days; and for an eclipse of 1, 2 or 3 aṅgulas, one day only is to be shunned. For an auspicious-yielding portent, one day is to be shunned.
Auspicious-yielding portents are: a lightning-strike; an earthquake; [an abnormality at] the twilight hour; a thunderclap; a halo; smoke from fire without dust; the Sun's disc red at rising and setting; [continues in the next chunk]

[ṭīkā, completing verse 32] …where a portent has occurred — all these are to be shunned for six months. (32)

PROHIBITION OF THE ECLIPSED NAKṢATRA ACCORDING TO THE DEGREE OF OBSCURATION

(33) One should reject the [eclipsed] star[?] for six, three and one month respectively (tarka, guṇa, indu) according as the obscuration is total, half or a quarter. [The three days] before[?] … when [the luminary] sets eclipsed, or rises eclipsed, or is half-obscured…

[ṭīkā] The degree to which the [eclipsed] nakṣatra (lunar mansion) is to be shunned, according to the extent of obscuration, is stated: if the eclipse is total, the eclipse-nakṣatra is to be rejected for six months; for a half obscuration, three months; for a quarter obscuration, one month. And if the luminary sets while eclipsed (grastāsta), the three preceding days are to be shunned and the following days are auspicious; if it rises eclipsed (grastodaya), the three following days are inauspicious and the preceding are auspicious. If the obscuration is half, then three days on each side. In a total eclipse, seven days [on each side]. (33) (Indravajrā)

THE VITIATIONS OF THE PAÑCĀṄGA AND THE REST, WHICH MUST GENERALLY BE SHUNNED

(34) The birth-nakṣatra, birth-month and birth-tithi; Vyatīpāta, Bhadrā, Vaidhṛti, the new-moon (pitṛ-day); the decayed and increased tithi[?]; the deficient and intercalary month; Kulika; the half-prahara; Pāta; and the first three ghaṭikās of the Viṣkambha and Vajra [yogas] — precisely these are to be rejected.

[ṭīkā] In auspicious undertakings the nakṣatra, month, tithi and the rest of one's birth are to be shunned. The measure of the month is stated by the lunar month, up to 30 days from the birth-tithi. Among the yogas beginning with Viṣkambha, Vyatīpāta and Vaidhṛti are shunned in every act; likewise Bhadrā, the new moon (pitṛ-day), and the śrāddha-day of one's mother and father; the kṣaya-tithi (the decayed tithi, in which three tithis are touched within one day); the vṛddhi-tithi (in which one tithi touches three weekdays); the kṣaya-māsa (the month in which two solar ingresses fall between two new moons); the adhika-māsa (in which no solar ingress falls between two [new moons]); and the Kulika yoga and the half-prahara (these will be stated further on); and Mahāpāta and Mahāvaidhṛti (these yogas are known by calculation); and however many ghaṭikās at the beginning of the Viṣkambha and Vajra yogas are to be shunned. Among the said doṣas (afflictions) the tithi stands by implication for the nakṣatras and yogas as well.
The parihāra (cancellation) for the decayed and increased [tithis] is given in another work: if Jupiter be in a kendra (angle), then [the doṣa of] the kṣaya [tithi and] the new moon— [continues in the next chunk]

चतुर्थी, षष्ठी, अष्टमी, [नवमी,] द्वादशी, चतुर्दशी—ये पक्षरन्ध्रतिथि हैं। आवश्यकतामें इनके ८। ९। १४। २५। १०। ५ इतनी घटिका आदिकी वर्जित हैं। जैसे चतुर्थीकी ८, षष्ठीकी ९, अष्टमीकी १४, नवमीकी २५, द्वादशीकी १०, चतुर्दशीकी ५ घटी वर्जित करके शेष शुभकृत्यमें ग्राह्य हैं ॥ ३६ ॥ (अनुष्टुप्)

कुलिकादिदोषाः

कुलिकः कालवेला च यमघण्टश्च कण्टकः ।

वर्तमान वारसे गिनकर, जितनी संख्यामें शनि हो उसे दूना कर जो अङ्क हो, उस दिन उतना मुहूर्त कुलिक होता है; तथा वर्तमान वारसे जितनेमें बुध हो उसे दूना कर जो अङ्क हो, उतनी संख्याका मुहूर्त कालवेला होता है। ऐसे ही वर्तमान वारसे बृहस्पति जितनी संख्यामें हो उसे दूना कर यमघण्ट मुहूर्त होता है; तथा वर्तमान वारसे मङ्गल जिस संख्यामें हो उसे दूना कर वह कण्टक मुहूर्त होता है।
उदाहरण जैसे—रविवारके दिन रविसे शनि सातवां है, इसे दूना कर १४ हुआ, तो रविवारके दिन चौदहवां मुहूर्त कुलिक हुआ; तथा रविसे बुध चौथा है, द्विगुण ८ हुआ, इस दिन आठवां मुहूर्त कालवेला है; तथा इससे बृहस्पति पांचवां, २ गुण १०, इस दिन दशवां मुहूर्त यमघण्ट है; ऐसे ही रविसे मंगल तीसरा, २ गुण ६, रविवारको छठा मुहूर्त कण्टक है। इसी प्रकार सभी वारोंके मुहूर्त जानने।
ये मुहूर्त ४।४[?] घटीके होते हैं, शुभकृत्योंमें वर्जित हैं; किन्तु किसी आचार्यका मत ऐसा भी है कि इन मुहूर्तोंका उत्तरार्ध निषिद्ध है, पूर्वार्ध दूषित नहीं, और रात्रिमें इनका दोष नहीं। अर्धयाम सर्वदा त्याज्य है, इसको आगे कहेंगे ॥ ३७ ॥

Prakaraṇa 1 — with the Hindī ṭīkā (commentary) · page (15)

(36) On the pakṣa-randhra tithis (lunar days) — 4 (veda), 6 (aṅga), 8 (aṣṭa), 9 (nava), 12 (arka) and 14 (indra) — one should reject [respectively] 8 (vasu), 9 (aṅka), 14 (manu), 25 (tattva), 10 (āśā) and 5 (śara) [ghaṭikās]; the nāḍīs beyond these are auspicious.

[ṭīkā] The fourth, sixth, eighth, [ninth,] twelfth and fourteenth are the pakṣa-randhra tithis. When [an act] is unavoidable, the first 8, 9, 14, 25, 10 and 5 ghaṭikās of these are shunned: that is, 8 ghaṭīs of the fourth, 9 of the sixth, 14 of the eighth, 25 of the ninth, 10 of the twelfth and 5 of the fourteenth being rejected, the remainder is acceptable for auspicious undertakings. (36) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE KULIKA AND THE OTHER DOṢAS

(37) Kulika, Kālavelā, Yamaghaṇṭa and Kaṇṭaka: [their] muhūrta [is found] from Saturn, Mercury, Jupiter and Mars respectively, [counted] from the current vāra (weekday).

[ṭīkā] Counting from the current weekday, take the ordinal position of Saturn and double it; the resulting number gives the muhūrta of that day which is Kulika. Likewise, take the ordinal position of Mercury from the current weekday and double it; the muhūrta of that number is Kālavelā. In the same way, double the ordinal position of Jupiter from the current weekday and that muhūrta is Yamaghaṇṭa; and double the ordinal position of Mars from the current weekday and that is the Kaṇṭaka muhūrta.
For example: on a Sunday, Saturn is seventh from the Sun; doubled this gives 14, so on Sunday the fourteenth muhūrta is Kulika. Mercury is fourth from the Sun; doubled, 8 — so on that day the eighth muhūrta is Kālavelā. Jupiter is fifth from it; doubled, 10 — so that day the tenth muhūrta is Yamaghaṇṭa. Likewise Mars is third from the Sun; doubled, 6 — so on Sunday the sixth muhūrta is Kaṇṭaka. In this manner the muhūrtas of all the weekdays are to be known.
These muhūrtas are of four ghaṭīs each[?], and are shunned in auspicious undertakings. But there is also the opinion of some ācāryas that only the latter half of these muhūrtas is prohibited, the former half is not vitiated, and that at night they carry no doṣa (affliction). The half-yāma is always to be rejected; this will be stated further on. (37)
ocr_review_note: One flagged reading: the ṭīkā's 'ये मुहूर्त ४।४ घटीके होते हैं' (these muhūrtas are of 4 ghaṭīs each) is inconsistent with the same ṭīkā's own worked example, which reaches a fourteenth muhūrta in a day, and with page 28's statement that a muhūrta is 2 ghaṭīs (a sixteenth of the day); the digit may be an OCR corruption of '२।२', so the figure is flagged rather than normalised. Note that the ṭīkā of verse 36 and the closing sentence of verse 37's ṭīkā are both parihāra rules.

[विपाशेरावतीतीरे शतद्रुतीरे?] त्रिपुष्करे ।

विपाशा (व्यासा) एवम् इरावती नदी (पंजाब देशमें हैं) के तीर, तथा शतद्रु (सतलज) के तीर, और त्रिपुष्कर देशमें (होलाष्टक) फाल्गुन शुद्ध अष्टमीसे फाल्गुन “हुताशनी” पूर्णिमा पर्यन्त विवाहादि शुभ कार्य शुभ नहीं; अन्य देशोंमें इनका दोष नहीं ॥ ४० ॥

(16) Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi [Śubhāśubha-prakaraṇa]

THE INAUSPICIOUS MUHŪRTAS ON THE WEEKDAYS BEGINNING WITH SUNDAY

(38–39) [The verses give the durmuhūrta serial numbers for each vāra (weekday) in bhūta-saṃkhyā numeral-words; the printed text is substantially corrupt in the scan and is not rendered word-for-word. Its content is given by the ṭīkā below.]

[ṭīkā] For ease in knowing the doṣas (afflictions), the durmuhūrtas and the rest are stated: on Sunday, muhūrtas 6, 7, 8, 10, 14; on Monday, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 13, 14; on Tuesday, 2, 4, 3, 6, 10, 10[?]; on Wednesday, 2, 4, 8, 9, 10, 14; on Thursday, 2, 6, 12, 15, 14, 16[?]; on Friday, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 12, 14; on Saturday, 1, 2, 8, 10, 11, 12. These muhūrtas are censured — that is, they bear as the case may be the names Duṣṭakṣaṇa, Kulika, Kaṇṭaka, Kālavelā, Ardhayāma and Yamaghaṇṭa.
For example, on Sunday the 10th muhūrta is the durmuhūrta and also the Kulika; the 6th is Kaṇṭaka; the 7th [and] the 8th are Ardhayāma, and the 8th is also Kālavelā; and the 10th bears the name Yamaghaṇṭa. In the same way, for Monday and the rest, the said names are to be known at the said numbers.
A muhūrta is of 2 ghaṭīs; but since the length of the day varies, a sixteenth part of the day has been taken here. Whatever the length of a given day, divide it by 16, and the quotient is to be known as one muhūrta. (38–39)

PROHIBITION OF THE HOLIKĀ-AṢṬAKA FOR MARRIAGE AND OTHER AUSPICIOUS ACTS

(40) [On the banks of the Vipāśā and the Irāvatī, on the bank of the Śatadru?] and in Tripuṣkara, the eight days preceding the Holikā [festival] are never [fit] for marriage and other auspicious [acts].

[ṭīkā] On the banks of the Vipāśā (Vyāsā) and the Irāvatī rivers (which are in the Punjab country), and on the bank of the Śatadru (Sutlej), and in the Tripuṣkara country, the Holāṣṭaka — from the bright eighth of Phālguna up to the Phālguna "Hutāśanī" full moon — is not auspicious for marriage and other auspicious undertakings. In other countries these carry no doṣa. (40)

THE EXCEPTION (APAVĀDA) TO THE MṚTYU, KRAKACA AND SIMILAR [YOGAS]

आनन्दादि योगोंमें मृत्युयोग, क्रकच, वारदग्ध (दग्धयोग) “सूर्येशपञ्चाग्नी” इत्यादि, और विषयोग, हुताशन योगादि पूर्वोक्त दुष्टयोग, चन्द्रमाके गोचर-प्रकरणोक्त प्रकारसे शुभ होनेमें शुभ अर्थात् उक्त दुष्टफल छोड़कर शुभ फल देनेवाले होते हैं। किसी आचार्यका मत ऐसा भी है कि उक्त दुष्टयोगोंका एक प्रहरसे उपरान्त दोष नहीं है। और किसी किसीका मत है कि उक्त योग यात्राहीमें वर्जित हैं, और कार्योंमें नहीं ॥ ४१ ॥ (अनु०)

अयोगे सुयोगोऽपि चेत्स्यात्तदानीमयोगं निहत्येष सिद्धिं तनोति ।

भद्रानिषेधः

[?— यहां श्लोक ४३ के प्रथम पादका एक विच्छिन्न पुनरावृत्त खण्ड मुद्रित है: “न पूर्वार्ध...योर्भद्रैकाद्...”; स्कैन-दोष]

पूर्वार्धेऽष्टमीपञ्चदश्योर्भद्रैकादश्यां चतुर्थ्यां परा ।
कृष्णेऽन्त्यार्धे स्यात्तृतीयादशम्योः पूर्वभागे सप्तमीशम्भुतिथ्योः ॥ ४३ ॥

शुक्लपक्षकी अष्टमी, पूर्णिमाके पूर्वार्धमें, एवं एकादशी, चतुर्थीके उत्तरार्धमें भद्रा होती है; कृष्णपक्षकी तृतीया, दशमीके उत्तरार्धमें, तथा सप्तमी, चतुर्दशीके पूर्वभाग (पूर्वार्ध) में भद्रा होती है। यह भद्रा विष्टि करण है। करण गिननेकी रीतिसे उक्त तिथियोंके उक्त दलोंमें यह करण आता है। यह बड़ा दोष समस्त शुभकृत्योंमें वर्ज्य है ॥ ४३ ॥ (शालिनी)

Prakaraṇa 1 — with the Hindī ṭīkā (commentary) · page (17)

[ṭīkā, on verse 41] Among the Ānandādi yogas, the Mṛtyu yoga, Krakaca, Vāradagdha (the Dagdha yoga — "Sūrya, Īśa, Pañcāgni," etc.), and the Viṣa yoga, the Hutāśana yoga and the rest of the malefic yogas stated above, become auspicious when [the Moon] is auspicious in the manner set out in the chapter on the Moon's gochara (transit) — that is, they abandon the said evil fruit and yield an auspicious one. There is also the opinion of certain ācāryas that the said malefic yogas carry no doṣa (affliction) after the first prahara. And some hold that the said yogas are shunned in yātrā (a journey) only, and not in [other] undertakings. (41) (Anuṣṭubh)

(42) If a good yoga occurs together with a bad one, it slays the bad yoga then and there and bestows success. Others [say] that by purity of the lagna (ascendant) there is destruction of the evil yogas and the rest; and [that] the Viṣṭi (Bhadrā) and the others are commendable after midday.

[ṭīkā] On a day on which some malefic yoga such as Mṛtyu or Krakaca occurs, and the Siddhi (Amṛtasiddhi) yoga also occurs, [the latter] destroys the fruit of the malefic yoga and grants accomplishment of the undertaking. Other ācāryas hold that when the lagna is sound and strong (lagna-śuddhi), the Mṛtyu, Krakaca, Dagdha and similar yogas are destroyed; and that the doṣa of Bhadrā, Vyatīpāta and the like lasts only until midday and not after midday. The same holds for Tuesday, the pratyari [star] and the birth-nakṣatra as well. (42) (Bhujaṅgaprayāta)

PROHIBITION OF BHADRĀ

(43) In the bright fortnight Bhadrā falls in the first half of the eighth and of the fifteenth, and in the latter half of the eleventh and the fourth; in the dark fortnight it falls in the last half of the third and the tenth, and in the first part of the seventh and the fourteenth (Śambhu's tithi).

[ṭīkā] Bhadrā occurs in the first half of the bright eighth and full moon, and in the latter half of the bright eleventh and fourth; and in the latter half of the dark third and tenth, and in the first part (first half) of the dark seventh and fourteenth. This Bhadrā is the Viṣṭi karaṇa. By the method of reckoning the karaṇas, this karaṇa falls in the said halves of the said tithis (lunar days). It is a great doṣa and is to be shunned in all auspicious undertakings. (43) (Śālinī)

अष्टमीके दूसरे प्रहरकी ५ घटी, एकादशीके सातवें प्रहरकी, पूर्णिमाके चौथे, तृतीयाके आठवें, सप्तमीके तीसरे, चतुर्दशीके पहले प्रहरकी पांच घटी भद्राका मुख होता है। यह अति दोषद है।
चतुर्थीके चौथे, अष्टमीके प्रथम, एकादशीके छठे, पूर्णिमाके तीसरे, तृतीयाके सातवें, सप्तमीके दूसरे, दशमीके पांचवें, चतुर्दशीके चौथे प्रहरकी अंतिम (पिछली) तीन (३) घटी पुच्छसंज्ञक होती हैं। यह पुच्छभद्रा दुष्ट नहीं होती अर्थात् शुभकार्यमें ग्राह्य है। यहां प्रहरगणना तिथिके आरम्भसे है; तिथिका सर्व भोग्यके आठ भाग ८ प्रहर मानने चाहिये।
भद्राके अंगविभाग ग्रन्थान्तरोंमें ऐसे हैं—मुखमें ५, ग्रीवामें[?] १, हृदयमें ११, नाभिमें ४, कटिमें ६, पुच्छमें ३ घटी हैं; इनमेंसे पुच्छकी २[?] घटी शुभ हैं।
श्रीपत्याचार्य कहते हैं कि, एक समय दैत्योंने देवताओंको जीत लिया, तब महादेवजीने क्रोधसे भालनेत्र खोला; खोलते ही क्रोधाग्निका एक कण निकला, यह खरमुखी, तीन पैरकी, लांगूल चढ़े, सात हाथवाली, सिंहसमान गला, कृशोदरी, प्रेतवाहिनी मूर्ति उत्पन्न होकर दैत्योंका संहार करती हुई। तब देवताओंने स्तुति करके इसका नाम भद्रा रक्खा और बवादि करणोंमें स्नान एवं भाग दिया।
आवश्यक कृत्यमें भद्राका परिहार कहते हैं कि, तिथि उत्तरार्धकी भद्रा दिनमें तथा तिथि पूर्वार्धकी रात्रिमें शुभ होती है; और आचार्यान्तरमत ऐसा भी है कि भद्रा, मङ्गलवार, व्यतीपात, वैधृति, मृत्युयोग—ये मध्याह्नसे ऊपर दोष नहीं देते ॥ ४४ ॥ (शा० वि०)

भद्रानिवासस्तत्फलञ्च

कुम्भकर्कद्वये मर्त्यं स्वर्गेऽब्जे[?]ऽजाश्रयेऽलिगि ।
स्त्रीधनूजक[?]नक्रेऽधो भद्रा तत्रैव तत्फलम् ॥ ४५ ॥

भद्रावास कहते हैं कि—कुम्भ, मीन, कर्क, सिंहके चन्द्रमामें भद्रा हो तो मृत्युलोकमें तथा
content_en:
(18) Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi [Śubhāśubha-prakaraṇa]

[ṭīkā, continued] …the 5 ghaṭīs of the second prahara of the eighth; of the seventh prahara of the eleventh; of the fourth [prahara] of the full moon; of the eighth of the third; of the third of the seventh; and of the first prahara of the fourteenth — these five ghaṭīs constitute the mouth of Bhadrā. This is exceedingly productive of doṣa (affliction).
The last (final) three (3) ghaṭīs of the fourth prahara of the fourth tithi, of the first of the eighth, of the sixth of the eleventh, of the third of the full moon, of the seventh of the third, of the second of the seventh, of the fifth of the tenth, and of the fourth of the fourteenth, are termed the tail (puccha). This puccha-Bhadrā is not malefic — that is, it is acceptable for auspicious work. Here the praharas are counted from the beginning of the tithi (lunar day); the whole span of a tithi is to be taken as eight parts, i.e. 8 praharas.
The division of Bhadrā's limbs, as given in other works, is thus: in the mouth 5, in the neck[?] 1, in the heart 11, in the navel 4, in the waist 6, and in the tail 3 ghaṭīs; of these, 2[?] ghaṭīs of the tail are auspicious.
Ācārya Śrīpati relates that once the daityas conquered the gods, whereupon Mahādeva in wrath opened his brow-eye; the moment he opened it, a single spark of the fire of his wrath came forth, and there arose a form ass-faced, three-footed, with tail erect, seven-armed, lion-throated, lean-bellied, riding a corpse, which went on destroying the daityas. Then the gods propitiated her with praise, named her Bhadrā, and assigned her a bath and a share among the karaṇas beginning with Bava.
The parihāra (cancellation) of Bhadrā when an act is unavoidable is stated: a Bhadrā belonging to the latter half of a tithi is auspicious by day, and one belonging to the former half of a tithi is auspicious by night. And there is also the opinion of other ācāryas that Bhadrā, Tuesday, Vyatīpāta, Vaidhṛti and the Mṛtyu yoga give no doṣa after midday. (44)

THE ABODE OF BHADRĀ AND ITS FRUIT

(45) When [the Moon is] in the two pairs beginning with Kumbha and Karka, [Bhadrā dwells] in the world of mortals; in Meṣa's group[?] and in Ali (Vṛścika), in heaven; in Strī (Kanyā), Dhanus, [Tulā?] and Nakra (Makara), below. Bhadrā's fruit is felt in that very [world in which she dwells].

[ṭīkā] The abode of Bhadrā is stated: if Bhadrā occurs while the Moon is in Kumbha, Mīna, Karka or Siṃha, then in the world of mortals, and [continues in the next chunk]
ocr_review_note: Three flagged points. (1) ṭīkā limb-division list: read as 'ग्रीवामें १' (neck) on contextual grounds only. (2) 'इनमेंसे पुच्छकी २ घटी शुभ हैं' conflicts with the preceding 'पुच्छमें ३ घटी है'; digit flagged, not emended. (3) Verse 45: two sign-groups do not resolve cleanly onto the ṭīkā's sign-lists — the pātāla group in particular requires Tulā, for which the OCR gives only a fragment. The doctrine itself (Kumbha/Mīna/Karka/Siṃha → mṛtyuloka; Meṣa/Vṛṣa/Mithuna/Vṛścika → svarga; Kanyā/Dhanus/Tulā/Makara → pātāla) is secure from the ṭīkā.

(47) Initiation, the establishment of the sacred fire, marriage, tonsure, the first sight of a deity or a tīrtha, the taking of saṃnyāsa and of an alms-seeker's estate[?], the audience of a king[?], royal consecration, [setting out on] a journey; the Cāturmāsya and the Samāvartana; the ordeal[?] — these one should reject when Jupiter and Venus are combust, in their infancy or old age, and likewise in a deficient or intercalary month.

[ṭīkā] Kāla-śuddhi (purity of time) is stated: the construction of a new step-well, a garden, a tank, a well, and the commencement of a house; the consecration of a house (house-entry); the commencement of vows; the concluding rite of vows; the sixteen great gifts beginning with the tulā-dāna; the Soma sacrifice; the Aṣṭakā-śrāddha; the godāna (keśānta rite); the iṣṭi-saṃcayana; a public water-shed; the first Upākarma (Śrāvaṇī); the Veda-vrata; the Upaniṣad-vrata; the Mahānāmnī and other vows; the optional vṛṣotsarga — "not the eleven-day one" — and the jātakarma and other sacraments of children, but [only] those whose proper time has already lapsed; initiation (the receiving of a mantra); the tonsure rite; the first sight of a deity or a tīrtha not seen before; the agnihotra; the Cāturmāsya sacrifice; the samāvartana; the piercing of the ears; the ordeal of the heated bean and the like (which belongs to trial by divine judgment); the entry of a new bride; the installation of a deity; the investiture with the sacred thread; marriage; the taking of saṃnyāsa; the first appearance of the menses; royal consecration; and journey — all these acts one should not perform when Jupiter and Venus are combust, in their infancy or old age, nor in an intercalary (mala) month, nor in a decayed month.
On this there is a determination in another work:
"Those [sacraments] from the sīmantonnayana and the jātakarma up to the annaprāśana — for them there is no doṣa of the intercalary month nor of the combustion of Jupiter and Venus. (1)"
"All those acts whose [proper] time has passed are to be done when the Sun is in the northern course, and when Venus and Jupiter also are visible, and on a day whose pañcāṅga is unbroken as prescribed for that act. (2)"
That is: all the infant sacraments from the sīmanta and the jātakarma up to the annaprāśana, being performed at their fixed times, incur no doṣa from an intercalary month, a decayed month, or the combustion of Jupiter or Venus. But when the proper time of the said act (as the naming rite is fixed for the 11th or 12th day, and the annaprāśana for the sixth month) has for some reason lapsed, then that act is to be performed in the northern course of the Sun, at the heliacal rising of Jupiter and Venus, and on a day whose pañcāṅga for that act is unbroken (entirely [continues in the next chunk]

THINGS TO BE SHUNNED WHEN JUPITER IS IN SIṂHA OR MAKARA, AND THE LIKE

(48) What is to be shunned at [Jupiter's] combustion is to be shunned when Jupiter stands in Siṃha or Nakra (Makara); some [say it is to be shunned] also when he is retrograde or in accelerated motion (aticāra); [and] in the Gurvāditya [conjunction], and in a Viśvadhasra fortnight also; and likewise, they have said, the wearing of ivory, jewels and similar ornaments.

[ṭīkā] Whatever acts have been declared prohibited when Jupiter is combust are prohibited also when Jupiter is in Siṃha or in Makara; but by the opinion of other ācāryas there is no doṣa (affliction) for a pilgrimage to Gayā or the Godāvarī. Certain ācāryas hold that the said acts are prohibited also when Jupiter is retrograde or in aticāra, but [only] for 28 days [continues in the next chunk]

सिंहस्थ गुरुके परिहार तीन प्रकारसे कहते हैं। विवाह तथा मतांतरसे व्रतबन्ध मात्रमें सिंह गुरुका दोष है, अन्य कार्योंमें नहीं; वह भी सिंहराशिके सिंहांशक १३।२० अंशसे १६।४० अंशपर्यन्त, समस्त सिंहराशिके गुरुमें नहीं। गोदावरीके उत्तर, भागीरथीके दक्षिण—अर्थात् गंगा-गोदावरी नदियोंके बीच जो देश हैं—उनमें उक्त दोष है, अन्य देशोंमें नहीं। और मेषके सूर्य (सौरमान) के वैशाखमें भी उक्त दोष सर्वत्र नहीं है ॥ ४९ ॥ (इ० व०)।

[ṭīkā, continued] …[only] up to [28 days]. And there is also this: that for one from whose [birth-sign] Jupiter stands by transit in the 5th, 9th, 7th, 2nd or 11th rāśi (sign), there is no doṣa (affliction) in the said acts even during retrogression or aticāra — this too is a divergent opinion. And in the Gurvāditya — Jupiter and the Sun being in one and the same sign — the said [acts] are likewise prohibited. By another opinion the Gurvāditya is said to be the Sun in Jupiter's sign and Jupiter in the [Sun's] sign, and in that all auspicious acts are prohibited; but the principal view is the one first stated. Likewise in a Viśvadhasra fortnight — the fortnight in which two tithis are lost so that the fortnight is of thirteen (13) days — the said acts are also prohibited. And ornaments of ivory and the like, and those of jewels and the like, are not to be worn under the said doṣa (Jupiter in Siṃha etc.). (48) (Śālinī)

THREEFOLD PARIHĀRA (CANCELLATION) FOR JUPITER STANDING IN SIṂHA

(49) When Jupiter is in Siṃha and in the Siṃha [navāṃśa], marriage is inauspicious; and [the doṣa holds] north of the Godāvarī and on the southern bank of the Bhāgīrathī — [it is] a doṣa there alone, not in another country, nor even when the Sun is in Meṣa.

[ṭīkā] The parihāra for Jupiter standing in Siṃha is stated in three ways. The doṣa of Jupiter in Siṃha applies to marriage only — and by another opinion to the investiture with the sacred thread as well — and not to other undertakings. And even then it applies only to the Siṃha navāṃśa of the sign Siṃha, from 13°20′ to 16°40′, and not to Jupiter throughout the whole sign of Siṃha. The said doṣa holds in the countries north of the Godāvarī and south of the Bhāgīrathī — that is, in the lands lying between the Gaṅgā and the Godāvarī — and not in other countries. And in the Vaiśākha of the Sun in Meṣa (by solar reckoning) the said doṣa likewise does not hold anywhere. (49) (Indravajrā)

(नीच) मकरके बृहस्पतिका दोषपरिहार दो प्रकारसे कहते हैं कि—रेवा (नर्मदा), दक्षिण अमरकंटकसे जबलपुर, विंध्यके पार्श्व, होशंगाबाद[?], ओंकारनाथ, मण्डलेश्वर, महेश्वर, भडोचके समीप, खम्भातकी खाड़ीमें, द्वारिकाके समीप पश्चिम समुद्रमें मिली है—उसके पूर्व भागके देशोंमें; तथा (गंडकी) नेपाल जिलाके पश्चिम भाग, हिमालय मुक्तिनाथसे पटना हरिहर क्षेत्र पर गंगामें मिली, इससे लेकर मानपर्वत व सारस्वतदेश अर्थात् द्वारिकाके उत्तर-पश्चिम समुद्रपर्यन्त गण्डकीका पश्चिम है—इन देशोंमें; तथा शोणनद (अमरकंटकसे विंध्याचल होकर जिला आरा और मनेरके बीच गंगामें मिला) इससे दक्षिण उड़ीसा, सिरगुजा, लोहारदगा, सुहता, सगड, विहार आदि, एवम् उत्तरमें बुंदेलखण्ड, प्रयागराज (इलाहाबाद), अवध, रुहेलखण्ड, दिल्ली (इन्द्रप्रस्थ), आगरा, मथुरा, नदीनाथ, ज्वालामुखी आदि उत्तर हिमालयपर्यन्त—इन देशोंमें मकरगुरुका दोष नहीं। तथा (कोंकण) मुंबईसे १४० मील दक्षिण समुद्रके तीर, (गौडदेश) गौड, बंगाला, मालदह, पुर्णिया (लक्ष्मणावती), जन्नताबाद, (मगधदेश) जिला गया, पटना, (सिंधुदेश) अटक और शेरमके बीच जिसको सिंधुसागर कहते हैं—इन देशोंमें शुभकार्य वर्जित हैं। इन दोनों ही पक्षोंसे अतिरिक्त देशोंको ग्रन्थांतरीयमतसे ६० दिन वर्जित हैं। तथा मकरमें मकरांशमात्र वर्जित है, समस्त मकरगुरु तथा सभी देशोंके लिये नहीं*॥ ५२ ॥ (शालिनी)

लुप्तसंवत्सरदोषापवादः

गोऽजान्त्यकुम्भेतरभेऽतिचारगो नो पूर्वराशिं गुरुरेति वक्रितः ।
तदा विलुप्ताब्द इहातिनिन्दितः शुभेषु रेवासुरनिम्नगान्तरे ॥ ५३ ॥

Prakaraṇa 1 — with the Hindī ṭīkā (commentary) · page (21)

TWOFOLD PARIHĀRA (CANCELLATION) FOR JUPITER STANDING IN MAKARA

(52) East of the Revā, west of the Gaṇḍakī, and north and south of the Śoṇa, Jupiter in his debilitation is not[?] to be shunned; but in Koṅkaṇa, in Magadha, in Gauḍa and in Sindhu he is to be shunned in auspicious [undertakings].

[ṭīkā] The cancellation of the doṣa (affliction) of Jupiter in Makara (his debilitation) is stated in two ways.
First, the Revā (Narmadā) — which runs from Amarakaṇṭaka in the south by Jabalpur, along the flank of the Vindhya, Hoshangabad[?], Oṃkāranātha, Maṇḍaleśvara, Maheśvara, past Broach, and joins the western sea in the Gulf of Khambhat near Dvārakā — in the countries east of it; and the Gaṇḍakī — which from the western part of the Nepal district, from Muktinātha in the Himālaya, joins the Gaṅgā at the Harihara-kṣetra at Patna, and west of which lie Mount Māna and the Sārasvata country up to the sea north-west of Dvārakā — in those countries; and the Śoṇa river — to its south, Odisha, Sirguja, Lohardaga, Suhta, Sagaḍ, Bihar and the rest, and to its north Bundelkhand, Prayāgarāja (Allahabad), Avadh, Rohilkhand, Delhi (Indraprastha), Agra, Mathurā, Nadīnātha, Jvālāmukhī and so on up to the northern Himālaya — in these countries there is no doṣa of Jupiter in Makara.
But in Koṅkaṇa (the sea-coast 140 miles south of Bombay), in the Gauḍa country (Gauḍa, Bengal, Maldah, Purnia, Jannatabad), in the Magadha country (the districts of Gayā and Patna), and in the Sindhu country (between Attock and Sherm, which is called the Sindhu-sāgara) — in these countries auspicious undertakings are prohibited.
For countries falling outside both these divisions, by the opinion of another work 60 days are to be shunned. And within Makara only the Makara navāṃśa is prohibited, not the whole of Jupiter's transit of Makara, nor for all countries.* (52) (Śālinī)

THE EXCEPTION (APAVĀDA) TO THE DOṢA OF THE LOST YEAR (LUPTA-SAṂVATSARA)

(53) If, having gone by aticāra (accelerated motion) into a sign other than Go (Vṛṣa), Aja (Meṣa), Antya (Mīna) and Kumbha, Jupiter when retrograde does not return to the former sign, then that is [called] the lost year; and it is exceedingly censured here for auspicious [undertakings] in the tract between the Revā and the river of the gods (the Gaṅgā).
ocr_review_note: Two flagged points. (1) Verse 52 pāda 3, a negation plus a lost word or two; the sense (no doṣa in the regions just named) is fixed by the ṭīkā, but the printed reading is not. (2) In the ṭīkā's course of the Narmadā, a corrupt place-name, read conjecturally as Hoshangabad and flagged. The remainder, including verse 53, is clean.

content_en:
[ṭīkā, on verse 53] If Jupiter, in signs other than Vṛṣa, Meṣa, Mīna and Kumbha, passes by aticāra (accelerated motion) into the next sign (within ten or eleven months), and then turning retrograde after some days does not come back into the former sign, that year is called "lost" (lupta); and it is exceedingly censured for auspicious undertakings. But if he performs the aticāra in the 1st, 2nd, 11th or 12th signs, the doṣa (affliction) of the lost year does not obtain. There is also a parihāra (cancellation) by difference of region: the Revā (Narmadā) [continues in the next chunk]

[ṭīkā, footnote] * On this subject, in Saṃvat 1946, A.D. 1890, at the instigation of certain envious persons, I published a critical review of this matter in the newspapers; upon which I received from an assembly of 64 learned Ārya[?] śāstrins resident in Kāśī a certificate of victory embodying their determination, in which the above is established by many proofs.
ocr_review_note: One flagged reading, in the footnote: the number 64 and the sense are clear, but the qualifying word (read here as 'आर्य') and the case-ending are corrupt. The doctrinal body of the ṭīkā is clean.

और (गंगा) भागीरथीके देशोंमें लुप्तसंवत्सरका दोष है, अन्यत्र नहीं। आचार्यान्तरमतसे बृहस्पति-शुक्रके सम-सप्तम (एकसे दूसरी सातवीं राशि) में होनेपर भी उक्त देशोंमें अस्तके तुल्य दोष है ॥ ५३ ॥ (वंशस्थ)।

वारप्रवृत्तिः

पादोनरेखापरपूर्वयोजनैः[?] ...ऋणधनोनास्तिथयो[?] दिनार्धतः ।
ऊनाधिकास्तद्विवरोद्भवैः[?] पटेर्ध्वं तथाधो दिनपप्रवेशनम् ॥ ५४ ॥

लंकासे सुमेरपर्यन्त एक समसूत्र बांधकर उसके नीचे जो जो आवें वह मध्य रेखा है। जहांसे उस रेखागत कोई देश समीप हो, वह जितने योजन (चार कोशका एक) हो, वे देशांतर योजन कहते हैं। उन योजनोंके चतुर्थांश घटाकर पंद्रह (१५) में (न्यूनाधिक)—पर योजन हो तो जोड़ना, पूर्व हो तो घटाना। जिस दिन वारप्रवेश देखना है उस दिनके दिनार्धमें (न्यूनाधिक) पन्द्रहमें न्यून वा अधिक किया गया जो देशांतर है, वह (१५) से अधिक हो तो उसमें १५ घटाना; यदि १५ से न्यून हो तो [दिनार्ध] से उसे घटा देना—यह वारप्रवृत्ति होती है। उसमें भी स्मरण रखना चाहिये कि दिनार्ध संस्कारविशिष्ट अंकसे यदि १५ न्यून हो तो सूर्योदयसे पीछे; उक्त पलोंमें यदि १५ से न्यून वह गणितागत अंक हो तो सूर्योदयसे प्रथम ही वार प्रवेश जानना।
उदाहरण—काशीपुरी प्राक् मध्यरेखा कुरुक्षेत्रसे ६३ योजन है; चौथाई घटाया ४७।१५; प्राक्योजन होनेसे १५ में पल ४७ घटाये तो १४।१३ हुए; दिनार्ध १७।२ से न्यून होनेसे १४।१३ घटाया, २।४९ शेष रहा। दिनार्धसे न्यून गणितागत अंक होनेसे सूर्योदयसे पीछे २।४९ में वारप्रवेश होगा ॥ ५४ ॥ (उपजाति)।

वारादेर्घटिकाद्विघ्नाः[?] स्वाक्ष...[?]शेषवर्जिताः ।
सैकास्त...[?] नगैः कालहोरेशा दिनपात्क्रमात् ॥ ५५ ॥

[संख्याको] द्विगुण कर २ जगह स्थापन करना; एक जगह (५) से भा[ग]

(22) Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi [Śubhāśubha-prakaraṇa]

[ṭīkā, completing verse 53] …and in the countries of the Bhāgīrathī (Gaṅgā) the doṣa (affliction) of the lost year obtains, and nowhere else. By the opinion of other ācāryas, when Jupiter and Venus stand in mutual seventh signs (from one to the seventh from it) there is, in the said countries, a doṣa equal to that of combustion. (53) (Vaṃśastha)

THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE WEEKDAY

(54) [Take] the yojanas east or west of the meridian, less a quarter[?]; …subtracted or added[?] from half the day; less or more by the difference thence arising[?] — [thus is found] the entry of the day-lord, above or below [sunrise].

[ṭīkā] Stretch a straight line from Laṅkā to Sumeru; whatever places fall beneath it constitute the central meridian. The distance in yojanas (one yojana being four kośa) by which any country lies from that meridian is called the deśāntara-yojanas. Deduct a quarter of those yojanas, and [apply the remainder] to fifteen (15) — adding if the place is WEST [of the meridian], subtracting if EAST. On the day for which the weekday-entry is to be found, in the half-day of that day, [take] the deśāntara thus made less or greater than fifteen: if it exceeds 15, subtract 15 from it; if it is less than 15, subtract it from [the half-day] — this gives the commencement of the weekday. One should further bear in mind: if the deśāntara-corrected half-day figure comes out less than 15, the weekday-entry falls after sunrise; whereas if the computed figure itself (in the palas just described) is less than 15, the weekday-entry is to be reckoned as falling before sunrise. [?] Example: the city of Kāśī lies 63 yojanas east of the central meridian at Kurukṣetra; deducting a quarter gives 47;15. Being an eastern longitude, 47 palas are subtracted from 15, giving 14;13. Since this is less than the half-day 17;2, subtracting 14;13 leaves a remainder of 2;49. As the computed figure is less than the half-day, the weekday-entry will occur 2;49 after sunrise. (54) (Upajāti)

THE HORĀS, PREFACED BY THE PURPOSE OF THE WEEKDAY-COMMENCEMENT

(55) [The count] from the weekday, in ghaṭikās, doubled[?]; …[?] with the remainder removed; increased by one …[?]; [divided] by seven (naga) — [thus] the lords of the kāla-horās, from the day-lord, in order.

[ṭīkā] Double [the number] and place it in two positions; in one position divi[de] by (5) [continues in the next chunk]
ocr_review_note: CORRECTED 2026-08-03 after independent verification (verifier findings: (1) east/west sign of the deśāntara correction was inverted — the Hindi unambiguously reads 'पर योजन हो तो जोड़ना, पूर्व हो तो घटाना' = add if WEST, subtract if EAST, which the worked Kāśī example itself already confirmed (Kāśī is east of the meridian and 47 is subtracted) even though the general rule as first translated said the opposite; now corrected to match both the ṭīkā's own wording and its own worked example. (2) A full rule-bearing sentence on whether weekday-entry falls before or after sunrise was present in cleaned_devanagari_text but dropped from content_en; it has been restored, rendered as literally as the compressed Hindi allows, and marked [?] since the underlying procedural clause is terse enough that independent re-derivation was not possible this pass.) Four or more other flagged points remain as originally noted: verses 54 and 55's mūla are badly corrupt and the renderings are governed by the ṭīkā's worked procedure, not the verse text.

(२३)

बुधकी होरा हुई। यहां वारप्रवृत्ति केवल कालहोराके निमित्त है, और कार्योंमें वार सूर्योदयसे ही माना जाता है—यह वसिष्ठसिद्धान्तमें लिखा है ॥ ५५ ॥ (अनु०)।

कालहोराप्रयोजनम्

वारे प्रोक्तं कालहोरासु तस्य धिष्ण्ये प्रोक्तं स्वामितिथ्यंशके[?]ऽस्य ।
कुर्याद्दिक्शूलादि[?] चिन्त्यं क्षणेषु नैवोद्धृष्यः[?] परिवेश्चापि[?] दण्डः ॥ ५६ ॥

कालहोराका प्रयोजन है कि, जो कार्य जिस वारमें करना कहा है वह उसकी कालहोरामें हर एक वारमें कर लेना। जैसे रविवारके दिन प्रवेशका निषेध है, परन्तु चन्द्र, बुध, गुरु, शुक्रके होरामें रविवारके दिन भी आवश्यकमें प्रवेश कर लेना। ऐसे ही जिस नक्षत्रमें जो कार्य नहीं करना कहा है, उसमें यदि आवश्यक हो तो उस नक्षत्रमें जिस मुहूर्तमें पूर्वोक्त नक्षत्रके स्वामीकी कालहोरा हो, उसमें वह कृत्य कर लेना। मुहूर्तके स्वामी विवाहप्रकरणमें कहे हैं। उक्त विषयके मुहूर्तमें इतना अवश्य स्मरण चाहिये कि दिक्शूल तथा परिदण्डादि विचार छोड़ें नहीं—इनका विचार यात्राप्रकरणमें है ॥ ५६ ॥ (शालिनी)।

मन्वादियुगादीनां निर्णयस्तन्निषेधश्च

मन्वाद्या[?]क्षितिथी मधौ तिथिरवी[?] ...शुचौ दिक्तिथी-
ज्येष्ठेऽन्त्ये च तिथिस्त्विषे[?] नव तपस्याः सहस्ये शिवाः ।
भाद्रेऽग्निश्च सिते त्वमाष्टनभसः कृष्णे युगाः सिते
गोऽग्नी[?] गाहुलराधयोर्मेदनदशौ[?] भाद्रमाघासिते ॥ ५७ ॥

इति मुहूर्तचिन्तामणौ प्रथमं शुभाशुभप्रकरणम् ॥ १ ॥

चैत्र शुक्लपक्षकी ३।१५; कार्तिक शुक्लकी १५।१२; आषाढ शुक्लकी १०।१५; ज्येष्ठ तथा फाल्गुनकी १५; आश्विन शुक्लकी [?]; माघशुक्लकी ७; पौषशुक्लकी ११; भाद्रशुक्लकी ३; श्रावणकृष्णकी ३० (अमा), ८ (अष्टमी)—ये मन्वादि हैं। और कार्तिकशुक्लकी ९; वैशाखशुक्लकी ३; भाद्रकृष्णकी १३; माघकी ३० (अमा)—ये युगादि हैं। इतनी तिथियां पुण्यपर्व

Prakaraṇa 1 — with the Hindī ṭīkā (commentary) · page (23)

[ṭīkā, completing verse 55] …so it is Mercury's horā. Here the commencement of the weekday is reckoned only for the sake of the kāla-horā; in [other] undertakings the weekday is counted from sunrise alone — so it is written in the Vasiṣṭha-siddhānta. (55) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE PURPOSE OF THE KĀLA-HORĀ

(56) What is prescribed for a [particular] vāra (weekday) [may be done] in the kāla-horās of that [lord]; what is prescribed for [a particular] nakṣatra (lunar mansion), in the [horā of] its lord[?] … One should [nevertheless] consider the dik-śūla[?] and the like at those moments; and [the] paridaṇḍa[?] is not to be disregarded[?].

[ṭīkā] The purpose of the kāla-horā is this: an act that is prescribed to be done on a particular weekday may be done on any weekday in the kāla-horā of that [weekday's lord]. For example, house-entry is prohibited on a Sunday; yet in the horā of the Moon, Mercury, Jupiter or Venus, entry may in case of necessity be made even on a Sunday. In the same way, where an act is prohibited in a particular nakṣatra, then if it be unavoidable, that act may be performed in that nakṣatra during the muhūrta in which the kāla-horā of the lord of the aforesaid nakṣatra falls. The lords of the muhūrtas are stated in the marriage chapter. In the muhūrta for the said purpose this much must be borne in mind — that the considerations of dik-śūla and paridaṇḍa and the like are not to be dropped; their consideration is given in the chapter on journeys. (56) (Śālinī)

DETERMINATION OF THE MANVĀDI AND YUGĀDI [TITHIS], AND THEIR PROHIBITION

(57) [The verse enumerates the manvādi and yugādi tithis by month and numeral-word; the printed text is substantially corrupt in the scan and is not rendered word-for-word. Its content is given by the ṭīkā below.]

Here ends the first chapter, the Śubhāśubha-prakaraṇa, in the Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi. (1)

[ṭīkā] The 3rd and 15th of the bright fortnight of Caitra; the 15th and 12th of the bright fortnight of Kārtika; the 10th and 15th of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha; the 15th of Jyeṣṭha and of Phālguna; the [?] of the bright fortnight of Āśvina; the 7th of the bright fortnight of Māgha; the 11th of the bright fortnight of Pauṣa; the 3rd of the bright fortnight of Bhādrapada; and the 30th (new moon) and 8th (aṣṭamī) of the dark fortnight of Śrāvaṇa — these are the manvādi [tithis]. And the 9th of the bright fortnight of Kārtika, the 3rd of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, the 13th of the dark fortnight of Bhādrapada, and the 30th (new moon) of Māgha — these are the yugādi. These tithis are holy occasions [continues in the next chunk]

content_en:
The wearing of cloth even on a defective day (in certain cases)

That which is [given] at the command of a brāhmaṇa, and at a marriage, and what a king has bestowed out of affection — such cloth, the wise have declared, may be worn even on a censured [day]: on Pitrya (Maghā)[?], on an [inauspicious] vāra (weekday), and so forth. || 12 ||

[ṭīkā] When cloth and the like is given at the command of a brāhmaṇa, at a wedding, or by a king out of pleasure, then it may be put on even without the muhūrta (elected moment) stated above, or even in a censured nakṣatra (lunar mansion), vāra, and so on. || 12 || (Anuṣṭubh)

content_en:
(36) Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi [Nakṣatra-]

The muhūrta for the oblation of homa
From the Sun's nakṣatra (lunar mansion), counting by threes up to the Moon's nakṣatra: the Sun, Vid (Mercury), Śukra (Venus) and Paṅgu ("the lame one" — Saturn); then the Moon, Āra (Mars), Ijya (Jupiter), Ahi[?] (Rāhu) and Śikhin (Ketu). The homa-oblation is not desirable in [the share of] a malefic. || 35 ||

[ṭīkā] The oblation of homa is stated: perform the homa in the oblation-share of a benefic planet, not in that of a malefic. Counting three by three from the Sun's nakṣatra up to the Moon's nakṣatra, know the oblation to belong, in order, to the Sun in the first three, to Mercury in the next three, and thereafter to Venus, Saturn, the Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Rāhu and Ketu. || 35 || (Anuṣṭubh)

The residence of Vahni (fire), and its fruit — agnivāsa
That [current] tithi (lunar day), with one added and joined to the vāra (weekday), is divided by four. When the remainder is guṇa (three) or abhra (zero), the residence of Vahni (fire) is upon the earth: therein a homa makes for happiness. When the remainder is śaśi (one) or yugma (two), [the fire dwells] in the sky and beneath the earth respectively, and there is destruction of the life-breath and of wealth. || 36 ||

[ṭīkā] Add 1 to the current tithi, add the vāra, divide by 4 and keep the remainder. If the remainder is 0 or 3, know the residence of Agni to be in the earth: performing the oblation will bring happiness. If the remainder is 1 or 2, the residence of Vahni is, respectively, in the sky (ākāśa) and in the netherworld (pātāla); performing a homa then destroys the life-breath and wealth. || 36 || (Indravajrā)

The muhūrta for eating the new grain
The new grain is auspicious in a cara ("movable"), kṣipra ("swift") or mṛdu ("soft") nakṣatra and in a good lagna (ascendant) — excluding the nandā tithis, the viṣa-ghaṭī ("poison hour"), the months Madhu (Caitra) and Pauṣa, and the days of Ārki (Saturn) and Bhūmija (Mars). || 37 ||

[ṭīkā] Leaving aside all of these — the months Pauṣa and Caitra, Saturday and Tuesday, the nandā tithis 1, 6 and 11, and the viṣa-ghaṭī (as stated in the marriage chapter) — one should take the first eating of the grain of the new harvest (navānna) in a desired lagna occupied by benefics, and in the cara, kṣipra and mṛdu nakṣatras. || 37 || (Anuṣṭubh)

The muhūrta for building a boat
In the nakṣatras of Yāmya (Bharaṇī), Brāhma[?] (Rohiṇī), Viśākhā, Indra (Jyeṣṭhā), Sārpa (Āśleṣā), Pitrya (Maghā), Īśa (Ārdrā) and Maitra (Anurādhā), on the days of Bhṛgu (Venus), Ijya (Jupiter) and Arka (the Sun), the building of a boat in a good lagna is auspicious. || 38 ||

[ṭīkā] In the nakṣatras Bharaṇī, Rohiṇī, Viśākhā, Jyeṣṭhā, Āśleṣā, Maghā and Ārdrā[?], and on Friday, Thursday and Sunday, one should build a boat (a vessel or dinghy) and the like. || 38 || (Anuṣṭubh)

The muhūrta for vīra-sādhana and the like
In Mūla, Ārdrā, Bharaṇī, Pitrya (Maghā) and Mṛgaśirā, with Saumya (Mercury) [in the lagna] — or Venus in the fourth (sukha) — the lagna being Ghaṭa (Aquarius) and the eighth house unoccupied, there is success in vīra-sādhana (the propitiation of a vīra spirit) and in abhicāra (hostile magical rites). || 39 ||
ocr_review_note: Three flagged loci, none of them in the agnivāsa passage. (1) v.35 pāda 3: OCR 'आगु' for the Rāhu-word — both अहि ('serpent', a standard Rāhu epithet) and अगु scan in Anuṣṭubh, and the ṭīkā fixes the referent as Rāhu, so only the akṣara is at issue. (2) v.38 pāda 1: OCR 'याम्य्यविशाच…' leaves one two-syllable nakṣatra term illegible; Anuṣṭubh requires 16 syllables in the first line, and ब्राह्म (Rohiṇī) both fills the gap and matches the ṭīkā's list, but it is supplied, not read. (3) v.38 ṭīkā: OCR 'आर्द्रारहित' reads either as 'आर्द्रा-रहित' (excluding Ārdrā), which contradicts the mūla's ईश = Ārdrā, or as 'आर्द्रा, राधा' (Ārdrā, Anurādhā), which agrees with it; the two readings invert the sense of the whole rule and the scan cannot arbitrate. NOTE: verse 36, the agnivāsa rule itself, is clean — all four pādas scan exactly as Indravajrā, and the ṭīkā's arithmetic (remainder 0/3 = earth, 1 = sky, 2 = pātāla) independently confirms the emendation शेषे गुणेऽभ्रे (guṇa = 3, abhra = 0) against OCR 'शेषे एणेऽभरे'. Verse numbers ३७ and ३९ were printed by OCR as '२७' and '२९' and are corrected on the ṭīkā's authority.

[ṭīkā] If a person falls ill in the nakṣatra (lunar mansion)s Ārdrā, Āśleṣā, Jyeṣṭhā, Śatatārā (Śatabhiṣā), Bharaṇī, the three Pūrvās, Viśākhā, Dhaniṣṭhā or Kṛttikā; or on a pāpa-vāra (a malefic weekday); or on a riktā tithi (the lunar days 4, 9 and 14), on the twelfth or on the sixth — then that sick person swiftly meets death. It is especially so when the Moon stands in the 4th, 8th or 12th by transit [from the natal rāśi]. || 47 || (Upajāti)

content_en: On a bhadrā tithi (lunar day — the 2nd, 7th or 12th), on the vāra (weekday) of Ravija (Saturn), Bhūtanaya (Mars) or Arka (the Sun), and in the nakṣatra (lunar mansion) of Rādhā (Viśākhā), Aryaman (Uttaraphālgunī), Ajacaraṇa (Pūrvabhādrapadā), Aditi (Punarvasu), Vahni (Kṛttikā) or Vaiśva (Uttarāṣāḍhā)[?] — there arises the Tripuṣkara yoga, which renders threefold whatever occurs by way of death, of loss, or of increase; and it makes [only] twofold when [the nakṣatra is] Vasu (Dhaniṣṭhā), Tvāṣṭra (Citrā) or Cāndra (Mṛgaśirā). || 50 ||

(40) Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi [Nakṣatra-]

[ṭīkā, on verse 50] The bhadrā tithi (lunar day)s 2, 7 and 12; Saturday, Tuesday and Sunday; and the nakṣatra (lunar mansion)s Viśākhā, Uttaraphālgunī, Pūrvabhādrapadā, Punarvasu, Kṛttikā and Uttarāṣāḍhā — when this much of tithi, vāra (weekday) and nakṣatra falls at one and the same time, the Tripuṣkara yoga is formed. If someone dies in it, two more will die in that house; if some article is lost, two more will be lost; if some article is gained or increases, two more will be gained. If, in the place of [those] nakṣatras, Dhaniṣṭhā, Citrā or Mṛgaśirā stands, the said results become twofold — this is the Dvipuṣkara yoga. || 50 || (Vasantatilakā)

Times forbidden for the cremation of a substitute effigy of the corpse
On the days of Śukra (Venus), Āra (Mars) and Ārki (Saturn); on darśa (the new moon), bhūta (the fourteenth) and madana (the thirteenth); on the nandā tithis[?]; in a tīkṣṇa ("sharp") or ugra ("fierce") nakṣatra, in Pauṣṇa (Revatī) or Vāruṇa (Śatabhiṣā); on a Tripuṣkara day; in a deficient (kṣaya) or intercalary (adhika) month; at an ayana (solstitial ingress) — and, if more than a year has passed [since the death], also in the southern (yāmya) course; in the Pāta (Vyatīpāta) and Parigha yogas; when Devejya (Jupiter) or Venus is heliacally set; in Bhadrā and Vaidhṛti; and in the bright fortnight — the cremation of the effigy-image of the corpse is not [to be performed]. || 51 ||

For the performer, the janma and pratyari tārās, and the Moon in the fourth, twelfth or eighth[?] [from his natal rāśi], are not good. In Sanmaitra (Anurādhā), Bhaga (Pūrvaphālgunī), Aditi (Punarvasu), the dhruva ("fixed") nakṣatras, Viśākhā …[?] and Citrā, and on Wednesday, [the act is] admissible as well [though middling]. It is best on the days of Arka (the Sun), Ijya (Jupiter) and Vidhu (the Moon), and in Śruti (Śravaṇa), Kara (Hasta), Svātī, Aśvinī and Puṣya. And all this is to be weighed after the period of impurity has passed; within it, only so far as is possible. || 52 ||

[ṭīkā] When the corpse of one who has died is not recovered, the muhūrta for making the parṇaśara (the leaf-effigy, pratikṛti) is stated: one should not perform the cremation of the parṇaśara on Friday, Tuesday or Saturday; on the fourteenth, the new moon or the thirteenth; on the nandā tithis 1, 6, 11; in tīkṣṇa and ugra nakṣatras, in Revatī or Śatatārā; in the Tripuṣkara yoga; in an intercalary or deficient month; at the Karka and Makara saṅkrāntis; and — if more than a year has passed since the death — also in the dakṣiṇāyana (southern course); likewise in the Vyatīpāta and Parigha yogas, when Venus or Jupiter is heliacally set, in Bhadrā and Vaidhṛti, and in the bright fortnight. || 51 || For the one performing the rite, that day should not be his janma [nakṣatra] or his pratyari tārā, and the Moon should not be in the 4th, 8th or 12th from his natal rāśi. In Anurādhā, Pūrvaphālgunī, Punarvasu, the dhruva nakṣatras, Viśākhā, Mṛgaśirā, Citrā, Dhaniṣṭhā, and on Wednesday, the said act is called middling; while Sunday, Thursday and Monday, and the nakṣatras Śravaṇa, Hasta, Svātī, Puṣya and Aśvinī, are auspicious. All these considerations [apply] after the period of impurity… [the sentence continues in the following chunk]
ocr_review_note: The priority content — the ṭīkā of v.50, which defines the Tripuṣkara and Dvipuṣkara vāra × nakṣatra × tithi yogas — is clean and carries no flags; all three flags fall in vv. 51–52. (1) v.51 pāda 1: the reconstruction 'दर्शभूतमदने नन्दासु तीक्ष्णोग्रभे' matches the ṭīkā term for term, but syllables 14–18 do not scan as Śārdūlavikrīḍita, indicating a residual OCR corruption or lost word-order that the ṭīkā cannot localise. (2) v.52 pāda 1: OCR 'तिसखान्त्यऽब्ने'; 'सुखान्त्यरन्ध्रे' (4th / 12th / 8th) is supplied from the ṭīkā's '​चौथा आठवां बारहवां चन्द्रमा' and is a reconstruction, not a reading. (3) v.52 pāda 2: OCR 'विशाखाद्वयङ्चिभ' leaves one or two nakṣatra terms illegible; the ṭīkā's list requires Mṛgaśirā and Dhaniṣṭhā at this point, but neither can be read off the scan. Pāda 3 of v.52 was recovered and verifies at 19 syllables against the ṭīkā's day- and nakṣatra-list.
