Chapter 2] With the Hindi ṭīkā (41)

The auspicious and inauspicious fruit of one born in Mūla or Āśleṣā
Others, again, have declared: the first eight ghaṭīs of Mūla and the last five nāḍīs of Śakra (Jyeṣṭhā) [are abhukta-mūla]. One should abandon the child so born; or else the father should not look upon its face for eight years. || 54 ||

[ṭīkā] Other ācāryas say that the 8 ghaṭīs at the beginning of Mūla and the 5 ghaṭīs at the end of Jyeṣṭhā constitute abhukta-mūla. Here, [the other] being the majority opinion, the ācārya has taken Nārada's view alone as authoritative. If a child is born in this abhukta-mūla, it is to be abandoned; or else the father should not look upon that child's face for eight years, and only then, after performing śānti (the propitiatory rite), should he look. By extension, the same consideration applies to the end of Āśleṣā, the beginning of Maghā, and so forth. || 54 || (Upajāti)

In the first pāda (quarter) of Mūla the father meets destruction; in the second, the mother; in the third, wealth. Of the fourth [quarter the fruit] is auspicious; and through śānti it becomes good in every case. In Ahi-bha (Āśleṣā) the order is reversed. || 55 ||

[ṭīkā] If a daughter or a son is born in the first quarter of Mūla, the father perishes; in the second, the mother dies; in the third, there is loss of wealth; if born in the fourth quarter it becomes auspicious once śānti has been performed, and there is doṣa (affliction) to no one. In Āśleṣā this same consideration is inverted — in the fourth quarter the father, in the third the mother, in the second loss of wealth; and the first quarter becomes auspicious after śānti is done. There is a further method: it destroys the father in the 1st year, the mother in the 3rd, wealth in the 2nd, the father-in-law in the 9th, a brother in the 6th, a wife's brother or maternal uncle in the 8th, and other kinsmen not named in the 7th year — therefore it is proper to perform śānti. By yet another method, a special consideration of Mūla and Āśleṣā in the form of a tree or a creeper, by way of laying out a cakra (diagram), is set down in the cakra [tables]. || 55 || (Upajāti)

[Appended cakra tables — the Mūla-puruṣa-cakra, the Mūla-cakra for the birth of a girl, and the Sarpa-vṛkṣa-cakra. Read as: body-part or plant-part — count — result. The scan of these tables is heavily damaged and the three columns are interleaved; only the entries legible in this chunk are given, and their continuation stands in muhurta_chintamani_pg0053_c02.]

Mūla-puruṣa-cakra: at the crown 4 — destruction of cattle; at the mouth 6 — loss of wealth; at the throat 5 — gain of wealth; at the heart 5 — crookedness; at the arm 5 — gain of wealth; at […] 7 — destruction of […][?].
Mūla-cakra for a girl's birth: at the head 5 — […][?]; at the mouth 7 — the father's decease; at the eye 2 — destruction of the mother; at the neck 2 — […][?]; at the shoulder 4 — devoted to elders; at the crown 5 — a king.
Sarpa-vṛkṣa-cakra: at the fruit 10 — wealth; at the flower 9 — wealth; at the leaf 9 — fear from the king[?]; at the branch 7 — loss; at the bark 13 — […][?]; at the nakṣatra 8 — destruction of the lineage.

The other five are all cells of the three appended cakra tables, whose columns are interleaved and partly illegible. The priority passage itself (vv. 54–55: the Mūla/Āśleṣā doṣa and its śānti-parihāra, including the explicit cancellation 'शान्त्या सर्वत्र सत्स्यात्') is otherwise clean — all four pādas of v.55, and pādas 1, 2 and 4 of v.54, verify exactly against the Upajāti pattern.

(42) Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi [Nakṣatra-]

[ṭīkā, on verse 56] In the months Āṣāḍha, Bhādrapada, Āśvina and Māgha, Mūla's residence is in heaven; in Śrāvaṇa, Kārttika, Caitra and Pauṣa, upon the earth; in Phālguna, Mārgaśīrṣa, Vaiśākha and Jyeṣṭha, it dwells in the netherworld. In whichever month it dwells wherever, it produces its inauspicious fruit there alone; elsewhere[?] there is no doṣa (affliction). || 56 || (Indravajrā)

The parihāra (remedy, cancellation) of gaṇḍānta and the other defects
Gaṇḍānta; Indra (Jyeṣṭhā); the yogas Śūla, Pāta, Parigha, Vyāghāta and Atigaṇḍa; the avama (omitted, kṣaya) tithi (lunar day); a saṅkrānti (solar ingress); Vyatīpāta; Vaidhṛti; Sinīvālī, Kuhū and Darśa; Vajra; the fourteenths of the dark fortnight; Yamaghaṇṭa; the Dagdha yoga; the Mṛtyu yoga; Viṣṭi (Bhadrā); the nakṣatra (lunar mansion) of a uterine brother; and the birth[?]-nakṣatra of the parents — [a birth in any of these] is commended as auspicious [only] through śānti (the propitiatory rite). || 57 ||

[ṭīkā] Gaṇḍānta, Jyeṣṭhā, Śūla, Pāta, Parigha, Vyāghāta, Atigaṇḍa, the kṣaya (decayed) tithi, saṅkrānti, Vyatīpāta, Vaidhṛti, Sinīvālī (the earlier half of the bright first tithi), Kuhū (the later half of the dark fourteenth), Darśa (the new moon), the Vajra yoga, the dark-fortnight fourteenth, Yamaghaṇṭa, the Dagdha yoga, the Mṛtyu yoga, Bhadrā, and the birth-nakṣatras of a uterine brother and of the mother and father — the birth of a son or a daughter within this many [conditions] is inauspicious; through the śānti of these it becomes auspicious. By extension, birth during an eclipse, a trika birth (a daughter after three sons, or a son after three daughters), and the like are treated in the same way. || 57 || (Śārdūlavikrīḍita)

Consideration of the number and the form of the stars of Aśvinī and the rest
[The star-counts of the twenty-seven nakṣatras, encoded in bhūta-saṅkhyā:] …[?] …; a hundred; and thirty-two. || 58 ||

[ṭīkā] The tārās (component stars) of the nakṣatras beginning with Aśvinī are stated: Aśvinī 3, Bharaṇī 3, and likewise Kṛttikā 6, Rohiṇī 5, Mṛgaśirā 3, Ārdrā 1, Punarvasu 4, Puṣya 3, Āśleṣā 5, Maghā 5, Pūrvaphālgunī 2, Uttaraphālgunī 2, Hasta 5, Citrā 1, Svātī 1, Viśākhā 4, Anurādhā 4, Jyeṣṭhā 3, Mūla 11, Pūrvāṣāḍhā 2, Uttarāṣāḍhā 2, Abhijit 3, Śravaṇa 3, Dhaniṣṭhā 4, Śatabhiṣā 100, Pūrvabhādrapadā 2, Uttarabhādrapadā 2, Revatī 32. By the counting of these stars, and by the shapes about to be stated, the nakṣatras are recognised. || 58 || (Upajāti)

The forms of Aśvinī and the rest: a horse's face; a yoni; a razor; a cart; a deer's head; a jewel; a house[?]; an arrow; a wheel; a house; a couch; a bed; a hand; a pearl; and coral. || 59 ||

A festal arch; [a heap] resembling a bali-offering; an earring; a lion's tail; an elephant's tusk; and couches… [the verse continues in the following chunk]

वज्रं शुक्रेऽब्जे शुभमुक्ता प्रवालं भौमेऽहौ गोमेदमार्के सुनीलम् ।
केतोर्वैदूर्यं गुरोः पुष्परागं ज्ञे पाचिः [?] माणिक्यमर्के तु मध्ये ॥ ९ ॥

ग्रहोंके दुष्टफलपरिहारको प्रत्येकके मणि तथा उनके नवरत्न धारणकी विधि है कि, शुक्रका हीरा अंगूठी वा बाजूके पूर्व किनारेपर, चन्द्रमाका मोती आग्नेयमें, मंगलका मूंगा दक्षिणमें, राहुका गोमेद नैर्ऋत्यमें, शनिका नीलम पश्चिममें, केतुका वैदूर्य वायव्यमें, बृहस्पतिका पुखराज उत्तरमें, बुधका पाचि (पन्ना) ईशानमें, सूर्यकी (माणिक्य) चुन्नी मध्यमें रखना अथवा एक एक ग्रहके प्रीत्यर्थ उक्त एक एकका धारण वा दान करना ॥ ९ ॥ (शालि०)

(54)
Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi
[Gocara —]

The wearing of gems for the parihāra (remedial cancellation) of afflicted grahas

A diamond for Śukra (Venus), a fine pearl for the Moon, coral for Bhauma (Mars), gomeda for the Serpent (Rāhu), fine blue sapphire for Ārki (Saturn); vaidūrya for Ketu, topaz for Guru (Jupiter), emerald for Jña (Mercury) [?], and the ruby for the Sun — in the middle. ‖ 9 ‖

[ṭīkā] For the parihāra of the evil results of the grahas there is a rule both for wearing the gem of each singly and for wearing them all as a navaratna (nine-gem setting): Venus's diamond on the eastern edge of the ring or armlet, the Moon's pearl in the āgneya (south-east) quarter, Mars's coral in the south, Rāhu's gomeda in the nairṛtya (south-west), Saturn's blue sapphire in the west, Ketu's vaidūrya in the vāyavya (north-west), Jupiter's pukhrāj (topaz) in the north, Mercury's pācī (emerald) in the īśāna (north-east), and the Sun's māṇikya (ruby) in the middle; or else, to propitiate one particular graha, one may wear or donate the single gem named for it. ‖ 9 ‖ (Śāli°)

Ruby, pearl, coral, gārutmaka (emerald), topaz, diamond, blue sapphire, gomeda and vaidūrya — these are the gems, reckoned from the Sun onward; and gold, for the pleasure of Jña (Mercury). ‖ 10 ‖

[ṭīkā] These are the gems fit to be worn: for the Sun the ruby (cunnī), Moon the pearl, Mars the coral, Mercury the emerald (pannā), Jupiter the topaz (pukhrāj), Venus the diamond, Saturn the blue sapphire, Rāhu [?], Ketu [?]; and for the propitiation of Mercury the wearing of gold is also prescribed. ‖ 10 ‖ (Iṃ° Va°)

Substitute gems, when one lacks the means to wear costly gems

Then lājāvarta for Rāhu and Ketu; silver for Venus and the Moon; pearl for Jupiter; iron for Manda (Saturn); coral for the Sun and Mars. The tārā is arrived at by counting in repeated cycles from the janma-nakṣatra (birth lunar mansion) up to the nakṣatra of the day. ‖ 11 ‖

[ṭīkā] If one has not the means to wear a costly gem — then let him wear Mercury's gold; this sense is construed from the preceding śloka. And for Rāhu and Ketu, lājāvarta; for the Moon and Venus, silver; for Jupiter, pearl; for Saturn, iron; for the Sun and Mars, coral. Other treatises also prescribe the wearing of herbal roots (jaḍī): for the Sun, bel; Moon, dūdhiyā; Mars, gojihvā; Mercury, vidhārā; Jupiter, bhāraṅgī; Venus, siṃhapuccha; Saturn, [?]; Rāhu, candana; Ketu, asagandha. And the tārā is to be known by counting nine by nine from the janma-nakṣatra up to the day's nakṣatra through three cycles (āvṛtti) — however many fall out, so many tārās are to be understood. ‖ 11 ‖ (Śāli°)

Tārā-bala (the strength of the tārās)

आवश्यककृत्ये दुष्टताराणां परिहारः
मृत्यौ स्वर्णतिलान् विपद्यपि गुडं शाकं च जन्मस्वथो
दद्यात्प्रत्यरितारकासु लवणं सर्वा विपत्प्रत्यरिः ।
मृत्युश्चादिमपर्यये न शुभदोऽथैषां द्वितीयेऽंशका
आद्यमध्यान्त्यतृतीयकाः [?] अथ शुभाः सर्वे तृतीये स्मृताः ॥ १३ ॥

आवश्यक कृत्यमें दुष्ट ताराओंका परिहार है कि, वध ७ तारामें तिल, सुवर्ण; विपत् ३ में (गुड) चीनी आदि, जन्म तारामें (शाक) भाजी, प्रत्यरि ५ में लवण दान करना। दूसरे प्रकार परिहार है कि, पहिली आवृत्तिमें ३।५।७ तारा पूरी ६० घटी पर्यन्त नेष्ट हैं; दूसरी आवृत्तिमें विपत्‌की आदिकी २० घटी, प्रत्यरिके मध्यकी २० घटी, वधके अन्त्यकी २० घटी छोड़नी; तीसरी आवृत्तिमें सभी शुभ हैं, दोष नहीं करतीं ॥ १३ ॥ (शार्दू०)

चन्द्रावस्थागणनोपायः
षष्ट्या हतं गतर्क्षं भुक्तघटीयुतं युगाहतम् ।
शेषं च शराब्धिहृत् [?] लब्धतोऽर्कशेषेऽवस्थाः क्रियाद्विधोः ॥ १४ ॥

प्रत्येक राशियोंमें चन्द्रमाकी १२ अवस्था होती हैं, नामसदृश फल समस्त कार्यारम्भमें देती हैं। अश्विनीसे लेकर जितने नक्षत्र हों उस संख्याको ६० से गुना कर वर्तमान नक्षत्रकी भुक्त घटी जोड़ देनी, ४ से गुणाकर ४५ से भाग लेना; जो लब्ध हुआ वह गत अवस्था, शेष वर्तमान अवस्था होती है। ४५ के भाग देनेसे लब्धि १२ से अधिक होवे तो १२ से भाग लेकर शेष गत अवस्था जाननी, उसके आधेकी वर्तमान अवस्था होती है। मेषके चन्द्रमा प्रवासादि, वृषमें नाशादि, मिथुनमें मरणादि — ऐसे ही सबका क्रम जानना। प्रकारान्तरसे इन अवस्थाओंके गिनलेका क्रम चक्रमें लिखा है (चक्र ५५, ५७ में देखो) ॥ १४ ॥ (अनु०)

अवस्थानामानि
प्रवासनाशौ मरणं जयश्च हास्यारतिक्रीडितसुप्तभुक्ताः ।
ज्वराख्यकम्पस्थिरता अवस्था मेषात्क्रमान्नामसदृक्फलाः स्युः ॥ १५ ॥

अवस्था नाम — प्रवास १, नाश २, मरण ३, जय ४, हास्य ५, अरति ६, क्रीडित ७

Chapter 4]
With the Hindi ṭīkā
(55)

The parihāra (remedial cancellation) of the evil tārās in a necessary undertaking

In the mṛtyu[-tārā] let him give gold and sesame; in vipat, jaggery; in the janma[-tārā], greens; and in the pratyari-tārā, salt. In the first cycle, the whole of vipat, pratyari and mṛtyu gives no good; in their second [cycle the portions to be avoided are] the first, middle and last thirds respectively [?]; and in the third, all are held to be auspicious. ‖ 13 ‖

[ṭīkā] The parihāra of the evil tārās in a necessary undertaking is this: in the vadha (7th) tārā give sesame and gold; in vipat (3rd), jaggery, sugar and the like; in the janma tārā, greens (śāka); in pratyari (5th), salt. A second kind of parihāra: in the first cycle (āvṛtti) the 3rd, 5th and 7th tārās are inauspicious throughout, for the full sixty ghaṭīs; in the second cycle one should leave out the first twenty ghaṭīs of vipat, the middle twenty of pratyari, and the last twenty of vadha; in the third cycle all are auspicious and cause no doṣa (affliction). ‖ 13 ‖ (Śārdū°)

The method of reckoning the Moon's avasthās
The elapsed nakṣatras multiplied by sixty, joined with the ghaṭīs already enjoyed [of the current one], multiplied by four; and the remainder divided by forty-five [?] — from the quotient, and from the remainder after [division by] twelve, one should determine the avasthās of the Moon. ‖ 14 ‖

[ṭīkā] In each rāśi the Moon has twelve avasthās (states); at the commencement of any undertaking they give results answering to their names. Take the number of nakṣatras counted from Aśvinī, multiply by 60, add the ghaṭīs already elapsed of the current nakṣatra, multiply by 4, and divide by 45; the quotient is the avasthā already past, the remainder is the current avasthā. If, on dividing by 45, the quotient exceeds 12, divide by 12 and take the remainder as the past avasthā; half of that is the current avasthā. For the Moon in Meṣa the series begins with pravāsa, in Vṛṣa with nāśa, in Mithuna with maraṇa — and so the order is to be known for all. By an alternative method, the sequence for counting these avasthās is set down in the chart (see the charts on pages 55 and 57). ‖ 14 ‖ (Anu°)

The names of the avasthās
Pravāsa and nāśa, maraṇa and jaya, hāsya, arati, krīḍita, supta, bhukta, the one called jvara, kampa, and sthiratā — these are the avasthās, in order from Meṣa, giving results resembling their names. ‖ 15 ‖

[ṭīkā] The names of the avasthās: pravāsa (sojourn abroad) 1, nāśa (loss) 2, maraṇa (death) 3, jaya (victory) 4, hāsya (laughter) 5, arati (discontent) 6, krīḍita (play) 7

(56)
Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi
[Gocara —]

The means of parihāra (remedy) for planetary derangement

A bath prepared with water containing lājā (parched grain), kuṣṭha, balā, priyaṅgu, mustā, siddhārtha (white mustard), niśā (turmeric) and dāru (devadāru), together with [śara-]puṅkhā and lodhra, is declared to destroy the evil arising from the grahas. A cow, a conch, a red bull, gold, a yellow garment, a white horse, a black cow, a buffalo and a goat [?] — these are the dakṣiṇās, reckoned from the Sun onward. ‖ 16 ‖

[ṭīkā] For the sake of the parihāra of afflicted grahas, the bathing herbs are: (lājā) parched grain, or else lajjāvatī; kūṭha; (balā) bhīmalī; mālakāṅganī; mustā; sarṣapa (mustard); devadāra; haridrā (turmeric); śarapuṅkhā; lodha. Bathing with all of these mixed into the water removes the ariṣṭa (evil) of the grahas. As to the dakṣiṇā (sacerdotal fee), it is said: to propitiate the Sun, a cow; the Moon, a conch; Mars, a red bull; Mercury, gold; Jupiter, a yellow garment; Venus, a horse; [Saturn,] a black cow; Rāhu, a khaḍga [?]; and to Ketu a goat is to be given as dakṣiṇā. ‖ 16 ‖ (Śā°)

The Chart of the Moon's Avasthās ‖

Same verse, ṭīkā: Rāhu's dakṣiṇā reads 'रा० खड' — resolvable as खड्ग (rhinoceros / sword) or खर (donkey), 1–2 akṣaras lost; it also fails to agree with the mūla reading reconstructed above, so mūla and ṭīkā loci are flagged separately.

मुहूर्तचिन्तामणि
[ गोचर-प्र० ४ ]

ग्रहाणां गन्तव्यराशेः फलदानकालः
सूर्यारसौम्यार्कजितोक्ष [?] नागसप्ताद्रिपञ्चसरान्विधोरग्निनाडीः ।

(58)
Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi
[Gocara — chapter 4]

The time at which the grahas give the result of the rāśi they are about to enter
The Sun, Mars (Āra), Mercury (Saumya) and Venus [?] — eight, seven, seven and five [days]; the Moon, three nāḍīs (ghaṭīs); Tamas (Rāhu), Yama (Saturn) and Ijyā (Jupiter) — three, six and two months: so far beforehand do they give the result of the rāśi they are about to enter. ‖ 17 ‖

[ṭīkā] The rāśi that the Sun is about to enter — its result he already gives five days beforehand; Mars from eight days, Mercury from seven days, Venus from seven days, the Moon from three ghaṭīs, Rāhu from three months, Saturn from six months, Jupiter from two months. That is, once a planet's true longitude has passed 27 degrees, it gives, in every case, the result of the rāśi ahead. ‖ 17 ‖ (U° Jā°)

Donation for the doṣa (affliction) of the tithi and the rest
For an evil yoga, gold; for the Moon, a conch; for the tithy-ardha (karaṇa, half a tithi), grain; for the tithi (lunar day), rice; for the vāra (weekday), a gem; for the ṛkṣa (lunar mansion / sign), a cow; for the nāḍī (durmuhūrta), gold; and for the tārās, rock-salt — thus let the king give. ‖ 18 ‖

[ṭīkā] Here is stated the donation for evil yogas in a necessary undertaking; "king" stands here by way of example [for whoever performs the act]. For Vyatīpāta and the like, gold; when the Moon is afflicted, a conch; for the tithi, rice; for the vāra, the gem named above; for the rāśi, a cow; for a durmuhūrta, gold; for the tārā, salt is to be given. ‖ 18 ‖ (Śālinī)

The result of the grahas' passage from one rāśi to another
The Sun and Mars give their result at the beginning of a rāśi, Venus and Jupiter always in the middle, the son of the Moon (Mercury) [throughout], the Moon and Manda (Saturn) at the end. Travel, food, fear of fire, right understanding, cloth, happiness and sorrow [respectively] in the month in which the janma-nakṣatra (birth lunar mansion) falls on Sunday and the rest. ‖ 19 ‖

Here ends the fourth Gocara chapter of the Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi composed by Śrī Daivajña Rāma, son of Ananta. ‖ 4 ‖

[ṭīkā] The Sun and Mars give their result in full within the first 10 degrees of a rāśi, and only slightly in the remaining degrees; likewise Venus and Jupiter in the middle 10 degrees, Mercury throughout all 30 degrees, and the Moon and Saturn in the last 10 degrees. In whichever month the janma-nakṣatra falls on a Sunday, there is travel; on a Monday, one obtains food and goods; likewise on Tuesday, fear of fire; on Mercury's day, righteous understanding; on Jupiter's, the obtaining of cloth; on Venus's, happiness; on Saturn's, sorrow. ‖ 19 ‖ (Va° Ti°)

Here ends the fourth Gocara chapter of the Hindi ṭīkā on the Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi composed by Mahīdhara. ‖ 4 ‖
ocr_review_note: Verse 17, pāda 1: OCR reads 'सूर्यारसौम्यार्कजितोक्ष' — the fourth planet-name in the compound is illegible; 'अर्कजित्' is not a planet-name and the ṭīkā requires Venus in this slot, so roughly 2–3 akṣaras are uncertain. The numeral-words in the same pāda and the ṭīkā together fix the sense beyond doubt (Sun 5, Mars 8, Mercury 7, Venus 7 days), so the translation is secure even though the akṣaras are not.

मातरि सगर्भायां चौलमुहूर्तः
पञ्चमासाधिके मातुर्गर्भे चौलं शिशोर्न सत् ।
पञ्चवर्षाधिकस्येष्टं गर्भिण्यामपि मातरि ॥ ३१ ॥
चौलवाले बालककी माताका गर्भ पाँच महीनेसे ऊपरका हो तो पाँच वर्षके भीतर अवस्थावालेका चूडाकर्म न करना; यदि बालक पाँच वर्षसे अधिक हो तो पाँच महीनेसे अधिक गर्भवती माता होनेमें भी दोष नहीं ॥ ३१ ॥ (अनु०)

चौले दुष्टतारापवादः
तारादौष्ठ्येऽब्जे त्रिकोणोच्चगे वा क्षौरं सत्स्यात्सौम्यमित्रस्ववर्गे ।
सौम्ये भेऽब्जे शोभने दुष्टतारा शस्ता ज्ञेया क्षौरयात्रादिकृत्ये ॥ ३२ ॥
यदि चन्द्रमा त्रिकोण (५।९) वा उच्च राशिमें हो अथवा रवि बुध गुरु शुक्रके वा अपने षड्वर्गमें तथा गोचरसे शुभस्थानमें हो तो [शुभ] नक्षत्रमें क्षौर एवं यात्रादि कृत्य दुष्ट तारामें भी कर लेना ॥ ३२ ॥

चौलादिकृत्ये निषिद्धकालः
ऋतुमत्याः सूतिकायाः सूनोश्चौलादि नाचरेत् ।
ज्येष्ठापत्यस्य न ज्येष्ठे केचिन्मार्गेऽपि नेष्यते ॥ ३३ ॥
बालककी माता रजोवती अथवा प्रसूता हो तो (चौलादि) चूडा व्रतबन्धन न करे और आद्यगर्भ कन्या पुत्रके चौल व्रत विवाह ज्येष्ठके महीनेमें न करना । कोई मार्गशीर्षमें भी न करना कहते हैं ॥ ३३ ॥ (अनुष्टुप्)

दन्तक्षौरनखक्रियाश्च विहिता चौलोदिते वारभे
[?]कुजार्कान्विहाय नवमं घस्रं च सन्ध्यां तथा ।
रिक्तां पर्व निशां निरासनरणग्रामप्रयाणोद्यतः
स्नाताभ्यक्तकृताशनेन [?] पुनः कार्यं हितप्रेप्सुभिः ॥ ३४ ॥
सामान्य क्षौर, दंत, केश, नखक्रिया भी चौलोक्त नक्षत्र वारादिकोंमें करना; मंगल, सूर्यवारमें तथा एक क्षौरसे नवमे दिनमें तथा सन्ध्या, रिक्तातिथि, पर्वदिन, रात्रिसमयमें न करना; और निरासन, रण अथवा ग्रामांतरकी तैयारीमें न्हायके नित्य नैमित्तिक कर्म करके तेल उबटन लगायके भोजन करके शृंगार भूषण वस्त्रादि पहनके अपने गुरु[?]

[Page header] Chapter 5 — with the Hindī ṭīkā — (67)

THE MUHŪRTA FOR CAUḶA WHEN THE MOTHER IS PREGNANT

(31) When the mother's pregnancy exceeds five months, the cauḷa (tonsure saṃskāra) of an infant is not proper; but for a child over five years of age it is approved even when the mother is pregnant.

[ṭīkā] If the mother of the boy whose cauḷa is due is more than five months pregnant, the cūḍākarma (tonsure rite) of a child under five years of age is not to be performed. If the child is more than five years old, there is no doṣa (blemish, astrological affliction) even though the mother is more than five months pregnant. (31) (Anuṣṭubh metre)

THE EXCEPTION (APAVĀDA) TO AN AFFLICTED TĀRĀ IN CAUḶA

(32) When the tārā (the "star", i.e. the nakṣatra of the day reckoned in the nine-fold count from the janma-nakṣatra) is defective, then if the Moon occupies a trikoṇa (trine) or is exalted, or stands in the ṣaḍvarga (six-fold divisional set) of a benefic, of a friend, or of its own, kṣaura (shaving/tonsure) is still proper. When the Moon is in an auspicious nakṣatra (lunar mansion), even a duṣṭa-tārā (afflicted tārā) is to be known as commended for such acts as kṣaura and yātrā (setting out on a journey).

[ṭīkā] If the Moon is in a trikoṇa (the 5th or 9th) or in its sign of exaltation, or is in the ṣaḍvarga of the Sun, Mercury, Jupiter or Venus, or of its own, and is besides in an auspicious place by gochara (transit) — then, in an [auspicious] nakṣatra, one may go ahead and perform kṣaura, yātrā and the like even during a duṣṭa-tārā. (32)

THE PROHIBITED TIMES FOR CAUḶA AND THE LIKE

(33) When the mother is in her courses or is newly delivered, one should not perform cauḷa and the rest for the son. For a first-born child these are not [to be done] in Jyeṣṭha; some do not approve of Mārgaśīrṣa either.

[ṭīkā] If the boy's mother is menstruating or has just given birth, do not perform the cūḍā (tonsure) or the vratabandha (upanayana, investiture with the sacred thread). And for a first-conceived child, whether daughter or son, the cauḷa, the vrata (initiation) and the vivāha (marriage) are not to be done in the month of Jyeṣṭha. Some say they are not to be done in Mārgaśīrṣa either. (33) (Anuṣṭubh)

(34) The cutting of the teeth [i.e. dental attention], shaving and nail-paring are likewise enjoined in the vāra (weekday) and nakṣatra stated for cauḷa, [?] excluding the days of Mars and the Sun, the ninth day [from a previous shaving], the twilight, a riktā tithi (lunar day — the 4th, 9th, 14th), a parva day and the night; and one who is bent on [?] — retirement from the world, on battle, or on travel to another village, having bathed, anointed himself and eaten [is exempt]. It is not to be done again by those seeking their own welfare.

[ṭīkā] Ordinary shaving, and attention to the teeth, hair and nails, are also to be done in the nakṣatra, vāra and so forth prescribed for cauḷa. They are not to be done on Tuesday or Sunday, on the ninth day counted from a previous shaving, at twilight, on a riktā tithi, on a parva day, or at night. And when one is bent upon renunciation, upon battle, or upon a journey to another village, having bathed, performed the daily and occasional rites, applied oil and unguent, eaten, and put on ornaments, dress and adornment, one's own guru [?] [— the ṭīkā breaks off here in the scan].
ocr_review_note: Three uncertainties. (1) Verse 34, opening of pāda 2: the first compound member (2-3 akṣaras) is unrecoverable; the sense 'excluding the days of Mars and the Sun (कुजार्कान् विहाय)' is fixed by the ṭīkā but the exact reading is not. (2) Verse 34, pāda 4: the word between 'कृताशनेन' and 'पुनः' is corrupt; the syntactic link to the final clause is therefore uncertain. (3) The ṭīkā of verse 34 is truncated mid-word in the scan at 'अपने गुरु' — the remainder of the sentence, and any verse-closing marker, are lost at the page break.

(७०)    मुहूर्तचिन्तामणि    [ संस्कार- ]

व्रतबन्धमें शुभ ग्रह ८।६।१२ स्थानोंमें अशुभ, अन्योंमें शुभ; तथा ३।६।११ स्थानोंमें पापग्रह शुभ; और वृष २ कर्क ४ राशियोंका चन्द्रमा यदि पूर्ण हो तो लग्नमें शुभ होता है ॥ ४२ ॥ (अनु०)

वर्णाधीशाः शाखेशाश्च
विप्राधीशौ भार्गवेज्यौ भूजार्कौ राजन्यानामोषधीशो विशाम् ।
शूद्राणां ज्ञश्चान्त्यजानां शनिः स्याच्छाखेशाः स्युर्जीवशुक्रारसौम्याः ॥ ४३ ॥
ब्राह्मणोंके स्वामी शुक्र, बृहस्पति; क्षत्रियोंके मंगल, सूर्य; वैश्योंका चन्द्रमा; शूद्रोंका बुध; चांडालोंका शनि स्वामी है । तथा ऋग्वेदका बृहस्पति, यजुर्वेदका शुक्र, सामवेदका मंगल, अथर्वका बुध शाखेश हैं ॥ ४३ ॥ (शालिनी०)

शाखेशवारतनुवीर्यमतीव शस्तं शाखेशसूर्यशशिजीवबलैर्व्रतं सत् ।
जीवे भृगौ रिपुगृहे विजिते च नीचे स्याद्वेदशास्त्रविधिना रहितो व्रती[?] ॥ ४४ ॥
व्रतबन्धमें शाखेश (वेदेश) का वार तथा लग्न और (गोचरोक्त) बल भी अति उत्तम होता है; तथा शाखेश, सूर्य, चन्द्रमा, बृहस्पतिका बल व्रतबन्धमें मुख्य है, इनके शुभ होनेमें शुभ, अशुभ होनेमें अशुभ होता है । यदि बृहस्पति शुक्र शत्रुराशि नीच राशिमें हों तथा (विजित) ग्रहयुद्धमें पराजित हों तो व्रतबन्धवाला वेद, शास्त्र और नित्य नैमित्तिक श्रौत स्मार्त कर्मोंसे भी रहित होवे । उपलक्षणसे इनके नीचांशकादिकोंका भी यही फल है ॥ ४४ ॥ (वसं०)

जन्मक्षमासलग्नादौ व्रते विद्याधिको व्रती ।
आद्यगर्भेऽपि विप्राणां क्षत्रादीनामनादिमे ॥ ४५ ॥
व्रतबन्धमें जन्मनक्षत्र, जन्ममास, जन्मलग्नादिकोंका दोष ब्राह्मणके आद्यगर्भ तथा द्वितीयादि गर्भको, और क्षत्रिय वैश्यके द्वितीयादि गर्भको नहीं है; केवल क्षत्रियादिकोंको आद्यगर्भमात्रको दोष है, द्वितीयादिकोंको किसीको भी दोष नहीं ॥ ४५ ॥ (अनु०)

गुरुबलविचारः
बटुकन्या जन्मराशेस्त्रिकोणायद्विसप्तगः ।
श्रेष्ठो गुरुः खषट्त्र्यङ्गे[?] पूजयान्यत्र निन्दितः ॥ ४६ ॥
content_en:
[Page header] (70) Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi [Saṃskāra-]

[ṭīkā — continuing verse 42, whose root text stands at the end of the preceding chunk] In vratabandha (upanayana, investiture with the sacred thread) the benefic grahas (planets) are inauspicious in the 8th, 6th and 12th houses and auspicious in the rest; the pāpa-grahas (malefics) are auspicious in the 3rd, 6th and 11th; and a full Moon in Taurus (2) or Cancer (4) is auspicious in the lagna (ascendant). (42) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE LORDS OF THE VARṆAS AND THE LORDS OF THE VEDIC ŚĀKHĀS

(43) Venus and Jupiter are the lords of the brāhmaṇas; Mars and the Sun of the kṣatriyas; the lord of the herbs (the Moon) of the vaiśyas; Mercury of the śūdras; and Saturn is of the outcastes. The śākheśas (lords of the Vedic recensions) are Jupiter, Venus, Mars and Mercury.

[ṭīkā] Venus and Jupiter are the lords of brāhmaṇas; Mars and the Sun of kṣatriyas; the Moon of vaiśyas; Mercury of śūdras; Saturn is lord of the caṇḍālas. And Jupiter is the śākheśa of the Ṛgveda, Venus of the Yajurveda, Mars of the Sāmaveda, Mercury of the Atharva. (43) (Śālinī metre)

(44) The vāra (weekday) of the śākheśa, and its strength in the lagna, are exceedingly commended; the rite is good when it has the strength of the śākheśa, the Sun, the Moon and Jupiter. But if Jupiter and Venus are in an enemy's house or in debilitation, or are defeated (vijita) [in graha-yuddha, planetary war], the initiate will be devoid of Veda, śāstra and prescribed observance.[?]

[ṭīkā] In vratabandha the vāra of the śākheśa (the lord of one's Vedic recension), and likewise the lagna and its (transit-reckoned) strength, are most excellent. The strength of the śākheśa, the Sun, the Moon and Jupiter is the principal consideration in vratabandha: when these are auspicious the result is auspicious, when inauspicious, inauspicious. If Jupiter and Venus stand in an enemy sign or a sign of debilitation, or are defeated in graha-yuddha (planetary war), then the initiate will be destitute of the Veda, of śāstra, and even of the daily and occasional śrauta and smārta rites. By extension the same result follows from their standing in debilitation navāṃśas and the like. (44) (Vasantatilakā)

(45) [Even] at the janma-nakṣatra, the janma-māsa, the janma-lagna and so on, in the vrata (initiation) the initiate becomes richer in learning — for brāhmaṇas even in the case of a first-conceived child, and for kṣatriyas and the rest in the case of a child not first-conceived.

[ṭīkā] In vratabandha, the doṣa of the janma-nakṣatra, the janma-māsa, the janma-lagna and the rest does not apply to a brāhmaṇa's first-conceived child nor to his second and later children, nor to the second and later children of a kṣatriya or a vaiśya. The doṣa applies only to the first-conceived child of kṣatriyas and the rest; for second and later children there is no doṣa for anyone at all. (45) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE EXAMINATION OF GURU-BALA (THE STRENGTH OF JUPITER)

(46) For a boy [at initiation] and for a girl [at marriage], Jupiter is best when he stands in a trikoṇa (5th, 9th), the 11th, the 2nd or the 7th from the janma-rāśi (natal Moon-sign); in the 10th, 6th, 3rd and the lagna[?] he is acceptable by means of worship; elsewhere he is condemned.
ocr_review_note: Two uncertainties. (1) Verse 44, final word: the closing word is corrupt; 'रहितो व्रती' (the initiate becomes devoid of…) is read from the ṭīkā's gloss, but 'रहितो व्रतेन' is metrically possible and would shift the sense to 'devoid of [the fruit of] the vrata'. (2) Verse 46, pāda 3: the compound naming the second class of houses is corrupt. It is restored as 'खषट्त्र्यङ्गे' (10th, 6th, 3rd, 1st) on the strength of the ṭīkā's house-list (chunk pg0082_c02 reads '१०।६।३।१[९]') and the standard guru-bala rule, but the exact akṣaras are not legible.

cleaned_devanagari_text: बालकके व्रतबन्धमें, कन्याके विवाहमें जन्मराशिसे ५।९।११।२।७ स्थानोंमें गोचरसे बृहस्पति श्रेष्ठ होता है; १०।६।३।१ में [?]; ४।८।१२ में निन्दित है ॥ ४६ ॥ (अनु०) १ में (पूजा) शान्ति करके लेना ।
content_en: [ṭīkā — this chunk carries only the commentary on verse 46, whose root text stands at the end of the preceding chunk] For a boy's vratabandha (upanayana, investiture with the sacred thread) and for a girl's vivāha (marriage), Jupiter by gochara (transit) is best in the 5th, 9th, 11th, 2nd and 7th from the janma-rāśi (natal Moon-sign); in the 10th, 6th, 3rd and 1st he is [?]; in the 4th, 8th and 12th he is condemned. (46) (Anuṣṭubh) In the 1st, it is to be accepted only after performing (pūjā) śānti — the propitiatory rite that serves as the parihāra (remedy/cancellation) for that position.
ocr_review_note: One uncertainty. The predicate governing the second house-group is lost. The house list itself is restorable ('१९' is a scan artefact for '१', giving 10-6-3-1, which agrees with verse 46's mūla and with the closing line about pūjā-śānti in the 1st), but the two or three words stating what Jupiter's status is in those houses — presumably 'acceptable after worship' — are illegible.

प्रकरणम् ५ ]    हिन्दी टीका सहित    (७१)

स्वोच्चे स्वभे स्वमित्रे वा स्वांशे वर्गोत्तमे गुरुः ।
रिःफाष्टतुर्यगोऽपीष्टो नीचारिस्थः शुभोऽप्यसत् ॥ ४७ ॥
बृहस्पति अपने उच्च ४, स्वभवन ९।१२, स्वमित्र १।८, स्वांश ९।१२ के और वर्गोत्तमांशमें अथवा उक्त उच्चादि अंशकोंमें हो तो गोचरसे ४।८।१२ में भी हो तो भी दोष नहीं; और नीच १० और शत्रुराशि नवांशकोंमें हो तो गोचरका शुभ भी अशुभ होता है ॥ ४७ ॥

व्रतबन्धे वर्ज्यानि
कृष्णप्रदोषेऽनध्याये शनौ निश्यपराह्णके ।
प्राक्संध्यागर्जिते नेष्टो व्रतबन्धो गलग्रहे ॥ ४८ ॥
कृष्णपक्ष (प्रथम त्रिभाग) प्रतिपदासे पंचमीपर्यन्त छोडके व्रतबन्धमें आरोग्य है; शुक्ल द्वितीयासे समस्त शुक्लपक्ष तथा कृष्णपंचमीपर्यन्त उक्त है । और जिस दिन प्रदोष हो, अनध्याय, शनिवार, रात्रिमें, (अपरा) दिनके पिछले त्रिभागमें, (प्राक्संध्या) पूर्वोक्त लक्षणसे पहिली सन्ध्याके मेघगर्जनमें, तथा (गलग्रह) ४।७।८।९।१२।१४।१५।१ तिथियोंमें व्रतबन्ध न करना ॥ ४८ ॥ (अनु०)

तत्र रव्याद्यंशफलम्
क्रूरो जडो भवेत्पापः पटुः षट्कर्मकृद्वटुः ।
यज्ञार्थभाक्तथा मूर्खो रव्यादेस्तनौ क्रमात् ॥ ४९ ॥
व्रतबन्धके लग्नमें सूर्यका नवांश हो तो बटु क्रूर, [चन्द्रमाके अंशमें ?], मंगलके पापी, बुधके चतुर, बृहस्पतिके (षट्कर्मा) यजन-याजन-दान-प्रतिग्रह-अध्ययन-अध्यापन करनेवाला, शुक्रके अंशमें यज्ञ [? ]वाला, तथा शनिके अंशमें मूर्ख होवे ॥ ४९ ॥ (अनु०)

[?] ... विद्यानिरतः ... चन्द्रे स्वांशे बहु... ॥ ५० ॥
व्रतबन्धमें चन्द्रमा शुभराशिके अंशक ... [?] ... करता है ॥ ५० ॥ (मौक्तिक?)
परन्तु श्रवण एवं पुनर्वसु नक्षत्रमें स्वांशक ... धनवान् ...

(47) When Jupiter is in his own exaltation, in his own sign, in a friend's sign, in his own navāṃśa, or in vargottama, he is desirable even when transiting the 12th, 8th or 4th; but standing in debilitation or in an enemy's sign, even his auspicious [transit] is not good.

[ṭīkā] If Jupiter is in his exaltation (4, Cancer), in his own houses (9, 12), in the houses of his friends (1, 8), in his own navāṃśas (9, 12), or in a vargottama navāṃśa — or in the exaltation navāṃśas and the rest just named — then there is no doṣa (affliction) even when he stands in the 4th, 8th or 12th by gochara (transit). And if he is in debilitation (10, Capricorn) or in the navāṃśas of an enemy's sign, then even an auspicious transit position becomes inauspicious. (47)

WHAT IS TO BE AVOIDED IN VRATABANDHA

(48) Vratabandha (upanayana) is not desirable in the dark fortnight's pradoṣa, on an anadhyāya (a day when Vedic study is suspended), on Saturday, at night, in the last part of the day, when there is thunder at the preceding twilight, or in a galagraha [tithi].

[ṭīkā] Excluding the first third of the kṛṣṇa-pakṣa (dark fortnight) from pratipadā to pañcamī, vratabandha is wholesome; it is prescribed from the śukla dvitīyā through the whole bright fortnight and up to the dark fifth. And it is not to be performed on a day on which pradoṣa falls, on an anadhyāya, on Saturday, at night, in the last third of the day (aparā), when there is thunder at the preceding twilight (prāk-sandhyā) as defined above, or on the galagraha tithis — the 4th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 12th, 14th, 15th and 1st. (48) (Anuṣṭubh)

THEREIN, THE RESULT OF THE NAVĀṂŚAS OF THE SUN AND THE REST

(49) The boy becomes, respectively, cruel, dull, sinful, clever, a performer of the six duties, one devoted to the purposes of sacrifice, and a fool — according as the navāṃśa in the lagna belongs to the Sun and the rest [in order].

[ṭīkā] If the navāṃśa in the lagna of the vratabandha belongs to the Sun, the boy is cruel; [in the Moon's navāṃśa, ?]; in Mars's, sinful; in Mercury's, clever; in Jupiter's, a performer of the ṣaṭkarma (the six brahminical duties — sacrificing for oneself and for others, giving, receiving, studying and teaching); in Venus's navāṃśa, one who [?] sacrifice; and in Saturn's navāṃśa, a fool. (49) (Anuṣṭubh)

(50) [?] ... devoted to learning ... when the Moon is in its own navāṃśa, much ... [The root text of this verse is largely lost in the scan and is not rendered.]

[ṭīkā] In vratabandha, when the Moon is in the navāṃśa of an auspicious sign ... [?] ... it produces [that result]. (50) — but in the nakṣatras Śravaṇa and Punarvasu, in its own navāṃśa, [the boy becomes] wealthy ...
ocr_review_note: Four uncertainties, all in the second half of the page; the first half (verses 47 and 48, which carry the doṣa-cancellation content) is sound. (1) Verse 49 ṭīkā: the Moon's result is lost — 4-5 akṣaras destroyed between the Sun's and Mars's results. (2) Verse 49 ṭīkā: Venus's result survives only fragmentarily — the participle is illegible, so 'one who performs/causes sacrifice' is inferred from the mūla's 'यज्ञार्थभाक्' rather than read. (3) Verse 50 mūla: only disconnected fragments survive amid scanner noise; the pādas cannot be reconstructed and the verse is left unrendered. (4) Verse 50 ṭīkā: reduced to isolated words; the protasis and apodosis are both lost, as is the metre-name in parentheses.

बह्वृचां ब्रह्मौदनप्रकारः
प्राग्ब्रह्मौदनपाकाद् व्रतबन्धानन्तरं यदि चेत् ।
उत्पातानध्ययनोत्पत्तावपि शान्तिपूर्वकं तत्स्यात् ॥ ५६ ॥
व्रतबन्धके दिन बह्वृचोंका ब्रह्मौदनसंस्कार होता है । व्रतबन्धसे ऊपर ब्रह्मौदनसे पूर्व यदि मेघगर्जन, भूकम्प, उल्का, दिग्दाहादि उत्पात, अनध्याय हो तो शास्त्रोक्त शान्ति करनी । बह्वृचोंसे अन्योंका उपनयनांग ब्राह्मणभोजन तथा वेदारंभांग ब्राह्मणभोजनपर्यन्त मानते हैं । (शान्ति) स्वस्तिवाचन, पायसहोम, गायत्री तथा बृहस्पतिसूक्त जप, गोदान, ब्राह्मणभोजन है ॥ ५६ ॥ (आर्या)

वेदक्रमाच्छ[?]शिवादिकरत्रिमूलपूर्वासु पौष्णकरमृगा द्वितीज्ये ।
भवेषु चाश्विवसुपुष्यकरोत्तरेशकर्णे मृगान्त्यलघुभैर्जधनादित... सत् ॥ ५७ ॥
वेदक्रमसे व्रतबन्ध नक्षत्र — मृगशिर, आर्द्रा, आश्लेषा, हस्त, चित्रा, स्वाती, मूल, तीनों पूर्वा ऋग्वेदियोंको; रेवती, हस्त, अनुराधा, मृगशिरः, पुनर्वसु, पुष्य यजुर्वेदियोंको; अश्विनी, धनिष्ठा, पुष्य, हस्त, उत्तरा, आर्द्रा, श्रवण सामवेदियोंको; मृगशिरः, पुष्य, अश्विनी, हस्त, अनुराधा, पुनर्वसु अथर्ववेदियोंको उपनयनमें विहित हैं ॥ ५७ ॥ (व° ति°)

[?— 'वेदपरत्व नक्षत्र' चक्र: तालिकाकी कोष्ठ-सामग्री अपाठ्य]

नान्दीश्राद्धोत्तरं मातुः पुष्पे लग्नान्तरे [?] नहि ।
शान्त्या चौलं व्रतं [?] कार्योऽन्यथा ... ॥ ५८ ॥

[Page header] Chapter 5 — [with the Hindī ṭīkā] — (73)

THE PROCEDURE OF THE BRAHMAUDANA FOR FOLLOWERS OF THE ṚGVEDA

(56) If, after the vratabandha (upanayana) but before the cooking of the brahmaudana, an utpāta (portent) or an anadhyāya (a day on which Vedic study is suspended) should arise, then that [rite] is still to be performed, preceded by śānti (a propitiatory remedial rite).

[ṭīkā] On the day of the vratabandha the brahmaudana-saṃskāra of the Bahvṛcas (followers of the Ṛgveda) is performed. If, after the vratabandha and before the brahmaudana, there occurs an utpāta — thunder, earthquake, a meteor, a conflagration of the quarters and the like — or an anadhyāya, then the śānti prescribed in the śāstra is to be performed. For those other than the Bahvṛcas, [the corresponding limit] is held to extend to the feeding of brāhmaṇas that forms a limb of the upanayana and to the feeding of brāhmaṇas that forms a limb of the commencement of Vedic study. The (śānti) consists of svastivācana, the pāyasa-homa (oblation of milk-rice), japa of the Gāyatrī and of the Bṛhaspati-sūkta, the gift of a cow, and the feeding of brāhmaṇas. (56) (Āryā metre)

(57) [The nakṣatras for upanayana, given] in the order of the Vedas: [Ārdrā?], Āśleṣā, Hasta, Citrā, [Svātī], Mūla and the Pūrvās [for the first]; Revatī, Hasta and Mṛgaśiras with Jupiter's [asterisms] for the second; and Aśvinī, Dhaniṣṭhā, Puṣya, Hasta, the Uttarās ... Mṛgaśiras, Revatī and the laghu asterisms ... are good.[?]

[ṭīkā] The vratabandha nakṣatras, in the order of the Vedas: for followers of the Ṛgveda — Mṛgaśiras, Ārdrā, Āśleṣā, Hasta, Citrā, Svātī, Mūla and the three Pūrvās; for followers of the Yajurveda — Revatī, Hasta, Anurādhā, Mṛgaśiras, Punarvasu and Puṣya; for followers of the Sāmaveda — Aśvinī, Dhaniṣṭhā, Puṣya, Hasta, Uttarā, Ārdrā and Śravaṇa; for followers of the Atharvaveda — Mṛgaśiras, Puṣya, Aśvinī, Hasta, Anurādhā and Punarvasu. These are enjoined for the upanayana. (57) (Vivāha-tilaka?)

[?— a tabular chart headed 'the nakṣatras according to one's Veda' follows here; the cells are illegible in the scan and are not rendered]

(58) After the nāndī-śrāddha, if the mother comes into her flowers (i.e. begins to menstruate), [the rite is] not [to be done except] in another lagna; [otherwise] the cauḷa, the vrata [and the marriage] are to be performed by means of śānti [in the lagna already fixed].[?]

[The ṭīkā on verse 58 continues in the following chunk.]
ocr_review_note: Four uncertainties. (1) Verse 57 mūla: the compound listing the Ṛgveda nakṣatras is corrupt from the outset and the concluding pāda is unrecoverable; the nakṣatra lists in the translation are taken from the ṭīkā, which is legible, not from the verse. (2) The 'vedaparatva nakṣatra' chart between verses 57 and 58 survives only as scattered akṣaras and column rules; no cell can be read. (3) Verse 58 pāda 2: the governing word between them (presumably 'कार्यम्') is lost. (4) Verse 58 pāda 3: the third item in the list (which the ṭīkā gives as vivāha) and the end of the verse are destroyed at the page break.

(७४)    मुहूर्तचिन्तामणि    [ संस्कारप्रकर० ५ ]

नान्दीश्राद्धसे ऊपर यदि कार्यवालेकी माता रजस्वला हो जाय तो चूडा, व्रतबन्ध, विवाह अन्य लग्नमें करना । यदि और लग्न न मिले तो शान्ति करके निश्चित लग्नमें करना । (शान्ति) सुवर्णप्रतिमामें लक्ष्मीका पूजन, श्रीसूक्तपाठ, प्रत्यृचा पायसहोम और अभिषेक करना ॥ ५८ ॥ (अनु०)

छरिकाबन्धनमुहूर्तः
विचैत्रव्रतमासादौ विभौमास्ते विभौमदिने ।
छरिकाबन्धनं शस्तं नृपाणां प्राग्विवाहतः ॥ ५९ ॥
क्षत्रियोंका व्रतबन्धसे ऊपर विवाहके भीतर छरिकाबन्धन करते हैं । यह चैत्र छोडकर व्रतबन्धोक्त मासादिमें होता है, परन्तु इतना विशेष है कि मंगल अस्त न हो तथा मंगलवार न हो । यह तलवार बाँधनेका मुहूर्त है ॥ ५९ ॥ (अनु०)

केशान्तसमावर्तनमुहूर्तः
केशान्तं षोडशे वर्षे चौलोक्तदिवसे शुभम् ।
व्रतोक्तदिवसादौ हि समावर्तनमिष्यते ॥ ६० ॥
इति श्रीरामदैवज्ञविरचिते मुहूर्तचिन्तामणौ पञ्चमं संस्कारप्रकरणम् ॥ ५ ॥

ब्राह्मणका १६, क्षत्रिय वैश्यका २२ वर्षमें चूडाकर्मोक्त मुहूर्तमें केशान्त कर्म करना । १३[?] वर्षमें महानाम्नी व्रत, १४ में महाव्रत, १५ में उपनिषद्व्रत, १६ में केशान्त तथा गोदान व्रतसंस्कार होते हैं; इन सभीमें चौलोक्त मुहूर्त हैं । और वह तथा विद्या पढके गोदानान्त संस्कार करके व्रतबन्धादि उक्त मुहूर्तमें समावर्तन संस्कार करना ॥ ६० ॥

इति श्रीदैवज्ञानन्तसुतरामविरचिते मुहूर्तचिन्तामणौ महीधरकृतायां माहीधर्य्यां भाषाटीकायां पञ्चमं संस्कारप्रकरणम् ॥ ५ ॥

[Page header] (74) Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi [Saṃskāra chapter 5]

[ṭīkā — completing verse 58, whose root text stands at the end of the preceding chunk] If, after the nāndī-śrāddha, the mother of the person for whom the rite is being done becomes rajasvalā (menstruant), then the cūḍā (tonsure), the vratabandha (investiture with the sacred thread) and the vivāha (marriage) are to be performed in a different lagna (ascendant). If no other lagna is obtainable, then it is to be performed in the lagna already fixed, after doing śānti (the propitiatory remedial rite). The (śānti) consists of worship of Lakṣmī in a golden image, recitation of the Śrī-sūkta, a pāyasa-homa with an oblation to each ṛc, and abhiṣeka (ceremonial bathing of the image). (58) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE MUHŪRTA FOR THE BINDING ON OF THE SWORD (CHARIKĀ-BANDHANA)

(59) Excluding Caitra, in the months and so forth [prescribed] for the vrata, when Mars is not combust and not on Mars's day, the binding on of the sword is commended for kings, before the marriage.

[ṭīkā] Kṣatriyas perform the charikā-bandhana after the vratabandha and before the marriage. It is done in the months and so forth prescribed for vratabandha, excluding Caitra; but with this particular qualification, that Mars must not be combust and it must not be a Tuesday. This is the muhūrta for girding on the sword. (59) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE MUHŪRTAS FOR KEŚĀNTA AND SAMĀVARTANA

(60) Keśānta (the first ritual shaving of the beard) in the sixteenth year, on a day prescribed for cauḷa, is auspicious; and samāvartana (the returning home at the close of studentship) is desired on the days and so forth prescribed for the vrata.

Thus ends the fifth chapter, on the saṃskāras, in the Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi composed by Śrī Rāma Daivajña. (5)

[ṭīkā] For a brāhmaṇa the keśānta rite is performed in the 16th year, for a kṣatriya and a vaiśya in the 22nd, in the muhūrta prescribed for the cūḍākarma. In the 13th[?] year comes the mahānāmnī vrata, in the 14th the mahāvrata, in the 15th the upaniṣad-vrata, and in the 16th the keśānta together with the godāna-vrata saṃskāra; for all of these the muhūrtas prescribed for cauḷa apply. And after that, having completed one's study and performed the saṃskāras up to the godāna, the samāvartana saṃskāra is to be performed in the muhūrta stated for the vratabandha and the rest. (60)

Thus ends the fifth chapter, on the saṃskāras, in the Māhīdharī vernacular ṭīkā composed by Mahīdhara upon the Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi of Rāma, son of Śrī Daivajña Ananta. (5)

It is read as १३ (thirteenth year) because the following items run 14 (mahāvrata), 15 (upaniṣad-vrata), 16 (keśānta and godāna), but the digit itself is not legible and could be another value.

कन्यका वा सुतो वा तदा पण्डितैस्तादृशापत्यमस्या विनिर्दिश्यते ॥ ८ ॥
प्रश्नसमयमें ज्योतिषीके समीप जैसी स्त्री आवे वैसा उत्तर प्रश्नका कहना; जैसे कोई स्त्री पुत्र लेके आवे तो विवाहवाली कन्याके पुत्र होंगे, कन्या लेके आवे तो कन्या होगी, दोनों हों तो कन्या पुत्र सभी होंगे । उपलक्षणसे उस स्त्रीके जैसे लक्षण — सुभगा, दुर्भगा, पुत्रवती, बाँझ आदि — हों वैसे ही कन्याके कहना ॥ ८ ॥ (सम्वि०)

(6) If, in a fortnight other than the bright one, the Moon stands in an even sign counted from the lagna (ascendant) of the praśna (horary query), in the 6th or the 8th house, and is aspected by an inauspicious graha (planet) — then this becomes a destroyer of the marriage.

[ṭīkā] If the Moon of the dark fortnight, in an even sign (2nd, 4th and so on) from the praśna-lagna, stands in the 6th or 8th house and is aspected by a malefic, then (there is destruction of the marriage) that marriage will not come about. (6) (Puṣpitāgrā)

THE PARIHĀRA (REMEDY) FOR THE YOGA OF EARLY WIDOWHOOD

(7) Having examined the natal chart and seen a bāla-vaidhavya-yoga (a combination indicating widowhood in girlhood), one should have her perform, [?] in private, the vrata of Sāvitrī or indeed that of the pippala (holy fig); or else, having openly performed a marriage in an auspicious lagna with an image of Acyuta (Viṣṇu), with a pippala tree, or with a water-jar, one should then give her to a long-lived bridegroom. In this way no doṣa (affliction) arises, nor the blemish of being a punarbhū (a woman twice given in marriage).

[ṭīkā] If in a girl's nativity the yogas that cause early widowhood, as declared in the jātaka texts and elsewhere, are seen, then her father and other elders should (rahaḥ) in private and with due resolve have her perform the Sāvitrī-vrata and the vrata connected with the pippala; or else, in an auspicious lagna and in the yogas declared for marriage that produce good qualities and saubhāgya (marital good fortune), a marriage should be performed by the marriage rite with an image of Viṣṇu, with an aśvattha tree, or with a water-jar, and this girl should then be given to a long-lived bridegroom (one who has a yoga of long life). By performing this upāya (remedial measure) the doṣa of widowhood does not take effect, and neither does the doṣa (punarbhū) of having been married to two bridegrooms. (7) (Śārdūlavikrīḍita)

THE PRAŚNA CONCERNING SONS AND DAUGHTERS

(8) If at the moment of the praśna-lagna a woman comes in of her own accord accompanied by a child of a particular sort — a daughter or a son — then the learned declare that the offspring of this [bride] will be of that same sort.

[ṭīkā] At the time of the praśna, the answer to the question is to be given according to the sort of woman who approaches the astrologer: if some woman comes bringing a son, the girl to be married will have sons; if she brings a daughter, a daughter will be born; if both, then both daughters and sons. By extension, whatever the characteristics of that woman — fortunate, unfortunate, mother of sons, barren, and so on — the same are to be declared of the bride. (8) (Saṃvidhāna?)

(9) By the sounds of the conch, the kettledrum and the lute, an auspicious result comes about; [by the contrary, ?] one should mark the contrary. But if a crow, an ass, a dog or a jackal cries out [?] at the moment of the praśna-lagna, [it is inauspicious].

A girl born in the first three pādas (quarters) of the nakṣatra (lunar mansion) Viśākhā is a giver of happiness to the devara (husband's younger brother). Those born in the last pāda of Mūla and in the first pāda of Sarpa (Āśleṣā) are auspicious for those two [the father-in-law and the mother-in-law spoken of in the preceding verse]. || 20 ||

[ṭīkā] A girl born in the first three quarters of Viśākhā [is a bringer of happiness] to the devara; only the fourth quarter is forbidden. In just the same way, of Mūla … [the chunk breaks off here, mid-sentence]

(84) Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi [Vivāha section]

[ṭīkā, continued from verse 31] The sixth rāśi (zodiacal sign) from an odd sign, and likewise the eighth from an even sign, comes to the same thing: this is the śatru-ṣaḍaṣṭaka (hostile six-eight relation), whose lords are enemies. And the sixth from an even sign and the eighth from an odd one form the mitra-ṣaḍaṣṭaka (friendly six-eight), whose lords are friends; this is auspicious, and the reverse of it inauspicious. The śatru-ṣaḍaṣṭaka brings death. If the signs of groom and bride stand 5–9 to one another there is loss of sons; if 2–12, poverty. In the remaining positions they are auspicious. || 31 || (metre: Anuṣṭubh) [This verse is an interpolation.]

The parihāra (cancellation) of an evil bhakūṭa
Even in an evil bhakūṭa, marriage is commended[?] when there is ekādhipatya (one and the same planet lording both signs); it is likewise declared auspicious when the two rāśi-lords are mutually friendly, provided there is nāḍī-śuddhi and nakṣatra-śuddhi; and again when the lords of the aṃśas (divisional-chart divisions) of those signs are mutually friendly and strong, together with nāḍī- and nakṣatra-śuddhi, and by force of tārā-śuddhi, and when rāśi-vaśyatā obtains — so the wise have declared. || 32 ||

[ṭīkā] Even in the evil bhakūṭa stated above there is a parihāra (cancellation), namely: if one and the same planet lords the signs of groom and bride — as Maṅgala (Mars) does for 1 and 8, and Śukra (Venus) for 2 and 7 — the marriage is auspicious. It is likewise auspicious when the rāśi-lords are friends, provided there is nāḍī-śuddhi (purity of nāḍī) and nakṣatra-śuddhi. And if the lords of the aṃśas of the said rāśi-lords are mutually friendly and are also strong, and there is nāḍī-śuddhi and tārā-śuddhi, and rāśi-vaśyatā too is fit, then the doṣa (affliction) of enmity between the planets does not arise. Here we have: (1) graha-maitrī, i.e. the friendly ṣaḍaṣṭaka; (2) ekādhipatya; (3) friendship of strong aṃśa-lords; (4) rāśi-vaśyatā; (5) tārā-śuddhi — five kinds of parihāra for the ṣaḍaṣṭaka. Even one of these being present, the ṣaḍaṣṭaka-doṣa does not stand; but nāḍī-[śuddhi] must be present in every case. || 32 || (metre: Śārdūlavikrīḍita)

When there is friendship between the two rāśi-lords, and also between the pair[?] of aṃśa-lords, there is no doṣa of the gaṇas. A good bhakūṭa destroys the enmity of the planets, and friendship of the planets likewise [destroys] an evil bhakūṭa. || 33 ||

[ṭīkā] The parihāra of the gaṇa-kūṭa, the bhakūṭa and the graha-kūṭa: if there is mutual friendship between the bride's and the groom's signs and between the aṃśa-lords, then the doṣa of an evil gaṇa (rākṣasa with manuṣya, and so on) does not arise; and if there is an auspicious rāśi-kūṭa, the third … [the chunk breaks off here, mid-sentence]

Chapter 6] With the Hindi ṭīkā (85)

[Verse 34, concluded:] Vāyu's star (Svātī), Agni's star (Kṛttikā)[?], Ahi's star (Āśleṣā) and the Viśve-devas' star (Uttarāṣāḍhā), each taken with its pair, and also Pauṣṇa (Revatī) — that is the last (apara) nāḍī. Marriage of a couple falling within one and the same nāḍī is not good; falling in the middle nāḍī, it means the death of both. || 34 ||

[ṭīkā] Jyeṣṭhā, Ārdrā, Uttaraphālgunī and Śatabhiṣā — two nakṣatras (lunar mansions) each, counted from these — form the ādya (first) nāḍī. Puṣya, Mṛgaśira, Citrā, Anurādhā, Bharaṇī, Dhaniṣṭhā, Pūrvāṣāḍhā, Pūrvāphālgunī and Uttarabhādrapadā form the madhya (middle) nāḍī. Svātī, Kṛttikā, Āśleṣā and Uttarāṣāḍhā — two nakṣatras each, counted from these — form the antya (last) nāḍī. If the marriage of groom and bride falls within one and the same nāḍī the result is inauspicious; if it falls in the middle nāḍī, the death of both is certain. Setting aside the middle nāḍī, the doṣa (affliction) of the two flanking nāḍīs does not apply south of the Godāvarī, nor to Kṣatriyas and the like.

[ṭīkā, continued] Some hold that the ādya nāḍī afflicts the groom, the antya the bride, and the madhya both. Of these, some take the antya nāḍī as admitting a further parihāra (cancellation), citing: 'Four, three, [the mountains =] seven, [the moon =] one, [the Aśvins =] two, arising in order[?] … counted in order from Aśvinī's star. From Agni's star and from Indu's star the nāḍī is [reckoned] as three, four, five … [?] || 1 ||'. From other works they speak of the tri-, catur- and pañca-nāḍī: if all four pādas (quarters) of the bride's nakṣatra fall in one and the same rāśi (sign), then the tri-nāḍī stated above applies; if three pādas fall in one sign, the catur-nāḍī; with two pādas, the pañca-nāḍī is to be considered. The tri-nāḍī is counted from Aśvinī, the catur-nāḍī from Kṛttikā, the pañca-nāḍī from Mṛgaśira. But the catur-nāḍī is current in the Ahalyā[?] country, the pañca-nāḍī in the Panjab, and the tri-nāḍī everywhere. Some declare a special doṣa within a nāḍī for the first, the fourth, and the third-and-second pādas of a nakṣatra. Nāḍī is to be considered for groom and bride, for master and servant, for [?], for friends, for a country, and for a new country, village, town or house. Where the nakṣatra-nāḍī [defect] has arisen but the pāda-nāḍī [defect] has not, there the doṣa is slight. When the parihāras stated above and the like obtain, there is also a śānti (propitiatory rite) for the nāḍī, namely: japa of the Mṛtyuñjaya and other [mantras], the gift of a golden nāḍī, and — in the varṇa and the other kūṭas — the giving of a cow, grain, cloth and gold. || 34 || (metre: Sragdharā)

(88) Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi [Vivāha section]

[ṭīkā, on verse 35] Six nakṣatras (lunar mansions) counted from Revatī are termed the pūrva-bhāga; twelve nakṣatras from Ārdrā are termed the madhya-bhāga; the remaining nine constitute the apara-bhāga. In the pūrva-bhāga the husband is dear to the wife; in the madhya-bhāga there is mutual affection between wife and husband; and in the apara-bhāga the wife is dear to the husband. || 35 || (metre: Indravajrā)
[Chart — count: 6 | 12 | 9; result: husband-beloved | mutual affection | wife-beloved; designation: pūrva-bhāga | madhya-bhāga | para-bhāga]

The varga-kūṭa approved by the Easterners
The letter-classes beginning with a, ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa, ya and śa belong respectively to Garuḍa, the cat, the lion, the dog, the serpent, the mouse, the deer and the sheep — eight [classes], each hostile to the fifth from itself. || 36 ||

[ṭīkā] The a-class is Garuḍa, the ka-class the cat, the ca-class the lion, the ṭa-class the dog, the ta-class the serpent, the pa-class the mouse, the ya-class the deer, the śa-class (avi) the goat — these are the lords of the eight classes. The fifth from one's own is the enemy: thus Garuḍa–serpent, cat–mouse, lion–deer, dog–goat, serpent–Garuḍa. If the nakṣatras of wife and husband stand as eater and eaten, it is not auspicious. Some examine [the same] also from the initial syllable of the name — for groom and bride, for master and servant, and for all the rest. || 36 || (metre: Āryā)

The special rule when nakṣatra or rāśi is identical
[Verse 37; the first half is largely lost in the scan:] … the pair of rāśis[?] likewise. There is no doṣa (affliction) of nāḍī or of the gaṇas when the nakṣatra is the same[?] but the pādas (quarters) differ — it is auspicious. || 37 ||

[ṭīkā] If the groom and the bride have one and the same rāśi (sign) [but different nakṣatras], and if the nakṣatra is the same but the pāda differs — that is, it is not the very same pāda — then nāḍī-doṣa and gaṇa-doṣa, and by implication tārā and the other doṣas as well, do not arise. In worldly dealings, royal service, battle and friendship, the results are taken from the nāma-rāśi (the sign of the name). || 37 || (metre: Śārdūlavikrīḍita)

The special rule on the nakṣatras of master and servant
[Verse 38; the text is heavily corrupt:] The nakṣatra of the pupil, the debtor, the young wife, the town and so on …[?] … of the servant, the wealthy man, the husband, the town and so on … destruction of service, destruction[?] …, and the loss of the happiness of the village and the rest — this is declared in due order. || 38 ||

[ṭīkā] If, counted from the nakṣatra of the servant, the wealthy man, the husband, or the village, the nakṣatra of the master, the debtor, the wife, or the town falls earlier, then one should know that there follow, in that order: destruction of service, destruction of wealth, destruction of the husband, and destruction of the happiness connected with the village. || 38 ||

प्रकरणम् ६ ]  हिन्दी टीका सहित  (९१)

चन्द्रमाके सूर्यके साथ हो तो दरिद्रता, एवं मंगलके साथ मृत्यु, बुधके साथ शुभ, बृहस्पतिके साथ सौख्य, शुक्रके साथ (सापत्न्य) सौत, शनिके साथ (वैराग्य) फकीरी; राहु केतु भी ऐसे ही जानना। यदि चन्द्रमा दो पापग्रहोंसे युक्त हो तो मृत्यु होवे। परन्तु मित्र, स्वक्षेत्र, उच्च, वर्गोत्तमादिगत चन्द्रमा पापयुक्त दोष नहीं करता — यह ग्रन्थान्तरमत है ॥ ४५ ॥ (अनु०)

अष्टमलग्नदोषस्यापवादः
जन्मलग्नभयोर्मृत्युराशौ नेष्टः करग्रहः ।
एकाधिपत्ये राशीशे मैत्रे वा नैव दोषकृत् ॥ ४६ ॥

जन्मलग्न-जन्मराशिसे अष्टम लग्न विवाहादि शुभ कार्यमें शुभ नहीं होता, परन्तु एकाधिपत्य जैसे १।८ हो तथा राशीश मैत्री (जैसे ५।१२) हो तो लग्नाष्टक और राश्यष्टकका दोष नहीं होता ॥ ४६ ॥ (अनु०)

मीनोक्षकर्कट्यलि[?]मृगस्त्रियोऽष्टमं लग्नं यदा नाष्टमगेहदोषकृत् ।
अन्योन्यमैत्रीत्ववशेन सा वधूर्भवेत्सुतायुर्गृहसौख्यभागिनी ॥ ४७ ॥

यदि १२।२।४।८।१०।६ ये राशि जन्मलग्न-जन्मराशिसे अष्टम हों तो उक्त अष्टकदोष नहीं होता, क्योंकि इनके स्वामी परस्पर मित्र हैं; इससे इन राशियोंके अष्टम होनेमें वधू पुत्र, आयु और घरके सुखयुक्त होती है। मतान्तर है कि, जो अष्टमराशीश केन्द्रमें किंवा स्वोच्चादिमें हो तो अष्टमोक्त दोष नहीं होता है ॥ ४७ ॥ (उ० जा०)

मृतिभवनांशो यदि च लग्ने[?] तदधिपतिर्वा कलहकरः स्यात् ।
व्ययभवनं वा भवति तदंशस्तदधिपतिर्वा कलहकरः स्यात् ॥ ४८ ॥

उक्त अष्टमराशिका नवांश अथवा अष्टमेश लग्नमें हो तो शुभ नहीं; यदि जन्मलग्न-जन्मराशिसे व्ययराशि वा उसका अंश अथवा तदीश लग्नमें हो तो कलहकारक होता है, कोई धनहानिकारक कहते हैं ॥ ४८ ॥ (कुसुमविचित्रा)

विषघटीदोषः
खरामतोऽन्त्यादितिवह्निपित्र्यभे खवेदतःकेशवतश्च[?] सार्पभे ।
खबाणतोऽश्वधृतितोऽर्यमाम्बुप[?] … कृतेभे … अष्टभविश्वजीवमे ॥ ४९ ॥
content_en:
Chapter 6] With the Hindi ṭīkā (91)

[ṭīkā, continued from verse 45] If the Moon is with the Sun there is poverty; with Maṅgala (Mars), death; with Budha (Mercury), auspiciousness; with Bṛhaspati (Jupiter), happiness; with Śukra (Venus), sāpatnya (a rival co-wife); with Śani (Saturn), vairāgya (renunciation, a mendicant's lot). Rāhu and Ketu are to be understood in the same way. If the Moon is joined by two malefic planets, death follows. But a Moon placed in a friend's sign, in its own sign, in exaltation, in vargottama and the like does not produce the doṣa (affliction) even when joined to malefics — this is the view of other works. || 45 || (metre: Anuṣṭubh)

The exception (apavāda) to the doṣa of the eighth lagna
Marriage (karagraha, the taking of the hand) is undesirable in the sign eighth from the janma-lagna (natal ascendant) or the janma-nakṣatra; but when there is ekādhipatya (one planet lording both), or when the rāśi-lords are friendly, it causes no doṣa whatever. || 46 ||

[ṭīkā] A lagna eighth from the janma-lagna or the janma-rāśi is not auspicious for marriage and other auspicious acts; but with ekādhipatya — as with 1 and 8 — and with friendship of the rāśi-lords (as with 5 and 12), the doṣa of the eighth lagna and of the eighth rāśi does not arise. || 46 || (metre: Anuṣṭubh)

When Mīna, Vṛṣa, Karka, Vṛścika[?], Makara or Kanyā is the eighth lagna, it does not cause the doṣa of the eighth house; by force of their mutual friendship that bride becomes a sharer in sons, long life and household happiness. || 47 ||

[ṭīkā] If the signs 12, 2, 4, 8, 10 and 6 fall eighth from the janma-lagna or janma-rāśi, then the aṣṭaka-doṣa spoken of does not arise, because their lords are mutual friends; hence, when these signs fall eighth, the bride is endowed with sons, long life and household happiness. There is another view, that if the lord of the eighth sign is in a kendra (angle), or in its own exaltation and the like, the doṣa declared for the eighth does not arise. || 47 || (metre: Upajāti)

If the navāṃśa of the house of death (the eighth), or its lord, be in the lagna[?], it becomes a cause of strife; and if it be the twelfth house, or its aṃśa, or its lord, that too becomes a cause of strife. || 48 ||

[ṭīkā] If the navāṃśa of the said eighth sign, or the lord of the eighth, is in the lagna, it is not auspicious. If the twelfth sign from the janma-lagna or janma-rāśi, or its aṃśa, or its lord, is in the lagna, it becomes a cause of strife; some say it causes loss of wealth. || 48 || (metre: Kusumavicitrā)

The doṣa of the viṣa-ghaṭī (poison ghaṭikā)
[Verse 49, opening; the text is corrupt from the second pāda onward:] From the thirtieth [ghaṭī] in Pauṣṇa (Revatī), Aditi's star (Punarvasu), Agni's star (Kṛttikā) and the Pitṛs' star (Maghā); from the fortieth …, and from …[?] in Sarpa's star (Āśleṣā); from the fiftieth …, from …[?] in Aryaman's and Varuṇa's stars … || 49 || [the ṭīkā on this verse follows in the next chunk]
ocr_review_note: Four uncertain loci. (1) verse 47 pāda 1: OCR 'भीनोक्षककाटिमृगस्ियो' is missing one sign-name; restored as 'मीनोक्षकर्कट्यलिमृगस्त्रियः' because the ṭīkā fixes the set as 12, 2, 4, 8, 10, 6 (Mīna, Vṛṣa, Karka, Vṛścika, Makara, Kanyā), but the akṣaras for Vṛścika (अलि) are not legible. (2) verse 48 pāda 1: OCR 'विर्गे' read as 'लग्ने' on the authority of the ṭīkā ('अष्टमेश लग्नमें हो तो'); the scan does not support the reading directly. (3)–(4) verse 49 is a bhūta-saṅkhyā numeric-cipher verse and is corrupt at the end of pāda 1 and through pāda 3 ('खवेदतःकेरदतश्च', 'खबाणतोऽश्वधृतितोऽ्यमाम्बुप कृतेभेगत्वाष्टभविश्वजीवमे'); only the securely decodable opening (30 ghaṭīs for Revatī / Punarvasu / Kṛttikā / Maghā, confirmed by the pg0104 ṭīkā) has been rendered, and the remaining figures are left unresolved rather than reconstructed.

प्रकरणम् ६ ] हिन्दी टीका सहित (९७)

यहाँ दुबारा कहे हैं । प्रथम शुभाशुभ प्रकरणमें भी कह आये थे । वहाँ साधारण दोष गणना है, अन्य कार्योंमें फल इनका दोषद नहीं ॥ ६५ ॥ (अनु०)

[?] — (दिवा/रात्रि नक्षत्र-सारणी; स्कैन नष्ट, पाठ अनुद्धार्य)

दग्धतिथिदोषः
चापान्त्यगे गोघटगे पतङ्गे[?] कर्काजगे स्त्रीमिथुने स्थिते च ।
सिंहालिगे नक्रतुलागे[?] समाः स्युस्तिथयो द्वितीयाप्रमुखाश्च दग्धाः ॥ ६६ ॥
दग्धतिथि — धनु मीनके सूर्यमें द्वितीया २, वृष कुम्भमें ४, कर्क मेषमें ६, मिथुन कन्यामें ८, सिंह वृश्चिकमें १०, मकर तुलामें १२ दग्ध होती है । ये मासदग्ध तिथि मध्यदेशमें ही वर्जित हैं ॥ ६६ ॥ (इ० व०)

यामित्रदोषः
लग्नाच्चन्द्रान्मदनभवनगे खेटे न स्यादिह परिणयनम् ।
किंवा बाणाद्रिगमितलवगे[?] यामित्रं स्यादशुभकरमिदम् ॥ ६७ ॥
लग्न तथा चन्द्रमासे सप्तम ग्रह होनेमें यामित्र दोष होता है, विवाहादिकमें अशुभ फल करता है । किंवा लग्न वा चन्द्रस्थित नवांशमें ५५ अंशपर हो तो विशेष दोष है । जैसे तुला ५ भागपर लग्न वा चन्द्रमा है तो मेषके ५ अंश — ५५ हुए; इसमें जो ग्रह हो उसकी यामित्री हुई । यह सुषम यामित्री है । इसमें शुभग्रहोंकी यामित्रीका फल ग्रन्थान्तरोंमें शुभ भी है ॥ ६७ ॥ (भ्रमरविलसित[?]०)
content_en:
[Chapter 6 · with the Hindi ṭīkā · p. 97]

[ṭīkā] Here they are stated over again. In the first prakaraṇa, on the auspicious and the inauspicious, this was already said. There it is a general reckoning of doṣa (astrological affliction); in other undertakings the result of these is not doṣa-producing. (65) (metre: Anuṣṭubh)

[ṭīkā] [A tabular chart of divā (day) and rātri (night) nakṣatra assignments with numeric columns stands here. The scan of the table is destroyed and no reading can be recovered; it is not translated rather than guessed at.]

Dagdha-tithi-doṣa (the affliction of the "burnt" lunar day)
When [the Sun] stands in Cāpa (Dhanus) or the last sign (Mīna), in Go (Vṛṣa) or Ghaṭa (Kumbha), in Karka or Aja (Meṣa), in Strī (Kanyā) or Mithuna, in Siṃha or Ali (Vṛścika), in Nakra (Makara) or Tulā — the even tithis (lunar days) beginning with the second are dagdha (burnt). (66)

[ṭīkā] Dagdha-tithi: when the Sun is in Dhanus or Mīna the 2nd tithi; in Vṛṣa or Kumbha the 4th; in Karka or Meṣa the 6th; in Mithuna or Kanyā the 8th; in Siṃha or Vṛścika the 10th; in Makara or Tulā the 12th — these become burnt. These māsa-dagdha tithis are prohibited in Madhyadeśa alone [and not elsewhere]. (66) (metre: Indravajrā)

Yāmitra-doṣa
If a planet (kheṭa) occupies the madana-bhavana (7th house) reckoned from the lagna (ascendant) or from the Moon, marriage should not be performed here; or, if [a planet] is in the navāṃśa reached at [55] degrees, that is yāmitra, and this is a producer of inauspiciousness. (67)

[ṭīkā] When there is a planet in the 7th from the lagna or from the Moon, yāmitra doṣa arises; it produces inauspicious results in marriage and the like. Or, if [a planet] stands at 55 degrees within the navāṃśa occupied by the lagna or the Moon, there is a special doṣa — for example, if the lagna or the Moon is at 5 degrees of Tulā, then [reckoning] to 5 degrees of Meṣa makes 55; whatever planet is there, its yāmitrī has occurred. This is the suṣama (even) yāmitrī. In this, the yāmitrī of benefic planets is held auspicious in other works as well. (67)
ocr_review_note: Five uncertain points. (1) The divā/rātri nakṣatra table between v.65 and v.66 is scan-destroyed — column headers and digits are unrecoverable; left untranslated. (2) v.66 pāda 1 'पङ्के' — read as 'पतङ्गे' (= the Sun, subject of स्थिते), plausible but not certain. (3) v.66 pāda 3 'नक्थटे' — restored as 'नक्रतुलागे' on the authority of the ṭīkā's 'मकर तुलामें १२'; akṣaras not legible. (4) v.67 'बाणाद्यगमितलवगे' — the bhūta-saṅkhyā compound yielding the ṭīkā's 55 degrees cannot be resolved; restored provisionally as 'बाणाद्रिगमित-'. (5) metre siglum after v.67 ('भमरपिल०') is illegible; read tentatively as Bhramaravilasita.

(९८) मुहूर्तचिन्तामणि [विवाह-

एकार्गलादिदोषाणामपवादः
एकार्गलोपग्रहपातलत्तायामित्रकर्तर्युदयास्तदोषाः ।
नश्यन्ति चन्द्रार्कबलोपपन्ने लग्ने यथार्कोदये तु दोषाः ॥ ६८ ॥
एकार्गल (खार्जूर) तथा उपग्रह, पात, लत्ता, यामित्री, कर्तरी, उदयास्त (वक्ष्यमाण) — इतने दोष विवाहलग्नमें सूर्य चन्द्रमाके बलवान् होनेमें नष्ट हो जाते हैं; जैसे सूर्यके उदय होनेमें रात्रिका अन्धकार नष्ट होता है ॥ ६८ ॥ (इ० व०)

उपग्रहर्क्षं कुरुबाह्लिकेषु [?]वङ्गेषु च पातितं भम् ।
सौराष्ट्रशाल्वेषु च लत्तितं भं त्यजेत विद्धं किल सर्वदेशे ॥ ६९ ॥
कुरुदेश, बाह्लीकदेश (पश्चिममें है) में उपग्रहनक्षत्र त्याज्य है, अन्य देशोंमें नहीं । वंग (पूर्वमें), मागधादिकोंमें पातदोष (चण्डीश, चण्डायुध) त्याज्य है । सौराष्ट्र, शाल्व (पश्चिममें है) में लत्ता त्याज्य है, और वेध सर्वत्र त्याज्य है । कहीं युतिदोष गौडमें, यामित्री यामुन प्रदेशमें कहा है ॥ ६९ ॥ (उ० जा०)

शशाङ्कसूर्यर्क्ष[?]युतेऽवशेषे खं भूयुगाङ्गानि दशेशतिथ्यः ।
नागेन्दवोऽङ्केन्दुमिता नखाश्चेद् भवन्ति चैते दशयोगसंज्ञाः ॥ ७० ॥
सूर्य-चन्द्रमाकी नक्षत्रसंख्या जोड़के २७ से भाग लेना; शेष ०।१।४।६।१०।११।१५।१८।१९।२० में से कोई रहे तो दशयोग संज्ञा होती है ॥ ७० ॥ (उ० जा०)

दशदोषयोगानां फलं तदपवादश्च
वाताग्निमहीपचौरमरणरुग्विवादाः क्षतिर्योगाङ्के दलिते समे [?] ।
… संमिताः[?] … रेखाः क्रमात् … अस्मिन् महच्चन्द्रयोगे शुभदः स्यादेकरेखास्थयोः ॥ ७१ ॥
आधा … ५ जोड़े (मनु) करना, जैसे — विषमांक १५ एक जोड़के १६, आधा ८ …
content_en:
[p. 98 · Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi · Vivāha-]

The apavāda (annulling exception) of ekārgala and the other doṣas
The doṣas of ekārgala, upagraha, pāta, lattā, yāmitra, kartarī and udayāsta perish when the lagna is endowed with the strength of the Moon and the Sun — just as the doṣās (nights) perish at sunrise. (68)

[ṭīkā] Ekārgala (khārjūra), and upagraha, pāta, lattā, yāmitrī, kartarī, udayāsta (to be described below) — these doṣas are destroyed in the marriage lagna when the Sun and the Moon are strong; just as the darkness of night is destroyed when the Sun rises. (68)

The upagraha-nakṣatra [is to be shunned] in Kuru and Bāhlīka; the pāta-struck nakṣatra in [?] and Vaṅga; the lattā-struck nakṣatra in Saurāṣṭra and Śālva; but the vedha-struck one is indeed to be shunned in every country. (69)

[ṭīkā] In Kuru-deśa and Bāhlīka-deśa (which lies in the west) the upagraha-nakṣatra is to be rejected, not in other countries. In Vaṅga (in the east) and in Magadha and the rest the pāta doṣa (Caṇḍīśa, Caṇḍāyudha) is to be rejected. In Saurāṣṭra and Śālva (in the west) lattā is to be rejected; and vedha is to be rejected everywhere. In some [works] yuti-doṣa is assigned to Gauḍa, and yāmitrī to the Yāmuna country. (69)

When the nakṣatra-numbers of Moon and Sun are added [and divided], if the remainder is 0, 1, 4, 6, 10, 11, 15, 18, 19 or 20, these bear the name of the ten yogas (daśa-yoga). (70)

[ṭīkā] Add together the nakṣatra numbers of the Sun and the Moon and divide by 27; if the remainder is any of 0, 1, 4, 6, 10, 11, 15, 18, 19, 20, the designation daśa-yoga applies. (70)

The result of the ten doṣa-yogas, and their apavāda (exception)
Wind, fire, [injury from] the king, thieves, death, disease, quarrel and loss [result] when the yoga-number, being halved, is even … [the middle of the verse — the reckoning of the "lines" (rekhā) — is not recoverable from the scan and is left untranslated] … but in this, when there is a great Moon-yoga, it becomes a giver of good, the two standing on a single line. (71)

[ṭīkā] … half … add 5 (manu) … thus: an odd number 15, adding one makes 16, half of that is 8 … [the ṭīkā breaks off and continues on the following page]
ocr_review_note: Four uncertain points. (1) v.69 pāda 2 '्गवङ्गष' — the first region-name is lost (2–3 akṣaras); the ṭīkā glosses it as Magadha, so 'मगधवङ्गेषु' is likely but the scan will not support it. (2) v.70 pāda 1 'शशाङ्कसूर्यक्षय॒भशेषे' — the division-instruction compound is corrupt; the sense (add the two nakṣatra numbers, divide by 27) is fixed by the ṭīkā, the wording is not. (3)–(4) v.71: pādas 2–3 (the rekhā/halving procedure) are substantially destroyed — only the phala list and the closing clause are legible. I have translated only the legible portions and marked the gap explicitly rather than supply a plausible-sounding reconstruction.

cleaned_devanagari_text:
प्रकरणम् ६ ] हिन्दी टीका सहित (९९)

… बलवान् एवं केन्द्रगत हो तो दशदोषका दोष नहीं होता — यह ग्रन्थान्तरका मत है ॥ ७१ ॥ (शार्दू०)

बाणदोषः पञ्चकाख्यः
लग्नेनाढ्या याततिथ्योऽङ्कतष्टाः शेषे नागद्व्यब्ध्यृत्विन्दुसंख्ये[?] ।
रोगोऽथ वह्नी राजचौरौ च मृत्युर्बाणश्चायं दाक्षिणात्यप्रसिद्धः ॥ ७२ ॥
लग्नमें शुक्लपक्ष प्रतिपदादिगत तिथि जोड़के ९ से तष्ट करे; शेष ८ रहे तो रोगबाण, २ शेषमें अग्नि, ४ में राजा, ६ में चोर, १ में मृत्युबाण होता है । यह दाक्षिणात्य (महाराष्ट्र) देशोंमें प्रसिद्ध है, अन्यत्र नहीं ॥ ७२ ॥ (शालिनी)

प्राच्यमतेन बाणः सापवादः
रसगुणशशिनागाब्ध्यर्कसंक्रान्तियातांशकमिति[?] … तष्टाङ्के यदा पञ्च शेषाः । रुग्नलनृपचौरामृत्युसंज्ञश्च बाणो नवहृतशरशेषे शेषकैक्ये सशल्यः ॥ ७३ ॥
निरयनांश सूर्यसंक्रान्तिसे गत अंशोंमें पृथक् पृथक् ६।३।१।८।४ जोड़के ९ से तष्ट करके जिस अंकमें ५ शेष रहे वह बाण इस प्रकार जानना । ६ में ५ शेष रहे तो रोगबाण, एवं ३ में अग्नि, १ में राज, ८ में चोर, ४ में मृत्युबाण होता है — यह काष्ठशल्य बाण है । पूर्वोक्त प्रकारसे ६ आदि अंकोंमें सूर्यगतांश जोड़के ९ से शेष करके जो नौ अंक शेष हैं उन सबको जोड़के ९ से शेष करना; यदि ५ शेष रहे तो (सशल्य) लोहशल्यसहित जानना, अन्यांक शेषमें शल्यरहित होता है । सशल्य अतिनिन्द्य है ॥ ७३ ॥ (मालिनी)

समयभेदेन तत्परिहारस्त्रिविधः
गुरौ[?] चौररुजौ दिवा नरपतिर्वह्निः सदा सन्ध्ययोः … शनौ [?] बुधे मृतिर्भौमेऽग्निश्चोरौ रवौ । रोगोऽथ व्रतगेहगोपनृपसेवायानपाणिग्रहे वर्ज्यौ क्रमतो … नरक्षमापालचौरा मृतिः ॥ ७४ ॥
चोर तथा रोगबाण रात्रिमें, नृपबाण दिनमें, वह्निबाण सदा अर्थात् दिन रात्रि दोनोंमें, मृत्युबाण[?] सन्ध्यासमयमें वर्ज्य हैं; तथा शनिवारमें राज, बुधमें मृत्यु, मंगलमें अग्नि चोर, [रविमें …]
content_en:
[Chapter 6 · with the Hindi ṭīkā · p. 99]

[ṭīkā, continuing v.71] … if [the Moon] is strong and placed in a kendra, then the doṣa of the ten doṣas does not obtain — this is the opinion of another work. (71) (metre: Śārdūlavikrīḍita)

Bāṇa-doṣa, called pañcaka (the five "arrows")
The elapsed tithis increased by the lagna and divided [by nine]: when the remainder is of the number 8, 2, 4, 6 or 1 [respectively] — disease, fire, the king, the thief, and death [are the bāṇas]. This bāṇa is well known among the southerners. (72)

[ṭīkā] Add to the lagna the tithis elapsed from the śukla-pakṣa pratipad and divide by 9. If the remainder is 8 it is roga-bāṇa (disease-arrow); with remainder 2, agni (fire); with 4, rāja (king); with 6, cora (thief); with 1, mṛtyu (death). This is current in the Dākṣiṇātya (Maharashtra) countries, not elsewhere. (72) (metre: Śālinī)

The bāṇa according to the eastern opinion, with its apavāda (exception)
[Adding severally] 6, 3, 1, 8 and 4 to the degrees elapsed of the Sun since the saṅkrānti … when, on division, the remainder is five [in a given case], the bāṇa is named disease, fire, king, thief and death [respectively]; and when, on dividing by nine, five remains from the sum of the [nine] remainders, it is sa-śalya ("with the barb"). (73)

[ṭīkā] To the nirayaṇa degrees elapsed of the Sun from the saṅkrānti add separately 6, 3, 1, 8 and 4, divide each by 9, and know the bāṇa from whichever number leaves a remainder of 5. If 5 remains in the case of 6, it is roga-bāṇa; so with 3, agni; with 1, rāja; with 8, cora; with 4, mṛtyu — this is the kāṣṭha-śalya (wooden-barbed) bāṇa. Then, in the manner stated above, add the Sun's elapsed degrees to the numbers 6 and the rest, take the remainders after dividing by 9, add all nine remainders together and divide by 9: if 5 remains, know it to be sa-śalya, i.e. attended by an iron barb; with any other remainder it is free of the barb. The sa-śalya is exceedingly to be condemned. (73) (metre: Mālinī)

Its parihāra (neutralisation), threefold, by difference of time
[The mūla of v.74 is heavily damaged; only the correspondences confirmed by the ṭīkā can be given:] the thief- and disease-bāṇas [are to be shunned] by day/night as stated, the king-bāṇa by day, the fire-bāṇa always, [the death-bāṇa] at the two twilights; and by weekday — on Saturn's day the king-, on Mercury's the death-, on Mars's the fire- and thief-[bāṇa] …; and by undertaking — in the vrata-bandha, house-protection, royal service, journey and marriage respectively. (74)

[ṭīkā] The thief- and disease-bāṇas are to be shunned at night, the king-bāṇa by day, the fire-bāṇa always, that is both by day and by night, and the death-bāṇa at the time of sandhyā (twilight). Further, on Saturday the king-, on Wednesday the death-, on Tuesday the fire- and thief-[bāṇa are shunned], on Sunday … [the ṭīkā continues on the next chunk]
ocr_review_note: Five uncertain points. (1) v.72 pāda 2 'नागद्वबन्धितकेन्दुसंख्ये' — the bhūta-saṅkhyā string is corrupt; the values 8/2/4/6/1 are fixed beyond doubt by the ṭīkā, but the exact akṣaras are restored conjecturally. (2) v.73 pāda 1 'नागान्ध्याटच' — the fifth numeral-word and the following 'रथ' are unresolvable; the ṭīkā fixes the series as 6,3,1,8,4 and the divisor as 9. (3)–(4) v.74 pādas 1–2 and 4 are largely destroyed ('गरौ … सन्ध्ययोरैतयुश्वाय शनौ', 'क्रमतो बु सुगनरक्षमापाल…'); I have translated only what the ṭīkā independently confirms and marked the verse as damaged rather than reconstruct it. (5) ṭīkā line 'षम बाण संध्यासमयमें' — the bāṇa name is illegible; 'मृत्यु' is forced by elimination from the closed set of five, but is not read off the page. Note also the ṭīkā's '९ में ५ शेष' is a scan error for '६ में ५ शेष' (corrected, since the series begins at 6 = roga).

… वर्जित है । और व्रतबन्धमें रोगबाण, गृहगोपनादि घरके कृत्यमें अग्निबाण, [राज]सेवामें नृपबाण, यात्रामें चोरबाण, विवाहमें मृत्युबाण त्याज्य है ॥ ७४ ॥
(शार्दूलविक्रीडित)
