[This chunk is the continuation of the ṭīkā on v.74 begun on the preceding page; it opens mid-sentence.]

[ṭīkā] … is prohibited. And in the vrata-bandha (investiture with the sacred thread) the roga-bāṇa (disease-arrow), in house-protection and the other domestic rites the agni-bāṇa (fire-arrow), in [royal] service the nṛpa-bāṇa (king-arrow), on a yātrā (journey) the cora-bāṇa (thief-arrow), and in marriage the mṛtyu-bāṇa (death-arrow) is to be avoided. (74)
(metre: Śārdūlavikrīḍita)

cleaned_devanagari_text:
(१०२) मुहूर्तचिन्तामणि [विवाह-

सूर्यके संक्रमसे पूर्वापरकी ३२ घटी, एवं शशि(चन्द्र)की २, मंगलकी ९, बुधकी ६, बृहस्पतिकी ८[?], शुक्रकी ९, शनिकी १३०[?] घटी संक्रमणकी शुभकार्यमें वर्जित हैं । और रविग्रहका जो घटीत्याग कहा है वह अतिनिन्दित है । इसका विशेष विचार संक्रान्तिप्रकरणमें कह आये हैं ॥ ८० ॥ (अनु०)

पङ्ग्वन्धकाणबधिराख्यलग्नदोषः
दिवा[?] तुलाली बधिरौ मृगाश्वौ रात्रौ च सिंहाजवृषा दिवान्धाः ।
कन्यानृयुक्कर्कटका निशान्धा दिने घटोऽन्त्यो निशि पङ्गुसंज्ञः ॥ ८१ ॥
दिनमें ७।८ लग्न बधिर हैं, १०।९ रात्रिमें बधिर हैं; ५।१।२ दिनमें, ६।३।४ रात्रिमें अन्धे हैं; ११ दिनमें, १२ रात्रिमें पंगु (खोड़) हैं ॥ ८१ ॥ (उ० जा०)

बधिरा धनुस्तुलालयोऽपराह्णे मिथुनं कर्कटकोऽङ्गना निशान्धाः ।
दिवसान्धा हरिगोक्रियास्तु कुब्जा मृगकुम्भान्तिमभानि सन्ध्ययोर्हि ॥ ८२ ॥
९।७।८ लग्न (अपराह्ण) दिनके पिछले त्रिभागमें बधिर हैं; ३।४।६ रात्रिमें अन्धे हैं; ५।२।१ दिनमें अन्धे हैं; १०।११।१२ सन्ध्यामें कुब्ज हैं ॥ ८२ ॥ (वसन्तमालिका)

एषां प्रयोजनं सापवादम्
दिवान्धलग्ने वैषम्यं शिशुमरणं निशान्धलग्ने ।
… धननाशमीयुः सर्वं बाधिर्ये[?] लग्नपगुरुदृष्टिभिर्न दोषः ॥ ८३ ॥
बधिरलग्नोंमें विवाहादि करनेमें दरिद्रता, दिवान्ध लग्नमें वैधव्य, रात्र्यन्ध लग्नमें शिशुमरण, पंगुलग्नमें समस्त धननाश होवे । यदि इनपर लग्नेश तथा बृहस्पतिकी दृष्टि हो तो इनका उक्त दोष नहीं है । और भी परिहार है कि — "पङ्ग्वन्धकाणलग्नानि मासशून्याश्च राशयः । गौडमालवयोस्त्याज्या अन्यदेशे न गर्हिताः ॥" अर्थात् उक्त दोष तथा मासशून्यराशि गौडदेश, मालवदेशमें त्याज्य है, अन्यत्र नहीं ॥ ८३ ॥ (प्रहर्षिणी)

विहितनवांशाः
कार्मुकतौलिककन्यायुगमकरे हरिषे[?] वा ।
ग्राह्ये भवेदुपयामस्तर्हि सती खलु कन्या ॥ ८४ ॥
विवाहलग्नमें यदि ९।७ …
content_en:
[p. 102 · Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi · Vivāha-]

[ṭīkā, on v.80] The 32 ghaṭīs before and after the Sun's saṅkrama (ingress), and likewise 2 ghaṭīs for the Moon, 9 for Mars, 6 for Mercury, 8 for Jupiter, 9 for Venus and 130 for Saturn about their ingresses, are prohibited for auspicious undertakings; and the ghaṭī-rejection stated for the planet Sun is the most strongly condemned of all. The detailed consideration of this has been given in the Saṅkrānti prakaraṇa. (80) (metre: Anuṣṭubh)

The lagna-doṣas named lame, blind, one-eyed and deaf
By day Tulā and Ali (Vṛścika) are deaf, and by night Mṛga (Makara) and [Dhanus]; Siṃha, Aja (Meṣa) and Vṛṣa are blind by day; Kanyā, Nṛyuk (Mithuna) and Karkaṭaka are blind by night; Ghaṭa (Kumbha) by day and the last sign (Mīna) by night bear the name lame. (81)

[ṭīkā] By day the 7th and 8th lagnas are deaf; the 10th and 9th are deaf by night. The 5th, 1st and 2nd are blind by day, the 6th, 3rd and 4th blind by night. The 11th by day and the 12th by night are lame (khoṛ). (81)

Dhanus, Tulā and Ālaya (Vṛścika) are deaf in the afternoon; Mithuna, Karkaṭaka and Aṅganā (Kanyā) are blind by night; Hari (Siṃha), Go (Vṛṣa) and Kriyā (Meṣa) are blind by day; while Mṛga (Makara), Kumbha and the last sign are hunchbacked at the two twilights. (82)

[ṭīkā] The 9th, 7th and 8th lagnas are deaf in the last third of the day (aparāhṇa); the 3rd, 4th and 6th are blind at night; the 5th, 2nd and 1st are blind by day; the 10th, 11th and 12th are hunchbacked at twilight. (82) (metre: Vasantamālikā)

Their application, together with its apavāda (exception)
In a day-blind lagna, inequity [widowhood]; in a night-blind lagna, death of the infant; … they meet with destruction of all wealth; [and in] deafness … — but through the aspects of the lagna-lord and of Guru (Jupiter) there is no doṣa. (83)

[ṭīkā] Performing marriage and the like in the deaf lagnas gives poverty; in a day-blind lagna, widowhood; in a night-blind lagna, the death of the infant; in a lame lagna, destruction of all wealth. But if the lagna-lord and Bṛhaspati aspect these, the stated doṣa of theirs does not hold. And there is a further parihāra (cancellation), namely: "The lame, blind and one-eyed lagnas, and the māsa-śūnya (month-void) signs, are to be shunned in Gauḍa and Mālava; in another country they are not censured." That is to say, the aforesaid doṣa and the māsa-śūnya signs are to be avoided in the Gauḍa country and the Mālava country, and not elsewhere. (83) (metre: Praharṣiṇī)

The prescribed navāṃśas
When the navāṃśa taken is that of Kārmuka (Dhanus), Taulika (Tulā), Kanyā, Yuga (Mithuna), Makara or [?] — if the marriage takes place then, the bride is assuredly chaste. (84)

[ṭīkā] If in the marriage lagna the navāṃśas of the 9th, 7th … [continues on the next chunk]
ocr_review_note: Four uncertain points. (1) ṭīkā on v.80: the ghaṭī figures are scan-mangled ('३२३', '८८', '१३०'); I have read 32 for the Sun and 8 for Jupiter as the intended values, but Saturn's '१३०' is anomalously large and may be a broken '१।३०'. (2) v.81 pāda 1 opening 'धसे' is illegible (restored 'दिवा' from sense); the pair 'मृगाश्वौ' does not obviously yield the ṭīkā's signs 10 and 9 — Makara is secure, the second is not. (3) v.83 pādas 2–3 are largely destroyed; the surviving mūla is translated only as far as it is legible, the phala-list being supplied from the ṭīkā and marked as such. (4) v.84 'हरिषे' — an unresolved sixth item; the ṭīkā's sign list reads '९।७।[८]।६।३।१२' but the mūla names Makara, so mūla and ṭīkā do not agree and neither reading can be preferred on the scan.

कर्तर्यादिमहादोषापवादः
पापौ[?] कर्तरिकारकौ रिपौ[?] नीचास्तगौ कर्तरीदोषो नैव, सिते[?]ऽरिगृहगते षष्ठे[?] दोषोऽपि न, भौमेऽस्तमिते नीचगे न हि भवेद् दोषोऽ[ष्टमे][?], नीचनवांशके शशिनि रिः[?]… [षडष्टव्यये] दोषोऽपि न ॥ ८८ ॥

The apavāda (annulling exception) of the kartarī and the other great doṣas

[The mūla of v.88 is severely damaged on this page; its content is fixed by the ṭīkā that follows on the next page, and is rendered here on that authority:] When the two pāpa-grahas that produce the kartarī (the "scissors" affliction) are in an enemy's house, in debilitation or combust, there is no kartarī-doṣa at all; if Śukra (Venus) is debilitated or in an enemy's sign, then even in the sixth there is no doṣa; if Bhauma (Mars) is debilitated or combust, no doṣa arises even in the eighth; and if the Moon is in a debilitated sign or a debilitated navāṃśa, [in the 6th, 8th or 12th] there is likewise no doṣa. (88)
ocr_review_note: The mūla of v.88 on this page is largely illegible — the scan preserves only scattered akṣara-clusters ('पौ कतैरिकारको रिषे नीचास्तगौ केतेरीदोषी नेव', 'भौमिऽतरिपनीचगे', 'नीचन्वाशके शशिनि'). The reading given is a reconstruction whose *sense* is established by Mahīdhara's ṭīkā on the following page (pg0116_c01), not read off this page; the akṣaras themselves are not recoverable. Six or more separate points are conjectural, hence the floor score. Verse number is printed as '८<' (= ८८).

(१०४) मुहूर्तचिन्तामणि [विवाह-

कर्तरीकारक पापग्रह यदि शत्रुगृहमें और नीच तथा अस्तंगत हो (तथा उनके बीच कोई शुभग्रह हो) तो लग्न वा सप्तममें कर्तरीका दोष नहीं । तथा शुक्र नीच वा शत्रुराशिका हो तो छठे हो तो भी दोष नहीं । मंगल यदि नीच राशिका वा अस्तंगत हो वा अष्टम हो तो भी दोष नहीं । और चन्द्रमा नीच राशि वा नीचनवांशका होकर ६।८।१२ स्थानोंमें हो तो इसका दोष नहीं ॥ ८८ ॥ (शा०)

विवाहेऽब्ददोषाद्यपवादः
अब्दायनर्तुतिथिमासभपक्षदग्धतिथ्यन्धकाणवधिरपङ्गुलाश्च दोषाः ।
नश्यन्ति विद्गुरुसितेष्विह केन्द्रकोणे तद्वच्च पापविधुयुक्तनवांशदोषाः ॥ ८९ ॥
अब्ददोष १, अयनदोष २, ऋतुदोष ३, तिथिदोष ४, मासदोष ५, नक्षत्रदोष ६, पक्षदोष ७, दग्धतिथि ८, अन्ध ९, काण १०, बधिर ११, पंगु आदि लग्नदोष १२, अकालवृष्ट्यादि १३ — इतने दोष लग्नसे केन्द्र (१।४।७।१०) कोण (९।५) में बुध बृहस्पति शुक्रके बलवान् होकर स्थित होनेमें अनिष्ट फल नहीं करते । वैसा ही पापयुत चन्द्रमा वा पापयुक्त नवांशदोष भी नष्ट हो जाता है ॥ ८९ ॥ (व०)

उक्तानुक्तदोषपरिहारः
केन्द्रे कोणे जीव आये रवौ वा लग्ने चन्द्रे वापि वर्गोत्तमे वा ।
सर्वे दोषा नाशमायान्ति चन्द्रे कामे तद्[?]ग्रहसैहर्तीशदोषाः ॥ ९० ॥
केन्द्र (१।४।७।१०) कोण (५।९) तथा ११ में [बृहस्पति], लग्नसे उपचय (३।६।१०।११) में रवि — उपलक्षणसे बुध शुक्र भी — हो तो उक्त समस्त दोष नष्ट होते हैं । ऐसे ही चन्द्रमा ११ में अथवा वर्गोत्तम नवांशमें [हो, तथा] सातवें भावमें हो तो "रात्र्यन्ध" इत्यादि कुमुहूर्त और पापग्रहनवांशदोष भी नष्ट होते हैं ॥ ९० ॥ (शा०)

सामान्येन दोषसहपरिहारः
विलग्ने कोणे केन्द्रे वा मदनरहिते दोषशतकं हरत्सौम्यः, शुक्रो द्विशतमपि, … लक्षं सुरगुरुः, … [?] … केन्द्रे लग्नप उतांशेशो[?] यदि तदा समूहं दोषाणां दहन इव तूलं शमयति ॥ ९१ ॥
विवाहलग्नसे सप्तमरहित केन्द्र (१।४।७।१०) कोण … [टीका अगले खण्डमें चलती है]
content_en:
[p. 104 · Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi · Vivāha-]

[ṭīkā, completing v.88] If the pāpa-grahas that produce the kartarī are in an enemy's house, in debilitation and combust (and if some benefic stands between them), then there is no kartarī-doṣa in the lagna or the seventh. And if Śukra is debilitated or in an enemy's sign, there is no doṣa even when he is in the sixth. If Maṅgala (Mars) is in a debilitated sign, or combust, or in the eighth, there is likewise no doṣa. And if the Moon, being in a debilitated sign or a debilitated navāṃśa, stands in the 6th, 8th or 12th, there is no doṣa from him. (88)

The apavāda of the year-doṣa and the rest in marriage
The doṣas of the year, the ayana, the season, the tithi, the month, the nakṣatra, the fortnight, the dagdha-tithi, and the blind, one-eyed, deaf and lame [lagnas] perish here when Mercury, Jupiter and Venus are in a kendra or a trine; and in the same way the doṣas of a Moon conjoined with malefics and of a navāṃśa held by malefics. (89)

[ṭīkā] The year-doṣa (1), ayana-doṣa (2), ṛtu-doṣa (3), tithi-doṣa (4), month-doṣa (5), nakṣatra-doṣa (6), pakṣa-doṣa (7), dagdha-tithi (8), blind (9), one-eyed (10), deaf (11), lame and the other lagna-doṣas (12), untimely rain and the like (13) — all these doṣas produce no evil result when Budha, Bṛhaspati and Śukra stand strong in a kendra (1, 4, 7, 10) or a koṇa (9, 5) from the lagna. In just the same way the doṣa of a Moon conjoined with malefics, or of a navāṃśa held by malefics, is destroyed. (89)

The parihāra of the doṣas both stated and unstated
When Jīva (Jupiter) is in a kendra, a trine or the eleventh, or the Sun [in the upacaya houses], or the Moon in the lagna or in a vargottama navāṃśa — all doṣas come to destruction; and when the Moon is in the seventh, the doṣas of [an evil] muhūrta and the rest [also perish]. (90)

[ṭīkā] If [Bṛhaspati] is in a kendra (1, 4, 7, 10), a koṇa (5, 9) or the 11th, and the Sun in an upacaya (3, 6, 10, 11) from the lagna — and by implication Budha and Śukra also — then all the aforesaid doṣas are destroyed. In the same way, if the Moon is in the 11th or in a vargottama navāṃśa, and in the seventh house, then the "night-blind" and the other bad muhūrtas, and the doṣa of a malefic navāṃśa, are also destroyed. (90)

The parihāra of doṣas in general, all together
When in the marriage-lagna, in a trine or in a kendra other than the seventh, Saumya (Mercury) stands, he removes a hundred doṣas; Śukra even two hundred; … the Guru of the gods a lakh; … and if the lord of the lagna and the lord of the navāṃśa are in a kendra, then he quiets the whole heap of doṣas as fire [consumes] cotton. (91)

[ṭīkā] In a kendra excluding the seventh (1, 4, 7, 10) or a koṇa reckoned from the marriage lagna … [the ṭīkā continues in the next chunk]
ocr_review_note: Three uncertain points. (1) v.90 pāda 4 'तदरहसैहर्तीशदोषाः' is corrupt; the ṭīkā glosses it as the ku-muhūrta and malefic-navāṃśa doṣas, which is the sense translated, but the compound cannot be restored. (2)–(3) v.91: the middle of the verse (the graded doṣa-counts between Venus's two hundred and Jupiter's lakh, and the phrase before 'केन्द्रे लग्नप') is broken, and 'उतेशो' is ambiguous between 'उत + अंशेशः' (navāṃśa lord, so the ṭīkā) and other readings. The ṭīkā for v.90 is also physically interleaved out of order in the scan and has been re-sequenced here to follow its sense.

प्रकरणम् ६ ] हिन्दी टीका सहित (१०७)

मण्डपादौ स्तम्भनिवेशनम्
सूर्येऽब्धिनासिद[?]षरेषु शैवे स्तम्भोऽरिकदण्डमृगेषु[?] वायौ ।
मीनाजकुम्भे निर्ऋतौ विवाहे स्थाप्योऽग्निकोणे वृषयुग्मकर्के ॥ ९९ ॥
मंडपमें प्रथम स्तम्भनिवेशन ६।५।७ के सूर्यमें ईशानकोणमें, ८।९।१० क्रममें वायव्य, १२।१।११ क्रममें नैर्ऋत्य, २।३।४ क्रममें आग्नेयमें करना । यही नियम गृहारम्भमें भी है ॥ ९९ ॥ (इन्द्रवज्रा)

गोधूलीप्रशंसा
नास्यामृक्षं न तिथिकरणं नैव लग्नस्य चिन्ता नो वा वारो न च लवविधिर्नो मुहूर्तस्य चर्चा ।
नो वा योगो न मृतिभवनं नैव यामित्रदोषो गोधूलिः सा मुनिभिरुदिता स्वकार्येषु शस्ता ॥ १०० ॥
गोधूलीमें नक्षत्र तिथि करणकी कुछ अपेक्षा नहीं, लग्नका विचार भी नहीं, तथा वार अंशक मुहूर्तकी भी चर्चा नहीं; दृष्टियोग, अष्टमशुद्धि, यामित्रदोष कुछ नहीं होता । यह गोधूलि मुनियोंने सब कार्योंमें शुभ कही है ॥ १०० ॥ (मन्दाक्रान्ता)

गोधूलीभेदाः
पिण्डीभूते दिनकृति हेमन्तर्तौ स्यादर्धास्ते तपःसमये गोधूलिः ।
सम्पूर्णास्ते जलधरमालाकाले ह्येधा योज्या सकलशुभे कार्यादौ ॥ १०१ ॥
उक्त गोधूलीका समय कहते हैं कि (हेमन्त) शीतकाल मार्गशीर्षसे ४ महीने सूर्य जब सायंकालमें नीहारादिरहित किरणशून्य पिण्डाकार हो; तथा (तप) उष्णकाल चैत्रसे ४ महीने (अर्धास्त) सूर्यबिम्ब आधा अस्त होनेमें; (जलधरमाला) वर्षाकाल श्रावणसे ४ महीने सूर्यके सम्पूर्ण अस्त हुएमें गोधूली होती है । समस्त शुभ कृत्यादिमें गुणदाता है ॥ १०१ ॥ (जलधरमाला)

तत्रावश्यवर्ज्यदोषाः
अस्तं याते गुरुदिवसे सौरे सके[?] लग्नमृत्यौ रिपुभवने लग्ने चन्द्रौ ।
कन्यानाशस्तनुमदमृत्युस्थे भौमे वोढुर्मे धनसहजे चन्द्रे सौख्यम् ॥ १०२ ॥
गोधूलीका और भी प्रकार है कि, गुरुवारके दिन सूर्यास्त होनेपर गोधूली होती है । सूर्यास्तके पूर्व आधी घटी अर्धयाम होनेसे छोड़ दिया । शनिवारमें सूर्य देखते ही हैं, क्योंकि …
content_en:
[Chapter 6 · with the Hindi ṭīkā · p. 107]

The setting of the pillar in the maṇḍapa and the rest
When the Sun is in [Kanyā, Siṃha, Tulā] the pillar is to be set in the Śaiva (north-east) corner; in [Vṛścika, Dhanus, Makara] in the Vāyu (north-west); in Mīna, Aja (Meṣa) and Kumbha in the Nirṛti (south-west); and in Vṛṣa, Yugma (Mithuna) and Karka it is to be set, at a marriage, in the Agni (south-east) corner. (99)

[ṭīkā] The first setting of the pillar in the maṇḍapa is to be done in the Īśāna corner when the Sun is in the 6th, 5th or 7th sign; in the Vāyavya when he is in the 8th, 9th, 10th in order; in the Nairṛtya when in the 12th, 1st, 11th in order; and in the Āgneya when in the 2nd, 3rd, 4th in order. The same rule holds for the commencement of a house. (99) (metre: Indravajrā)

In praise of godhūli
In it there is no nakṣatra (lunar mansion), no tithi (lunar day) or karaṇa, no consideration of the lagna at all, nor vāra (weekday), nor the rule of the navāṃśa, nor any discussion of the muhūrta; nor yoga, nor the house of death (the eighth), nor yāmitra-doṣa at all. That godhūli has been declared by the sages to be commended for one's every undertaking. (100)

[ṭīkā] In godhūli there is no requirement whatever of nakṣatra, tithi or karaṇa, nor any consideration of the lagna, nor any discussion of vāra, navāṃśa or muhūrta; there is no dṛṣṭi-yoga, no purity of the eighth, no yāmitra-doṣa at all. The sages have declared this godhūli auspicious for all undertakings. (100) (metre: Mandākrāntā)

The varieties of godhūli
When the Sun is congealed into a disc, in the Hemanta season; when he is half-set, in the season of heat; and when fully set, in the time of the rain-cloud garland — [in these three ways] godhūli is to be applied at the outset of every auspicious undertaking. (101)

[ṭīkā] The time of the said godhūli is stated thus: in the cold season (hemanta), the four months from Mārgaśīrṣa, when the Sun at evening is free of mist and the like, rayless and disc-shaped; in the hot season (tapas), the four months from Caitra, when the Sun's orb is half set; in the rainy season (jaladhara-mālā), the four months from Śrāvaṇa, when the Sun has fully set — then godhūli obtains. It is a giver of merit in all auspicious rites. (101) (metre: Jaladharamālā)

The doṣas that must be avoided even therein
When [the Sun] has set on Guru's day, on Saturn's [?] …; when the Moon is in the lagna, the house of death, or the house of the enemy [reckoned from the lagna], there is destruction of the bride; when Bhauma (Mars) is in the 1st, 7th or 8th, [destruction] of the bridegroom; but when the Moon is in the 2nd or 3rd, there is happiness. (102)

[ṭīkā] There is a further mode of godhūli: on Thursday, godhūli obtains after the Sun has set — the half ghaṭī before sunset was excluded because it is the ardha-yāma. On Saturday they take it at the very sight of the Sun, because … [the ṭīkā continues in the next chunk]

(2) v.102 pāda 1 'सौरे सके' — 2–3 akṣaras lost after 'सौरे'; the clause about Saturn's day cannot be completed from the mūla, and the ṭīkā's own explanation breaks off at the chunk boundary.

[ṭīkā] … [the evil combinations] arising from tithi (lunar day) and vāra (weekday) — [?] and the rest; those arising from nakṣatra (lunar mansion) and vāra — Mṛtyu and the rest; those arising from tithi, nakṣatra and vāra together — Hastārka-pañcamī and the rest; and other such duṣṭa-yogas (evil combinations); further doṣas such as the ardha-yāma and the kulika; a nakṣatra beset by malefics, a nakṣatra just quitted by a malefic, and a nakṣatra a malefic is about to enter, …

(1) The chunk opens mid-word: the preceding chunk ends '(सूर्यशे-' and this one resumes 'स्यादि)', so the name of the first tithi×vāra yoga class straddles the chunk boundary and cannot be recovered from either half — the parenthesis is left untranslated rather than guessed. (2) A stray '४' stands after 'आदि दुष्ट', where the governing noun (evidently 'योग') is lost. Note that the three-way classification here — tithi-vāra-born, nakṣatra-vāra-born, and tithi-nakṣatra-vāra-born combinations, with 'Mṛtyu' and 'Hastārka-pañcamī' named as instances — is the passage's substantive content for this topic.

अथ द्विरागमनप्रकरणम् ८
द्विरागमनमुहूर्तः
चरेदथौजहायने झषालिमेषगे रवौ रवीज्यशुद्धियोगतः शुभग्रहस्य वासरे ।
नृयुग्ममीनकन्यकातुलावृषे विशुद्धर्क्षे द्विरागमं लघुध्रुवे चरेऽल्पे मृदूडुनि ॥ १ ॥

सम्मुखशुक्रदोषः
… [यदि स्यात्] सम्मुखो दक्षिणो वा [भार्गवः][?], तर्हि न व्रजेयुर्बालो गर्भिणी नवोढा च[?] ।
बालश्चेद् व्रजति विपत्तिं [याति], नवोढा चेद् वन्ध्या भवति, गर्भिणी त्वगर्भा ॥ २ ॥
विवाहमें भर्ताके घर जानेमें यात्रोक्त शुक्रसम्मुखादि शुद्धि नहीं देखते, इसलिये द्विरागमनमें देखना आवश्यक होनेसे शुक्रशुद्धि कहते हैं कि — शुक्र सम्मुख तथा दक्षिण हो तो बालक, गर्भवती, नवविवाहिता गमन न करें । इस प्रतिशुक्रमें बालक गमन करे तो विपत्ति (मृत्यु) पावे, नवोढा वन्ध्या होवे, गर्भिणी गर्भरहित होवे । "अस्तं गते गुरौ शुक्रे सिंहस्थे वा बृहस्पतौ । दीपोत्सवदिने चैव कन्या भर्तृगृहं विशेत् ॥" किसीका मत है कि गुरु अस्त हो, वा शुक्र अस्त हो वा सम्मुख दक्षिण हो, वा सिंहस्थ गुरु हो — इन दोषोंमें भी आवश्यकता होनेमें (कन्या) नववधू (दीपोत्सव) दीपमालिकाके [दो दिन प्रथम, दो दिन पीछे के] दिनमें भर्ताके घर जावे तो दोष नहीं ॥ २ ॥ (प्रहर्षिणी)

प्रतिशुक्रापवादः
नगरप्रवेशे विषयाद्युपद्रवे करपीडने विबुधतीर्थयात्रयोः ।
वरे[?]णपीडने नववधूप्रवेशने प्रति भार्गवो भवति दोषकृन्न हि ॥ ३ ॥
शत्रुचक्रागम, राजविद्रोह आदि उपद्रवसे स्वनगरप्रवेशमें, किंवा दुर्भिक्षादि दुःखसे अन्यत्र …

[Chapter 8 · with the Hindi ṭīkā · p. 111]

Now the prakaraṇa on dvirāgamana (the bride's second coming), 8
The muhūrta for dvirāgamana
Let one perform it in an odd year, when the Sun is in Mīna, Vṛścika or Meṣa, with the purity of Sun and Jupiter conjoined, on the day (vāra, weekday) of a benefic planet, in the lagnas Mithuna, Mīna, Kanyā, Tulā or Vṛṣa, in a pure nakṣatra (lunar mansion) — one of the laghu, dhruva, cara or mṛdu class. (1)

[ṭīkā] When, after the vadhū-praveśa, the bride goes to her father's house and comes again to her husband's house, that is called dvirāgamana. It should be done in an odd year — the 1st, 3rd or 5th — when the Sun is in the 11th, 1st or 8th [sign], when the purity of the Sun and of Guru stated for marriage obtains, on the days of benefic planets, in the lagnas 3, 12, 6, 7, 2, and in the laghu, dhruva, cara and mṛdu nakṣatras. (1) (metre: Pañcacāmara)

The doṣa (affliction) of Śukra facing or to the right
[If Bhārgava (Venus)] be facing or to the right, then let not a child, a pregnant woman, or a newly-wed bride travel. If a child travels, [he meets] calamity; if a newly-wed, she becomes barren; and a pregnant woman loses her child. (2)

[ṭīkā] In marriage, when going to the husband's house, the purity of Śukra as to facing and the rest — which is prescribed for journeys — is not examined; and since it is therefore necessary to examine it at the dvirāgamana, the purity of Śukra is here stated: if Śukra is facing (sammukha) or to the right (dakṣiṇa), a child, a pregnant woman and a newly-wed bride should not travel. If a child travels under this pratiśukra he meets calamity (death); a newly-wed becomes barren; a pregnant woman loses her child. [And it is said:] "When Guru or Śukra has set, or when Bṛhaspati is in Siṃha, and likewise on the day of the festival of lamps, the girl may enter her husband's house." It is the opinion of some that even under these doṣas — Jupiter combust, or Venus combust or facing or to the right, or Jupiter in Siṃha — if there is necessity, then if the bride goes to her husband's house on the days of the Dīpotsava (Dīpāvalī) [reckoned two days before and two days after], there is no doṣa. (2) (metre: Praharṣiṇī)

The apavāda (annulling exception) of the pratiśukra
On entering a city; in a calamity such as [invasion of] the territory; at a marriage ("the seizing of the hand"); on a pilgrimage to the gods or to a tīrtha; on [?]; and at the entry of a newly-wed bride — Bhārgava confronting does not become a producer of doṣa at all. (3)

[ṭīkā] On entering one's own city because of a calamity such as the approach of an enemy host or a royal revolt; or, because of the distress of famine and the like, elsewhere … [the ṭīkā continues in the next chunk]
ocr_review_note: Three uncertain points. (1)–(2) The mūla of v.2 is severely corrupted ('दत्येन्यो द्भियुंखदक्षिणेयदिस्यारच्छेयुर्महिशिङ्गभिणीनवोटाः'): the subject-word and the verb of the first half, and the connective in the second, are unreadable. The translation follows the sense that Mahīdhara's ṭīkā establishes verbatim, and the akṣaras are not claimed. (3) v.3 pāda 3 'वरेपपीडने' — the occasion listed between the pilgrimage and the bride's entry cannot be read (2 akṣaras lost); the ṭīkā's corresponding item appears to be 'when the king expels [one]', but the correspondence is not secure. Also note the ṭīkā's Dīpāvalī window ('२ पके') is damaged; '(two days before, two after)' is supplied and bracketed.

The remaining damage in this fragment ('गौर' for 'और', 'पतविताहिता' for 'विवाहिता') is typographic and unambiguous.

भृग्वङ्गिरोवत्सवसिष्ठकश्यपात्रीणां भरद्वाजमुनेः कुले तथा ॥ ४ ॥
इति मुहूर्तचिन्तामणावष्टमं द्विरागमनप्रकरणम् ॥ ८ ॥
यदि कन्या पिताके ही घरमें (कुच) स्तन उग आवें तथा रजोदर्शन हो जावे तो प्रतिशुक्रका दोष नहीं; उपलक्षणसे सूर्य गुरुशुद्धि भी नहीं । और भृगु, अंगिरा, वत्स, वसिष्ठ, कश्यप, अत्रि, भरद्वाज — इन ऋषियोंके वंशमें, अर्थात् उक्त गोत्रवालोंको भी प्रतिशुक्रका दोष कभी नहीं है ॥ ४ ॥ (इ० व०)

श्रौत स्मार्त कर्मानुष्ठानके अग्निधारणको अग्न्याधान कहते हैं । यह कोई तो विवाहमें, कोई पिता व भाईसे पृथक् [होनेमें करते हैं] … ध्रुव, रेवती, मृगशिरा, ज्येष्ठा, पुष्य नक्षत्रमें …

… केन्द्रत्रिकोणे … षट् … नौ कर्कनक्रझषकुम्भनवांशे … नो लग्ने तनौ रविशशिगुरुकुजे[?] युते व्ययरिपौ ॥ २ ॥
… [लग्न] वा नवांशक तथा लग्नका चन्द्रमा — ये न लेने चाहिये । और [गुरु, बुध,] शुक्र, राहु, केतु ३।११।६।१० स्थानोंमें हों, तथा लग्नसे अष्टमभाव ग्रहरहित हो, जन्मराशिसे अष्टम लग्न न हो, तो उक्त कृत्य शुभ होता है ॥ २ ॥ (व० ति०)

[p. 112 · Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi · Agnyādhāna prakaraṇa]

If, while still in her father's house, the flowering of the breasts has occurred in women, there is no doṣa arising from the pratiśukra; likewise in the lineage of Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Vatsa, Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa, Atri and the sage Bharadvāja. (4)
Here ends the eighth prakaraṇa, on dvirāgamana, in the Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi. (8)

[ṭīkā] If, while the girl is still in her father's very house, the breasts (kuca) have grown and menstruation has appeared, then there is no doṣa of the pratiśukra; and by implication the purity of the Sun and of Guru is likewise not required. And in the lineage of the sages Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Vatsa, Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa, Atri and Bharadvāja — that is, for those of the said gotras — there is never any doṣa of the pratiśukra at all. (4) (metre: Indravajrā)
Here ends the eighth prakaraṇa in Mahīdhara's vernacular ṭīkā on the Śrī Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi. (8)

Now the prakaraṇa on agnyādhāna (the establishing of the sacred fire), 9
The muhūrta for agnyādhāna
[The mūla of v.1 is badly damaged; only these members are legible:] … the rite … when the Sun is in the northern [signs] … or in the three Uttarā [nakṣatras] …; in a nakṣatra of the Moon, Venus and [the benefics] …; not when the Moon, Mars, Jupiter or Venus is debilitated, nor combust, nor defeated [in planetary war], nor in the house of [a malefic]. (1)

[ṭīkā] The taking up of the fire for the performance of the śrauta and smārta rites is called agnyādhāna. Some perform it at marriage, some on separating from father or brother … in the dhruva [nakṣatras], Revatī, Mṛgaśiras, Jyeṣṭhā and Puṣya …

[v.2, likewise damaged:] … in the kendras and trines … the sixth …; not in the navāṃśas of Karka, Nakra (Makara), Jhaṣa (Mīna) or Kumbha …; not in the lagna, when the Sun, Moon, Jupiter or Mars is conjoined in the twelfth or the sixth. (2)

[ṭīkā] … the [lagna] or the navāṃśa, and the Moon of the lagna — these are not to be taken. And if [Jupiter, Mercury,] Venus, Rāhu and Ketu are in the 3rd, 11th, 6th or 10th houses, and the eighth house from the lagna is free of planets, and the lagna is not the eighth from the natal rāśi, then the said rite is auspicious. (2)
ocr_review_note: Verse 4 and its ṭīkā — the parihāra material for which this chunk is flagged priority — are clean and are rendered with confidence. The uncertainty is confined to the opening of the Agnyādhāna prakaraṇa that follows on the same page, where three points are unreadable: (1) v.1 pāda 1 'सपादब्निहोधविधिरुत्तरेदिनेशेमिशरथवात्यशशिशकसरेल्यधिष्ण्य' — the rite-name and the sign/nakṣatra conditions are run together and partly lost; (2) v.1 pāda 4 'न च शङ्जगेहे' — the house-owner word is corrupt; (3) v.2 is broken by column damage ('केन्दरक्षषट् विभेव', 'रविशशीज्यङ्कजे युतेविल्यरे') and its house-lists survive only in the ṭīkā. Those portions are translated only so far as legible, with the gaps marked rather than filled.

[ṭīkā] …(saṃdhi — a negotiated settlement) results. This consideration [applies to] every journey[?]. || 15 || (Śā. Vi.)

THE RESULT OF THE AKULA–KULĀKULA–KULA CAKRA

|| 16–17 || [The two mūla verses are severely damaged in this scan. Only the following is legible with confidence, and the enumeration of nakṣatra is largely lost:] The akula class is constituted by certain nakṣatra (lunar mansions) — among them Anurādhā and the triad beginning with it, together with the dhruva ("fixed") nakṣatra — and by the odd-numbered tithi (lunar days). The kulākula class carries the tithi reckoned as ten, six and two. The kula class is constituted by nakṣatra named in the verse by their presiding deities — the Pūrvā group, Ījya (Puṣya), Aśva (Aśvinī), Indu (Mṛgaśira), Karṇa (Śravaṇa), Dahana (Kṛttikā), Indra (Jyeṣṭhā) and Citrā — and by the tithi measured as twelve, eight, fourteen and four. Thereupon: the yāyī (the king who marches out) is the victor [under the akula members]; the sthāyī (the king who holds his ground) [is the victor under the kula members]; and where the two are mixed (kulākula) the outcome is saṃdhi (a truce in which both prevail). || 16 || || 17 ||

Numerals are secure: 'दशषड्द्वि' = tithi 10/6/2 and 'अर्काष्टेन्द्रवेद' = tithi 12/8/14/4. धर्मे भास्करे वित्तमोक्षे शशी वित्ते धर्ममोक्षस्थितिः शस्यते ।
कामगे धर्ममोक्षार्थगः शोभनो मोक्षगे केवलं धर्मगः प्रोच्यते ॥ १९ ॥

धर्म वा मोक्षमार्ग में हो तो भी शुभ (२) । अथवा काममार्ग में सूर्य, धर्ममार्ग में वा मोक्षमार्ग में
content_en:
[ṭīkā] [Commentary continuing on vv. 16–17:] The nakṣatra (lunar mansions) Svātī, Bharaṇī, Āśleṣā, Dhaniṣṭhā, Revatī, Hasta, Anurādhā, Punarvasu, the three Uttarā and Rohiṇī; the odd tithi (lunar days) 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15; and the vāra (weekdays) of the Sun, Moon, Saturn and Jupiter — these are designated akula. Wednesday; the nakṣatra Mūla, Śatabhiṣā, Ārdrā and Abhijit; and the tithi 10, 6, 2 — these are designated kulākula. The three Pūrvā, Aśvinī, Puṣya, Maghā, Mṛgaśira, Śravaṇa, Kṛttikā, Viśākhā, Jyeṣṭhā and Citrā; Friday and Tuesday; and the tithi 12, 8, 14, 4 — these are designated kula. If the war-march falls under the akula members, the yāyī (the king marching out) is victorious; under the kula members, the sthāyī (the king holding his ground) is victorious; under the kulākula members both are victorious, that is, there is saṃdhi (a truce). || 16 || || 17 || (Va. Ti.; Śā. Vi.)

THE PATHI-RĀHU-CAKRA (the wheel of Rāhu upon the road)

Dasra (Aśvinī), Puṣya, Uraga (Āśleṣā), Vasu (Dhaniṣṭhā), Jala (Śatabhiṣā), [?] and Maitra (Anurādhā) [belong to the dharma quarter]; then in artha, the constellations Yāmya (Bharaṇī), Ajapāda (Pūrvabhādrapadā), Indra (Jyeṣṭhā), Karṇa (Śravaṇa), Aditi (Punarvasu), Pitṛ (Maghā) and Pavana (Svātī); then in kāma, those named Vahni (Kṛttikā), Ārdrā, Budhnya (Uttarabhādrapadā), Citrā, Nirṛti (Mūla), Vidhi (Abhijit) and Bhaga (Pūrvāphalgunī); then in mokṣa, Rohiṇī, Aryaman (Uttaraphalgunī), Āp (Pūrvāṣāḍhā), Indu (Mṛgaśira), Viśve (Uttarāṣāḍhā), the last constellation (Revatī) and Dinakara (Hasta) — [thus stand the constellations] in the Rāhu-of-the-road [cakra]. || 18 ||

[ṭīkā] Aśvinī, Puṣya, Āśleṣā, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣā, Viśākhā and Anurādhā — write these nakṣatra in the dharma place; Bharaṇī, Pūrvabhādrapadā, Jyeṣṭhā, Śravaṇa, Punarvasu, Maghā and Svātī in the artha place; Kṛttikā, Ārdrā, Uttarabhādrapadā, Citrā, Mūla, Abhijit and Pūrvāphalgunī in the kāma place; and Rohiṇī, Uttaraphalgunī, Pūrvāṣāḍhā, Mṛgaśira, Uttarāṣāḍhā, Revatī and Hasta are to be set down in the mokṣa path. This is the pathi-rāhu-cakra. || 18 || (Sragdharā metre)

[A cakra (diagram) is printed here; only the cell-labels "Kṛ.", "Ā.", "U. Phā." and "Ci." survive the scan.[?]]

THE RESULT OF THE PLANETS IN THE RĀHU-CAKRA

The Sun in dharma with the Moon in vitta (artha) or mokṣa; [the Sun] in vitta with [the Moon's] station in dharma or mokṣa — [these] are commended. When [the Sun] goes to kāma, [the Moon] going to dharma, mokṣa or artha is excellent; when [the Sun] is in mokṣa, only [the Moon] going to dharma is declared [good]. || 19 ||

[ṭīkā] The Sun in the dharma path and [the Moon] in the artha path or the mokṣa path — auspicious (1). If the Sun is in the [artha] path and the Moon in the dharma or mokṣa path — also auspicious (2). Or the Sun in the kāma path, and in the dharma path or the mokṣa path…
ocr_review_note: Two flags. (i) Mūla v.18 pāda 1: the deity-name standing for Viśākhā is illegible, 2–3 akṣaras uncertain; the rest of pāda 1 and all of pādas 2–4 decode securely against the ṭīkā. (ii) The printed cakra between v.18 and the v.19 heading is reduced to scattered cell-labels; its grid cannot be reconstructed from this scan.

इन चार श्लोकों का अर्थ चक्र से प्रकट होता है । पौष महीने की प्रतिपदादि १२ तिथि
क्रम से लिखनी, माघ की द्वितीयादि, एवं फाल्गुन ३, चैत्र ४, वैशाख ५, ज्येष्ठ ६, आषाढ ७, श्रावण
८, भाद्रपद ९, आश्विन १०, कार्तिक ११, मार्गशीर्ष की १२ से लिखना । त्रयोदशी तृतीया के
तुल्य, चतुर्दशी चतुर्थी के, पंचदशी पंचमी के तुल्य जानना । फल इनके पूर्वादिक्रम से चक्र में लिखे
हैं वही जानने ॥ २०–२३ ॥ (शा०)

तिथ्यक्षवारयुतिरद्रिगजाग्निहृता स्थानत्रयेऽब्जवियति प्रथमेऽतिदुःख[?]-
ती । मध्ये धनक्षतिरथो चरमे मृतिः स्यात्स्थानत्रयेऽङ्कयुजि सौख्य-

तिथि यहाँ शुक्लपक्षादि ली जाती है । तिथि नक्षत्र वार जोड़कर ३ जगह रखना; एक
जगह ७ से, दूसरे ८ से, [तीसरे ३ से][?] भाग लेना । प्रथम में शून्य हो तो यात्री दुःखी हो, दूसरे में शून्य हो तो
धनहानि, तीसरे में शून्य हो तो मृत्यु हो । यदि तीनों स्थानों में अंक हों तो सौख्य तथा जय हो
॥ २४ ॥ (वसन्ततिलका)

आडलभ्रमणदोषौ

रवेर्भतोऽब्जभोन्मितिर्नगावशेषिता [?] ।
महाडलो न शस्यते त्रिषण्मिताद्‌ भवेत् ॥ २५ ॥

सूर्यनक्षत्र से चन्द्रनक्षत्रपर्यन्त गिनना; जितना हो उसमें ७ से भाग दे । यदि ७ शेष रहे
तो महाडल नामा दोष होता है, यह अच्छा नहीं है । यदि ३।६ शेष रहे तो भ्रमण नामा
दोष अशुभ होता है । इसमें यात्रा न करनी, और आड दोष में समस्त शुभकृत्य वर्जित हैं
॥ २५ ॥ (प्रमाणिका)

हिम्बराख्ययोगः

शशाङ्कभं सूर्यभतोऽर्क गण्यं पक्षादितिथ्या दिनवासरेण ।
युतं नवाप्तं नगशेषकं चेत्स्याद्धिम्बरं तद्‌ गमनेऽतिशस्तम् ॥ २६ ॥

सूर्यनक्षत्र से चन्द्रमा के नक्षत्रपर्यन्त जितने हों उसमें प्रतिपदादि वर्तमान तिथि तथा वार
नक्षत्र जोड़ ९ से भाग लेना; ७ शेष रहे तो हिम्बराख्य योग होता है, यह अतिशुभ है । ये गुण-
दोष दक्षिणात्यों में प्रसिद्ध हैं ॥ २६ ॥ (उ० जा०)
content_en:
[ṭīkā] The sense of these four verses [20–23] emerges from the diagram. For the month of Pauṣa write the twelve tithi (lunar days) in order beginning from pratipadā; for Māgha begin from dvitīyā; likewise Phālguna from the 3rd, Caitra from the 4th, Vaiśākha from the 5th, Jyeṣṭha from the 6th, Āṣāḍha from the 7th, Śrāvaṇa from the 8th, Bhādrapada from the 9th, Āśvina from the 10th, Kārttika from the 11th and Mārgaśīrṣa from the 12th. Know trayodaśī as equivalent to tṛtīyā, caturdaśī to caturthī, and pañcadaśī to pañcamī. The results are written in the diagram in the order east and so on; take them exactly so. || 20–23 || (Śā.)

The sum of tithi, ṛkṣa (= nakṣatra, lunar mansion) and vāra (weekday), divided in three separate places by the mountains (7), the elephants (8) and fire (3), — if in the first place [the remainder is] nought, [the traveller becomes] utterly wretched[?]; in the middle, loss of wealth; and in the last, death results. If in [all] three places a figure is left over, comfort and victory are declared. || 24 ||

[ṭīkā] Tithi here is taken from the beginning of the śukla-pakṣa. Add the tithi, the nakṣatra and the vāra, and set the sum down in three places; divide the one by 7, the second by 8, [and the third by 3][?]. If the first leaves zero, the traveller will be wretched; if the second leaves zero, loss of wealth; if the third leaves zero, death. If all three places leave a figure, then comfort and victory. || 24 || (Vasantatilakā)

THE ĀḌALA AND BHRAMAṆA DOṢA (afflictions)

The measure from the Sun's constellation to the Moon's constellation, left with the mountains (7) as remainder, [?] — the Mahāḍala is not commended; from a remainder of three or six it [the other, Bhramaṇa] arises. || 25 ||

[ṭīkā] Count from the Sun's nakṣatra up to the Moon's nakṣatra; divide that figure by 7. If 7 remains, the doṣa named Mahāḍala occurs — this is not good. If 3 or 6 remain, the inauspicious doṣa named Bhramaṇa occurs. One should not travel in these; and in the Āḍa doṣa every auspicious undertaking is forbidden. || 25 || (Pramāṇikā)

THE YOGA NAMED HIMBARA

The Moon's constellation is to be reckoned from the Sun's constellation; joined with the tithi counted from the beginning of the pakṣa and with the weekday, [the sum] divided by nine — if the remainder is the mountains (7), that is Himbara, and it is most excellent for setting out. || 26 ||

[ṭīkā] Whatever the count from the Sun's nakṣatra up to the Moon's nakṣatra, add to it the current tithi reckoned from pratipadā, together with the vāra and the nakṣatra, and divide by 9. If 7 remains, the yoga named Himbara occurs; this is most auspicious. These merits and defects are well known among the southerners. || 26 || (U. Jā.)
ocr_review_note: Three flags. (i) v.24 pāda 1 end: breaks across the line — 1–2 akṣaras lost; read tentatively as 'अतिदुःखी'. (ii) The v.24 ṭīkā names only two divisors (7 and 8) for three places, while the mūla compound gives three (7, 8, 3); the third divisor has been supplied in brackets from the mūla and flagged — it is not in the scan. (iii) v.25 pāda 1: the word after 'नगावशेषिता' is not securely readable; the arithmetic itself is confirmed by the ṭīkā.

[परिधिदंड-चक्रम् — केवल 'पू०', 'आ०' पठनीय]

विदिक्षुगमने नक्षत्राणि परिघापवादश्च

अग्नेर्दिशं नृप[?] प्रदक्षिणगता विदिशोऽथ कृत्वा ।
आवश्यकेऽपि परिधिं प्रविलङ्घ्य गच्छेच्छूलं विहाय यदि दिक्-
लग्नशुद्धिरस्ति ॥ ३७ ॥

विदिशाओं के लिये कहते हैं कि — पूर्वदिशागमनोक्त नक्षत्रों में आग्नेय, दक्षिणोक्तों में
नैऋत्य, पश्चिमोक्तों में वायव्य, उत्तरोक्तों में ईशान यात्रा राजा करे । आवश्यक कृत्य में
परिधिदंड-उल्लंघन करके भी यात्रा करनी, परन्तु वारशूल, नक्षत्रशूल न हों और दिग्लग्न-
शुद्धि हो — १।५।९ पूर्व, २।६।१० दक्षिण, ३।७।११ पश्चिम, ४।८।१२ उत्तर-
गत राशि हैं; इनकी "शुद्धि" सम्मुख दक्षिणादि तथा इनके अंशादिकों की भी होनी चाहिये
॥ ३७ ॥ (वसन्ततिलका)

मैत्रार्कपुष्याश्विनभैरुक्ता यात्रा शुभा सर्वदिशासु तज्ज्ञैः ।
[?] वक्रगतोऽत्र [?] ऋक्षं दिनं चास्य गमे निषिद्धम् ॥ ३८ ॥

[स] अनुराधा हस्त पुष्य अश्विनी नक्षत्र दिश्शूलहर हैं; ज्योतिष जाननेवाले आचार्यों ने
इनमें सभी दिशाओं की यात्रा शुभ कही है । यात्रालग्न में वक्री ग्रह[?] हो तो न लेना, तथा
वक्री ग्रह का ऋक्ष, नवांशक और वार भी न लेना; यात्राभंग करता है ॥ ३८ ॥ (इन्द्रवज्रा)

[A diagram of the paridhi-daṇḍa (the "boundary rod") is printed here; only the labels "pū." (east) and "ā." (āgneya, south-east) survive the scan.]

NAKṢATRA FOR TRAVEL TOWARD THE INTERMEDIATE QUARTERS, AND THE EXCEPTION TO THE PARIDHI

[?] the king [should travel] to the quarter of Agni (south-east), the intermediate quarters being taken in clockwise order [from the cardinal ones]. Even in a necessary undertaking, one may transgress the paridhi and go — provided one avoids the śūla (the "spear," the barred day/direction) and there is dik-lagna-śuddhi (purity of the lagna for that direction). || 37 ||

[ṭīkā] Concerning the intermediate quarters it is said: in the nakṣatra (lunar mansions) prescribed for going east, let the king travel to the south-east (āgneya); in those prescribed for the south, to the south-west (nairṛtya); in those for the west, to the north-west (vāyavya); in those for the north, to the north-east (īśāna). In a necessary undertaking one may travel even after transgressing the paridhi-daṇḍa, but there must be no vāra-śūla (weekday spear) and no nakṣatra-śūla, and there must be dig-lagna-śuddhi: the signs 1, 5, 9 belong to the east, 2, 6, 10 to the south, 3, 7, 11 to the west, and 4, 8, 12 to the north. Their "purity" must hold for the facing quarter, the right-hand quarter and so on, and for their degrees as well. || 37 || (Vasantatilakā)

By those who know [the science], travel has been declared auspicious in all directions in the constellations Maitra (Anurādhā), Arka (Hasta), Puṣya and Aśvin. [?] a retrograde [planet] here [?]; its ṛkṣa (nakṣatra) and its day are forbidden for setting out. || 38 ||

[ṭīkā] Anurādhā, Hasta, Puṣya and Aśvinī are diś-śūla-hara (removers of the direction-śūla); the ācārya who know jyotiṣa have declared travel in all directions auspicious in these. If there is a retrograde planet in the yātrā-lagna[?], it is not to be taken; and neither the ṛkṣa (nakṣatra), the navāṃśa nor the vāra of a retrograde planet is to be taken — [such a planet] wrecks the journey. || 38 || (Indravajrā)
ocr_review_note: Three flags. (i) v.37 pāda 1: roughly 6–8 akṣaras between 'नृप' and 'प्रदक्षिणगता' are unreadable; the sense is secured by the ṭīkā, but the exact wording is not. (ii) v.38 pāda 3: pāda 3 is largely scan noise; only the retrograde-planet prohibition of pāda 4 is recoverable. (iii) ṭīkā to v.38: 2–3 words corrupt around the condition on the retrograde graha.

(१२६)  मुहूर्तचिन्तामणि  [ यात्रा-

अयनशूलः

सौम्यायने सूर्यविधू तदोत्तरां प्राचीं व्रजेत्तौ यदि दक्षिणायने ।
प्रत्यग्यमाशां च तयोर्दिवानिशं भिन्नायनत्वेऽथ वधोऽन्यथा भवेत् ॥ ३९ ॥

जब सूर्य चन्द्रमा उत्तरायण में हों तो उत्तर-पूर्व की दिग्यात्रा शुभ, और दक्षिणायन में हों तो
पश्चिम-दक्षिण यात्रा शुभ होती है । यदि सूर्य चन्द्रमा भिन्न अयनों में हों तो जिस अयन में
सूर्य है उसकी उत्तर-दक्षिण दिशा में दिन में, जिस अयन में चन्द्रमा है उसकी उक्त दिशा में रात्रि में
जाना । इससे अन्यथा यात्रा करे तो मरण हो ॥ ३९ ॥ (उपजाति)

त्रिधा शुक्रसम्मुखता

उदेति यस्यां दिशि यत्र याति गोलभ्रमाद्वाथ ककुब्भसंस्थ[?] ।
त्रिधोच्यते सम्मुख एव शुक्रो यत्रोदितस्तां तु दिशं न यायात् ॥ ४० ॥

मुनियों ने शुक्र सम्मुख तीन प्रकार से कहा है — जिस दिशा में पूर्व-पश्चिम उदय हो रहा है
उस दिशा जाने में (१); अथवा गोलभ्रमण से दक्षिणगोल वा उत्तरगोल जहाँ हो उस दिशा में
सम्मुख होता है (२); अथवा (ककुब्भ-चक्र) पूर्वादि कृत्तिकादि दिननक्षत्रों में जिसमें शुक्र
है वह नक्षत्र जहाँ है उधर सम्मुख होता है (३) । इन ३ प्रकारों में उदयवाला प्रकार मुख्य है —
जिस दिशा में उदय हो उस दिशा में न जाना । आवश्यक में सम्मुख शुक्र की शांति सविस्तर
वसिष्ठसंहिता में है; उससे भी असमर्थों को दीपिका में दान लिखा है कि — "सितं वस्त्रं सितं
छत्रं हेममौक्तिकसंयुतम् । ततो द्विजातये दद्यात्प्रतिशुक्रप्रशान्तये ॥ १ ॥" अर्थात् श्वेतवस्त्र
श्वेतच्छत्र सुवर्ण मोती विधिपूर्वक ब्राह्मण को प्रतिशुक्र की दोषशांति के लिये दान देवे
॥ ४० ॥ (उपजाति)

तद्वक्रास्तादिदोषः सापवादः

वक्रास्तनीचोपगते भृगोः सुते राजा व्रजन् याति वशं [?] ।
बुधोऽनुकूलो यदि तत्र सञ्चरन् रिपुभ्य एव जयः ॥ ४१ ॥

[वक्र], अस्त, नीचत्वगत हुए में (तथा युद्ध के पराजित हुए) राजा जावे तो

(126)  Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi  [Yātrā-

THE AYANA-ŚŪLA (the "spear" of the solstitial half-year)

When the Sun and Moon are in the saumya (northern) ayana, let one then go north or east; if the two are in the southern ayana, [let one go] west and to the quarter of Yama (south). If the two are in different ayana, [go] by day and by night [respectively, in the quarter of each]; otherwise death results. || 39 ||

[ṭīkā] When the Sun and Moon are both in uttarāyaṇa, a journey to the north or east is auspicious; when they are in dakṣiṇāyana, a journey to the west or south is auspicious. If the Sun and Moon are in different ayana, then travel by day in the north/south direction of the ayana the Sun occupies, and by night in the corresponding direction of the ayana the Moon occupies. If one travels otherwise than this, death results. || 39 || (Upajāti)

THE THREEFOLD "FACING" OF ŚUKRA

[Śukra faces] in the quarter in which it rises and toward which it goes; or by the revolution of the sphere; or by its station in the quarter-constellation[?]. In three ways is Śukra (Venus) said to be sammukha (facing). One should not travel toward the quarter in which it has risen. || 40 ||

[ṭīkā] The sages have declared the facing of Śukra in three ways: (1) by the quarter, east or west, in which it is rising, when one goes in that quarter; (2) by the revolution of the sphere — it faces in whichever hemisphere, southern or northern, it stands; (3) by the quarter-constellation (kakubbha-cakra): among the day-nakṣatra assigned to the quarters, beginning with the east and beginning from Kṛttikā, whichever nakṣatra Śukra occupies, it faces toward where that nakṣatra lies. Of these three modes, the one by rising is primary — one should not go in the quarter in which it rises. When [travel] is unavoidable, the śānti (propitiatory rite) for a facing Śukra is given at length in the Vasiṣṭha-saṃhitā; and for those unequal even to that, the Dīpikā prescribes a gift: "White cloth, a white parasol, together with gold and pearl — these one should then give to a twice-born, for the appeasement of the pratiśukra (adverse Venus). || 1 ||" That is, one should give white cloth, a white parasol, gold and pearl to a brāhmaṇa with due rite, for the appeasement of the doṣa (affliction) of pratiśukra. || 40 || (Upajāti)

THAT [ŚUKRA'S] DOṢA OF RETROGRESSION, COMBUSTION AND THE REST, WITH ITS EXCEPTION

When the son of Bhṛgu (Venus) is retrograde, combust, or gone into debility, a king who marches goes into the power of [?] [the enemy]. But if Budha (Mercury) is favourable, moving there, victory over the enemies alone is his. || 41 ||

[ṭīkā] If the king marches while [Venus] is retrograde, combust or in debility (and likewise when he has been defeated in battle), then…
ocr_review_note: Two flags. (i) v.40 pāda 2: the final 2–3 akṣaras of the compound naming the third mode are not securely readable; the ṭīkā confirms the sense. (ii) v.41 pāda 2 is followed by an illegible run before the pāda-break — the word for the enemy is lost; supplied in brackets from the ṭīkā at PG138:C2.

प्रतिशुक्रापवादः

[?]प्रभृत्या कृत्तिकाया[?]पादे शुक्रोऽन्धो न दुष्टो[?] गते ऋक्षे ।
मध्यमार्गे भार्गवेऽस्तेऽपि राजा तत्र[?] तिष्ठेत् सम्मुखत्वेऽपि तस्य ॥ ४२ ॥
content_en:
[ṭīkā] …he will certainly fall into the power (bondage) of the enemy. But if, while Śukra (Venus) is retrograde and so forth, Budha (Mercury) is favourable — that is, at his back — he will conquer the enemy. The same result holds of Mars and Mercury when they stand facing (prati-sammukha) Śukra. || 41 || (Upajāti)

THE EXCEPTION TO PRATIŚUKRA (adverse Venus)

[Beginning from Revatī?][?] up to the [first] quarter of Kṛttikā[?], Śukra is "blind" (andha) and is not evil[?] when [the Moon] has gone into that ṛkṣa (nakṣatra). And should Bhārgava (Venus) set while [the king is] midway on the road, the king should remain right there[?] — even though it is facing him. || 42 ||
ocr_review_note: Four flags in a two-line mūla. (i) v.42 pāda 1 opens with an initial word which must name the nakṣatra from which the andha-śukra span is reckoned (Revatī, per the ṭīkā at PG139:C1), unrecoverable from this scan. (ii) The qualifier on Kṛttikā's pāda is uncertain. (iii) 3–4 akṣaras lost between 'दुष्टः' and 'गते ऋक्षे'. (iv) The adverb before 'तिष्ठेत्' is corrupt. The full sense of v.42 is preserved in the Hindi ṭīkā that opens PG139:C1; it has deliberately NOT been imported into the Devanāgarī of this chunk, and the translation above marks each reconstructed element.

[ ११ प्रकरणम् ]  हिन्दी टीका सहित  (१२७)

जब चन्द्रमा रेवती से कृत्तिका के प्रथमचरणपर्यन्त रहता है उन दिनों शुक्र अंधा कहाता

कुम्भलग्नकुम्भांशकौ त्याज्यौ सर्वदा गमने बुधैः ।
तत्र प्रयातुर्नृपतेर्धननाशः पदे पदे ॥ ४३ ॥

यात्रा में कुम्भलग्न कुम्भांशक जाननेवालों ने सर्वदा त्याग किये हैं; यदि इनमें राजा यात्रा
करे तो पद पद चलने में धन वा प्रयोजन नाश हो ॥ ४३ ॥ (अनु०)

अथ मीनलग्न उत वा तदंशके चलितस्य वक्रमिह वर्त्मनि[?] जायते ।
जनिलग्नजन्मभपती शुभग्रहौ भवतस्तदा तदुदये शुभो गमः ॥ ४४ ॥

राशीश, शुभग्रह लग्न में हों तो उस लग्न में गमन शुभ होता है; जो वे पापग्रह भी हों तथापि
गमनलग्न में शुभ होते हैं । और जन्मनक्षत्र जन्मराशि भी यात्रालग्न में शुभ कही है ॥ ४४ ॥

जन्मराशितनुतोऽष्टमेऽथवा स्वारिभाच्च रिपुभे तनुस्थिते ।
लग्नगास्तदधिपा यदाथवा स्युर्गते हि नृपतेर्मृतिप्रदम् ॥ ४५ ॥

जन्मराशि जन्मलग्न से अष्टम राशि लग्न में तथा स्वकीय शत्रु को जन्मराशि जन्म से

[A column-order dislocation in the scan: the line that opens this chunk — "…bestows what the mind desires. A water sign…" — does not belong here; it is a fragment of the ṭīkā on v.46, which continues at PG139:C2.][?]

[ṭīkā] [continuing on v. 42:] When the Moon stands from Revatī up to the first quarter of Kṛttikā, in those days Śukra (Venus) is called "blind"; therefore it produces no evil result from being sammukha (facing) or dakṣiṇa (on the right hand). And if, having set out on a journey in those days, Śukra should set while one is on the road, the king should remain within that same journey until its heliacal rising; when it rises, let him put it at his back and complete the journey. It is the same with the facing-and-right-hand case: if, having set out at the muhūrta, Śukra becomes facing or on the right before the march is complete, one should remain within that same march until it comes to be on the left or at the back. If Mercury likewise sets while on the road there is no doṣa (affliction); but if Mercury, having risen, comes to face [the traveller], there is doṣa, and one should again remain on the road until its setting. || 42 || (Śālinī)

THE INAUSPICIOUS LAGNA

Kumbha-lagna (Aquarius rising) and the Kumbha aṃśa are always to be shunned for setting out, [say] the wise; for a king who marches in them there is destruction of wealth at every step. || 43 ||

[ṭīkā] Those who know have always rejected Kumbha-lagna and the Kumbha navāṃśa for a journey; if a king travels in them, wealth or purpose is destroyed at every step of the way. || 43 || (Anuṣṭubh)

Now if [the lagna is] Mīna, or its aṃśa, a turning back on the road[?] befalls him who has set out. If the lord of the birth-lagna and the lord of the birth-constellation's sign are benefic planets, then at their rising the setting out is auspicious. || 44 ||

[ṭīkā] If the king departs in Mīna-lagna or the Mīna navāṃśa, he will have to turn back from the road. If the lord of the janma-lagna, the lord of the janma-rāśi, or benefic planets stand in the lagna, then departure in that lagna is auspicious; and even should those [lords] be malefics, they are still auspicious in the lagna of departure. The janma-nakṣatra and janma-rāśi too are said to be auspicious in the yātrā-lagna. || 44 || (Mañjubhāṣiṇī)

When the eighth sign from one's own janma-rāśi and janma-lagna stands as the [yātrā-]lagna, or when the sixth sign from the enemy's constellation stands as the lagna, or when the lords of those signs occupy the lagna — for one who has departed, this brings death upon the king. || 45 ||

[ṭīkā] The eighth sign from the janma-rāśi and janma-lagna standing as the lagna, and the enemy's janma-rāśi reckoned from birth…

(i) The chunk opens with two lines carried in out of place by column-order scrambling in the OCR; the text is legible but belongs to v.46, whose ṭīkā runs at PG139:C2 — its correct position cannot be determined from the scan. (ii) v.44 pāda 2: 'वर्त्मनि' is a probable but not certain reading, and the participle before it is partly effaced.

दत्त्वा दानं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो दिगीशं ध्यात्वा चित्ते भूमिपालोऽधिगच्छेत् ॥ ८३ ॥

[ṭīkā] (concluding verse 79) In these matters — vratabandha (the sacred-thread investiture), deva-pratiṣṭhā (installation of a deity), marriage, festivals such as Holikā, and sūtaka (ritual impurity arising from a birth or from a death) of both kinds — one must not travel until the period laid down for each in its own authority has fully elapsed. Likewise, if lightning or a thunderbolt, thunder of clouds, rain, frost (nīhāra) or snow occurs out of season, one must not travel for seven nights; at their proper season these carry no doṣa (astrological blemish/affliction). || 79 || (metre: Vasantamālikā in the odd pādas)

SPECIAL RULE WHERE DEPARTURE AND ENTRY ARE ACCOMPLISHED IN A SINGLE DAY

(verse 80) When a king's departure from one city and his entry into another fall on a single day, the paṇḍita should never at all consider [the doṣas of] nakṣatra-śūla (the "spike" of the lunar mansion), vāra-śūla (of the weekday), pratiśukra (adverse Venus), and yoginī.

[ṭīkā] If the king's going from one city to another and his entry occur on one and the same day, then only pañcāṅga-śuddhi (the purity of the five limbs of the almanac) is to be examined, as occasion permits. The paṇḍita should not consider these doṣas — nakṣatra-śūla, vāra-śūla, pratiśukra, yoginī. But if the entry into the destination falls on a day other than the day of departure, then all the aforesaid are to be considered. || 80 || (metre: Vaṃśastha)

(verse 81) If a king's departure and entry both occur on one and the same day, then the wise man should consider the time (muhūrta) prescribed for entry; the traveller's muhūrta does not apply there.

[ṭīkā] If the king rises from his house and enters the desired place on the same day, the intelligent one should examine the muhūrta prescribed for entering, and should not consider the muhūrta prescribed for travel. || 81 || (metre: Āryā)

THE DOṢA OF THE NINTH DAY IN SETTING OUT

(verse 82) One should never make the departure reckoned from the entry, nor the entry reckoned from that [departure], on the ninth tithi (lunar day), and likewise not on the ninth nakṣatra or the ninth vāra (weekday).

[ṭīkā] One should not set out again on the ninth tithi, nakṣatra or vāra counted from the house-entry, nor enter again [counted] from the departure. In other treatises it is said that it should not be done in the ninth month or the ninth year either. || 82 || (metre: Āryā)

THE RULE OF OBSERVANCES FOR TRAVEL AND THE LIKE

(verse 83) Having offered oblation into the fire, having worshipped the deity, having bowed to and honoured the brāhmaṇas, having honoured the dig-īśa (regent of the quarter), having given gifts to the brāhmaṇas, and having meditated in his heart upon the dig-īśa, let the lord of the earth set forth.

[ṭīkā] The king, having performed the homa, having worshipped his chosen deity, having saluted the brāhmaṇas, [and having worshipped the lord of] the direction in which he is to go — [the ṭīkā continues in the next chunk]

अश्विन्यादि नक्षत्रोंके दोहद कहते हैं — अश्विनीमें उरद [?], एवं २ में तिल चावल, ३ में उरद, ४ में गौका दही, ५ में गौका घी, ६ में दूध, ७ में हरिणका मांस, ८ में हरिणका रुधिर, ९ में पायस, १० में चाषपक्षीका मांस, ११ में मृगमांस, १२ में शशका मांस, १३ में (साठी) धान, १४ में (प्रियंगु) कांगनी, १५ में पक्वान्न, १६ में (चित्रपक्षी) तीतर, १७ में उत्तम फल, १८ में कछुएका मांस, १९ में (सारिका) मैनाका मांस, २० में गोधाका मांस, २१ में (शल्य) शल्यकका मांस, २२ में (हविष्य) मुद्गादि, २३ में खिचड़ी, २४ में (मुद्गान्न) मूंगकी खिचड़ी, २५ में जौका सत्तू, २६ में मच्छी मांस सहित भात, २७ में अनेक पक्वान्न, २८ में दही भात — इन वस्तुओंको देश कुल आचारके अनुसार खाना वा देखना, सूंघना वा स्पर्श करना; इस कृत्यसे नक्षत्रोक्त दोष नहीं होता ॥ ८४ ॥ ८५ ॥ (शार्दूल)

आज्यं तिलौदनं मत्स्यं पयश्चापि यथाक्रमम् ।
भक्षयेद्दोहदं दिश्यमाशां पूर्वादिकां व्रजेत् ॥ ८६ ॥
दिशाओंके दोहद — पूर्वदिशा जानेमें घी, दक्षिण जानेमें तिलमिश्रित भात, पश्चिम जानेमें मछली, उत्तर जानेमें दूध खाकर जाना; इससे कोई भी दुष्ट फल नहीं होता ॥ ८६ ॥ (अनुष्टुप्)

रसालं पायसं कांजिकं शृतं दुग्धं तथा दधि ।
पयोऽशृतं तिलान्नं च भक्षयेद्वारदोहदम् ॥ ८७ ॥
वारदोहद — रविवारको शिखरण, चन्द्रको पायस, मंगलको कांजिक, बुधको गरम किया
content_en:
(verse 84, continued from the previous chunk; the mūla is heavily damaged in the scan) ... the flesh, and likewise the blood of that same [deer]; so too pāyasa (milk-rice), and the flesh of the cāṣa bird [?], of the hare [?]; and ṣaṣṭika rice, and priyaṅgu millet, or apūpa (fried cake), the citra bird [partridge], ripe fruit [?] || 84 ||

(verse 85) Tortoise, the flesh of the sārikā and of the godhā, the flesh of the śalyaka (porcupine), haviṣya food [?], kṛsara [?], or mudga-rice, and barley-meal; rice with fish [?], variegated cooked food, or curd-rice [?] — in due order. Having considered this list of edibles, the intelligent man should eat [the item prescribed], or else look upon it. || 85 ||

[ṭīkā] The dohada (prescribed craving-offering) for the nakṣatras beginning with Aśvinī is now stated. In Aśvinī, urad [?]; in the 2nd (Bharaṇī), sesame and rice; in the 3rd, urad; in the 4th, cow's curd; in the 5th, cow's ghee; in the 6th, milk; in the 7th, deer flesh; in the 8th, deer blood; in the 9th, pāyasa; in the 10th, the flesh of the cāṣa bird (blue jay); in the 11th, deer flesh; in the 12th, hare flesh; in the 13th, ṣaṣṭika (sāṭhī) rice; in the 14th, priyaṅgu (kāṅganī millet); in the 15th, cooked sweets (pakvānna); in the 16th, the citra bird (partridge); in the 17th, choice fruit; in the 18th, tortoise flesh; in the 19th, the flesh of the sārikā (mynah); in the 20th, the flesh of the godhā (monitor lizard); in the 21st, the flesh of the śalyaka (porcupine); in the 22nd, haviṣya food (mudga and the like); in the 23rd, khicaṛī; in the 24th, mudga khicaṛī; in the 25th, barley sattu; in the 26th, rice together with fish; in the 27th, various cooked sweets; in the 28th, curd-rice. These substances are to be eaten — or, according to the custom of one's country and family, to be looked at, smelled, or touched. By this act the doṣa declared for the nakṣatra does not arise. || 84 || 85 || (metre: Śārdūlavikrīḍita)

(verse 86) Ghee, sesame-rice, fish, and milk respectively — one should eat the dohada belonging to the direction, and [then] proceed towards the quarter, beginning with the east.

[ṭīkā] The dohadas of the directions: when going east, ghee; when going south, rice mixed with sesame; when going west, fish; when going north, milk — one goes after taking these. By this no evil result whatever occurs. || 86 || (metre: Anuṣṭubh)

(verse 87) Rasāla (sweetened curd), pāyasa, kāñjika (sour gruel), boiled milk, and curd; unboiled milk, and sesame-rice — one should eat [these as] the dohada of the vāra (weekday).

[ṭīkā] The vāra-dohada: on Sunday śikharaṇa (śrīkhaṇḍa); on Monday pāyasa; on Tuesday kāñjika; on Wednesday, [milk] that has been warmed — [the ṭīkā continues in the next chunk]

प्रकरणम्‌ ११] हिन्दी टीका सहित (१३७)

तिथिदोहद — १ प्रतिपदाको आकके पत्र, २ को बबूलोंका धोवन, ३ को घी, ४ को यवागू, ५ को हविष्यान्न, ६ को सोनेका धोवन, ७ को पुआ, ८ को बिजौरा फल, ९ को जल, १० को गोमूत्र, ११ को जौ, १२ को पायस, १३ को गुड़, १४ को रुधिर, १५ को मुद्गान्न लाके प्राशन [?] करना ॥ ८८ ॥ (वसन्ततिलका)

गमनसमयविधिः
उद्धृत्य [?] पादमत एव दक्षिणं द्वात्रिंशत्पदमभिगम्य दिव्यं यानम् ।
आरोहेत्तिलघृतहेमताम्रपात्राणि दत्त्वादौ गणकवराय च प्रगच्छेत् ॥ ८९ ॥
राजा यात्रा समयमें प्रथम दाहिना पैर उठाके ३२ पैर पैदल चले, फिर वक्ष्यमाण सवारीमें आरोहण करे; उस समय ज्योतिषीको तिल, घी, सुवर्ण, तांबेका पात्र दान दे, यथाशक्ति भूयसी दक्षिणा देके गमन करे ॥ ८९ ॥ (प्रहर्षिणी)

दिश्ययानानि
प्राच्यां गच्छेद्गजेनैव दक्षिणस्यां रथेन [?] ।
दिशि प्रतीच्यामश्वेन तथोदीच्यां नरैः [?] ॥ ९० ॥
पूर्वदिशाकी यात्रामें हाथी, दक्षिणको रथ, पश्चिमको घोड़ा, उत्तरको मनुष्योंकी सवारीमें जाना ॥ ९० ॥ (अनुष्टुप्)

प्रस्थानविचारः
देवगृहाद्वा गुरुसदनाद्वा स्वगृहान्मुख्यकलत्रगृहाद्वा ।
प्राश्य हविष्यं विप्रानुमतः पश्यन्शृण्वन्मङ्गलमेयात् ॥ ९१ ॥
यात्रासमयमें देवताका पूजनगृहसे अथवा गुरुस्थानसे अथवा अपने शयनस्थान (आवास)से अथवा बहुत स्त्री सम्भवमें मुख्य स्त्री (पटरानी)के घरसे (हविष्य) यज्ञभाग हवनान्तमें प्राशन करके (ब्राह्मणानुमत) ब्राह्मण 'इदं विष्णुः' इत्यादि मन्त्रसे प्रथम पैर उठाकर जानेको आज्ञा देता है; तथा मंगलशब्द, गीत, वाद्य, कलशादि सुनता-देखता गमन करे ॥ ९१ ॥ (पादाकुलक)

कार्याद्यदिह गमनस्य वै विलम्बः [?] भूदेवादिभिरुपवीतमायुधं वा ।
क्षौद्रं चामलफलमाशु चालनीयं सर्वेषां भवति यदेव [?]
तभी यदि कार्यवशात् गमनमें विलम्ब हो तो ब्राह्मण यज्ञोपवीत, [क्षत्रिय] शस्त्र, वैश्य [?] ... आगे चला दे । इसे प्रस्थान कहते हैं, अथवा सभी ...
content_en:
[ṭīkā] (concluding verse 88 — the tithi-dohada) The dohada of the tithis (lunar days): on the 1st (pratipadā), leaves of arka; on the 2nd, the water in which babūla has been washed; on the 3rd, ghee; on the 4th, yavāgū (barley gruel); on the 5th, haviṣya food; on the 6th, the water in which gold has been washed; on the 7th, puā (fried cake); on the 8th, the bijaurā (citron) fruit; on the 9th, water; on the 10th, cow's urine; on the 11th, barley; on the 12th, pāyasa; on the 13th, jaggery; on the 14th, blood; on the 15th, mudga-rice — these are to be fetched and consumed [?]. || 88 || (metre: Vasantatilakā)

THE PROCEDURE AT THE MOMENT OF DEPARTURE

(verse 89) Having raised [?] the right foot first, and having gone thirty-two paces [on foot], let him mount the excellent conveyance; and having first given sesame, ghee, gold and a copper vessel to the best of the astrologers, let him proceed.

[ṭīkā] At the time of the journey the king should first raise his right foot and walk thirty-two paces on foot; then he should mount the conveyance to be described below. At that time he should give the jyotiṣī sesame, ghee, gold and a copper vessel in dāna, and having given as generous a dakṣiṇā as he is able, he should set out. || 89 || (metre: Praharṣiṇī)

CONVEYANCES PROPER TO EACH DIRECTION

(verse 90) To the east let him go by elephant; to the south by chariot [?]; in the western quarter by horse; and to the north, by men [?].

[ṭīkā] For a journey to the east, an elephant; to the south, a chariot; to the west, a horse; to the north, one goes in a conveyance borne by men. || 90 || (metre: Anuṣṭubh)

CONSIDERATION OF THE PRASTHĀNA (FORMAL SETTING-FORTH)

(verse 91) From the temple, or from the preceptor's house, or from his own house, or from the house of his chief wife — having eaten the haviṣya, authorised by the brāhmaṇas, seeing and hearing what is auspicious, let him go.

[ṭīkā] At the time of the journey [he sets forth] from the house where the deity is worshipped, or from the guru's place, or from his own sleeping quarters (residence), or, where there are many wives, from the house of the chief wife (paṭṭarānī); having consumed the haviṣya, the share of the sacrifice, at the close of the havana; and the brāhmaṇa, with the mantra 'idaṃ viṣṇuḥ' and the rest, gives him leave to go, whereupon he raises his foot first — and he proceeds while seeing and hearing auspicious words, song, instrumental music, full pots and the like. || 91 || (metre: Pādākulaka)

(verse 92, partly illegible) If here, by reason of business, there is delay in the going [?] — then by the brāhmaṇas and the rest, the sacred thread, or a weapon, honey, or the āmalaka fruit is to be sent forward at once; whatever is [dear] to each [?] ...

[ṭīkā] Then, if by reason of some business there is delay in the going, the brāhmaṇa [should send forward] the sacred thread, the [kṣatriya] a weapon, the vaiśya [?] ... he should send it forward. This is called prasthāna (formal setting-forth); or else all [may send forward] — [the ṭīkā continues in the next chunk]

यात्रार्थी राजा यात्रादिनसे ३ रात्र पूर्व दूध न पीवे, तथा पांच रात्रि पूर्व (क्षौर) मुण्डन-श्मश्रुकर्म न करे, और उस दिन शहद न खाय, तैलाभ्यङ्ग न करे, शरीरशोधनार्थ ओषधिप्रयोगसे वमन भी न करे — इतने वस्तु यत्नसे निश्चय वर्जित करे ॥ ९६ ॥

भुक्त्वा गच्छति यदि चेत्तैलगुडक्षारपक्वमांसानि ।
विनिवर्तते स रुग्णः स्त्रीद्विजमवमान्य गच्छतो मरणम् ॥ ९७ ॥

यदि मास[?]चतुष्के पौषमासादिषु वृष्टिर्हि भवेदकालवृष्टिः ।
पशुमनुजपदाङ्किता न यावद्वसुधा स्यान्न हि तावदेव दोषः ॥ ९८ ॥

अल्पायां वृष्टौ दोषोऽल्पो भूयस्यां [?] जीमूतानां [?] दुष्टो वा जातायां भूपः ।
सूर्येन्द्वोर्बिम्बे सौवर्णे कृत्वा विप्रेभ्यो दद्याद्दुःशकुने साज्यं सवर्णं दत्त्वा गच्छेत्स्वेच्छया ॥ ९९ ॥
... भी अल्प है; बहुत वर्षामें दोष होता है, यात्रा न करनी; यदि [?] वर्षाका भी यात्री राजाको दोष है । इतने दोषोंमें भी यदि आवश्यक यात्रा हो तो सुवर्णके सूर्य-चन्द्रमाके बिम्ब दान करके ब्राह्मणोंको देवे । यदि यात्रासमयमें दुःशकुन हो तो घी-सुवर्ण दान करके स्वेच्छासे गमन करे ॥ ९९ ॥ (अति-
content_en:
[ṭīkā] (concluding verse 96) The king who intends to travel should not drink milk for three nights before the day of the journey; for five nights before he should not have his head shaved or his beard trimmed (kṣaura); on that day he should not eat honey, should not take an oil-massage, and should not induce vomiting by the use of medicine for cleansing the body. All these he should scrupulously and without fail avoid. || 96 ||

(verse 97) If he goes having eaten things cooked in oil, jaggery, alkaline food, or cooked flesh, he turns back sick; and for one who goes after dishonouring a woman or a brāhmaṇa, there is death.

[ṭīkā] If the traveller sets out after eating things fried in oil, jaggery, or alkaline food and cooked meat of a kind other than the prescribed dohada, he falls ill and returns; if he goes having dishonoured a woman or a brāhmaṇa by abuse or by striking, then on that journey there is death — and death is of eight kinds, not merely the abandoning of the body. || 97 || (metre: Gīti)

THE DOṢA OF UNTIMELY RAIN

(verse 98) If rain falls in the four months [?] beginning with Pauṣa, that indeed is untimely rain (akāla-vṛṣṭi); but so long as the earth is not marked by the footprints of beasts and men, just so long there is no doṣa at all.

[ṭīkā] If rain falls in the four months from Pauṣa up to Caitra, it is called untimely rain in countries other than the mountain regions; or again, in whatever country a given season is not the rainy season, if rain falls then it is a doṣa for travel. But so long as the rain is not enough for the footprints of animals and men to be impressed upon the ground, that much rain carries no doṣa; when the footmark can be impressed, then there is a doṣa. || 98 || (metre: Vasantamālā)

(verse 99, partly corrupt) When the rain is slight the doṣa is slight; when it is heavy [?] ... [the sound] of the clouds [?] ... or when an evil [portent] has arisen, the king, having made discs of the Sun and the Moon in gold, should give them to the brāhmaṇas; and on a bad omen, having given ghee together with gold, he may go according to his own wish.

[ṭīkā] (concluding verse 109) Praveśa (entry) — the entry of a new bride is of four kinds: sapūrva, apūrva, dvandva, and bhaya [?]; it is to be done in the mṛdu (soft) and dhruva (fixed) nakṣatras. If the entry is made in the kṣipra (swift) or cara (movable) nakṣatras, there will be a further departure; in Viśākhā there is destruction of the wife; in Kṛttikā, destruction of the house by fire and the like; in the dāruṇa (harsh) nakṣatras, loss of a son; in the ugra (fierce) nakṣatras, one's own destruction. || 109 || (metre: Upajāti of the Jagatī class)

(verses 110–112: the collected doṣas. The mūla is a compressed catalogue of technical names and is substantially corrupt; the translation follows the ṭīkā, which decodes each term. Flagged readings are marked.)

(verse 110) The śūlas arising from the ayana (solstitial half-year), the nakṣatra, the month, the tithi, the kāla and the vāra; the cara [?]; [the doṣa of] Venus and Mercury facing [the traveller] and the [adverse] quarters they hold [?]; [the doṣas] named after Venus, retrogression and the rest, and the parigha-daṇḍa; likewise the menses of one's wife, ritual impurity, and festivals and the like [that bar departure].

(verse 111) Mṛta-pakṣa; the riktā tithis and those numbering twelve and six; the weekdays of Saturn, the Sun and Mars; also the Moon standing behind or to the left, and likewise [Mahāḍala] [?]; the pañcaka beginning with Dhaniṣṭhā; and also the Abhijit muhūrta, for a southward [journey].

(verse 112) As lagna: the natal lagna, the natal sign [?], the eighth [sign], and the sixth place [from the lagna] and its lord [?]; also Aquarius and Pisces as lagna or as navāṃśa, and a pṛṣṭhodaya (hind-rising) sign; [a lagna] falling in the nakṣatra of the quarter behind [?]; Saturn in the tenth, and Venus (kāvya) in the seventh; retrograde planets in a kendra, and the weekday of a retrograde planet [?] — and the doṣas declared for marriage: [all these] are not desired.

Here ends the eleventh chapter, on Travel, in the illustrious Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi. || 11 ||

[ṭīkā] The collection of doṣas (doṣa-samuccaya): ayana-śūla, per 'saumyāyane sūryam' etc.; māsa-śūla, of two kinds — for the signs in groups of three beginning with Taurus, the śūla towards the east and the rest, that is one; for the months in groups of three beginning with Kārttika, the śūla towards the east and the rest — these two are [called] kapāla and kaṇṭaka; nakṣatra-śūla and vāra-śūla, per 'na pūrvadiśī' etc.; tithi-śūla, per 'navabhūmyeti'; Venus and Mercury facing [the traveller], per 'sitajñadikkapā' etc.; vakra, asta and parājita and the rest, per 'śukravakrāstanīceti'; parigha-daṇḍa, per 'pūrvādiṣu catur' etc.; the sight of one's own wife's menses; ritual impurity (aśauca); the bar of a marriage or the like; mṛta-pakṣa, per 'tamobhuktatārā' etc.; the riktā tithis 4, 9, 14, and up to 12 [and] 6 [?], and the 15th and 30th tithis; the weekdays of Saturn, the Sun and Mars; and the Moon gone behind; Mahāḍala (the doṣa reckoned by remainder 7 counting from the Sun's nakṣatra to the Moon's, defined at Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi 3.25 above), per 'raverbhe' etc.; the pañcaka beginning with Dhaniṣṭhā; the Abhijit muhūrta for a southward [journey]; and the natal lagna, the natal rāśi, the eighth lagna, the lagna of an enemy's sign, the sixth place from the lagna and its lord, [and reckoned] from one's own natal rāśi — [the ṭīkā continues in the next chunk]

Six other readings remain flagged as originally noted: the mūla of ślokas 110-112 is a dense, heavily corrupted catalogue of technical doṣa-names, and the translation of 110-112 continues to rest on the ṭīkā's decoding, not the corrupt mūla.

content_en:
[ṭīkā] (continuing and concluding verses 110–112, the doṣa-samuccaya) ... the lord of the eighth from the lagna [of one's natal rāśi], and the lord of the sixth from the sign that is the enemy's lagna — [any of] these as the lagna; Aquarius or Pisces as lagna or as navāṃśa; a pṛṣṭhodaya (hind-rising) sign; a lagna contrary to the direction of travel; Saturn in the tenth; Venus in the seventh; a retrograde planet in a kendra, or the weekday of the [lord that is] retrograde — all these aforesaid doṣas are unconditionally to be shunned in travel. And the doṣas declared for marriage — those of 'utpātānsahapātadagdhaiḥ' etc. and of 'sendukarara' etc., the aforesaid doṣas — are likewise to be shunned. Among these, however, the māsa-doṣa (the Sun in Sagittarius and the like) and the yāmitra-doṣa (Venus favourably placed and the like) are simply not doṣas [here]. || 110–112 || (metres: Mañjubhāṣiṇī and Sragdharā)

Here ends the eleventh chapter, on Travel, in the vernacular ṭīkā composed by Mahīdhara upon the illustrious Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi. || 11 ||

content_en:
[ṭīkā] (concluding verse 23) ... at the commencement [of the house], if Venus is in the tenth, Mercury in the eleventh, the Sun anywhere but the lagna [?], and Jupiter in the fourth, the house lives 100 years; and if Jupiter is in the fourth, the Moon in the tenth, and Mars and Saturn in the eleventh, the life of the house is 80 years. || 23 || (metre: Indravajrā)

THE THREE YOGAS OF A HOUSE ENDOWED WITH LAKṢMĪ

(verse 24) When Venus is in its own exaltation and occupies the lagna, or Jupiter [exalted] occupies the fourth (the house-place), or Saturn in its own exaltation occupies the eleventh (lābha) — the house is endowed with Lakṣmī and endures long.

[ṭīkā] Exalted Venus in the lagna (1); or exalted Jupiter in the fourth (2); or Saturn exalted in the seventh sign [Libra] standing in the lābha-bhāva (3) — then that house remains prosperous and very stable. || 24 || (metre: Anuṣṭubh)

THE HOUSE PASSING INTO ANOTHER'S POSSESSION

(verse 25, partly corrupt) Within a short [?] year, if even a single planet standing in an enemy's aṃśa [occupies] the house [i.e. the seventh or tenth], it makes the house subject to another [?] — [but only when] the lord of the varṇa is weak.

[ṭīkā] If from the lagna of the house's commencement even one planet, in an enemy's navāṃśa, stands in the seventh or the tenth bhāva, then that house passes into another's hands within a year — but [this holds only] if the varṇeśa (the lord of the caste-class, the lord of the brāhmaṇas and so forth) is weak; when the varṇeśa is strong, the planet does not give the stated result. || 25 || (metre: Anuṣṭubh)

(verse 26) [A house] made under Puṣya, Dhruva [Rohiṇī], Indu [Mṛgaśira], Hari [Śravaṇa], the serpent-star [Āśleṣā] and Aja [?], together with the vāra (weekday) of Jupiter or of Venus, gives sons and sovereignty; and [a house made] under Viśākhā, Aśvinī, Citrā, Vasu [Dhaniṣṭhā], Pāśin [Śatabhiṣā] and Śiva [Ārdrā] [?], and on the day of Venus, gives wealth and grain.

[ṭīkā] Puṣya, Dhruva [Rohiṇī], Mṛgaśira, Śravaṇa, Āśleṣā, Pūrvāṣāḍhā — the [house-commencement made] on the day in which Jupiter falls among these nakṣatras gives sons and sovereignty; and if the house-commencement is made on the day on which Venus falls in one of Viśākhā, Aśvinī, Citrā, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣā, or Ārdrā, then grain and wealth become abundant. || 26 || (metre: Vasantatilakā)

(verse 27, largely illegible) ... in the corner [?] ... gives affliction by fire and affliction to sons [?] ... [with the] vāra [of Mars, a house so begun] gives comfort and sons.

[ṭīkā] If Mars is joined with the nakṣatras Hasta, Puṣya, Revatī, Maghā, Pūrvāṣāḍhā or Mūla, there is affliction by fire and affliction to sons in the house; and if [the nakṣatra] is one of Rohiṇī, Aśvinī, Citrā or Hasta, and it is also Tuesday [?], then [the house] is a giver of comfort and of sons. || 27 || (metre: Indra-)

सौख्यं चक्रमिदं विलोक्य सुधिया द्वारं विधेयं शुभम् ॥२९॥

इति श्रीमद्दैवज्ञानन्तसुतरामविरचिते मुहूर्तचिन्तामणौ द्वादशं वास्तुप्रकरणम् ॥१२॥

किसी के मत से द्वारचक्र है कि, सूर्य के नक्षत्र से चन्द्रमा के नक्षत्र पर्यन्त ४ नक्षत्र शिर में लक्ष्मीप्राप्ति कराते हैं, एवं ८ चारों कोणों में (उद्वसन) घर में कोई न रहने पावे, फिर ८ शाखाओं में सौख्य, ३ देहली में गृहपति की मृत्यु, फिर ४ मध्य में सौख्य देते हैं। (तथा ग्रन्थान्तरों में पंचांग भी कहा है कि अश्विनी, चित्रा, उत्तरा, स्वाती, रेवती, रोहिणी ये द्वारशाखा, देहली आदि को शुभ हैं; तथा ५।७।९।८ तिथि शुभ, ११।१२।१३[?]।१४ मध्यम, अन्य तिथि अशुभ हैं, वारयोगादि भी शुभ।) इस चक्र को देखकर पंडितजन द्वार का विधान करें ॥२९॥

इति श्रीमुहूर्तचिन्तामणौ महीधरकृतभाषाटीकायां द्वादशं वास्तुप्रकरणम् ॥१२॥

Chapter 12] With the Hindi ṭīkā (151)

**[28]** When the nakṣatras (lunar mansions) of Ajaikapād [Pūrvabhādrapadā], Ahirbudhnya [Uttarabhādrapadā], Śakra [Jyeṣṭhā], Mitra [Anurādhā], Anila [Svātī] and Antaka [Bharaṇī] are joined with Manda (Saturn), and the vāra (weekday) is Mandavāra (Saturday), the house will be one beset by rākṣasas and bhūtas (demons and spirits). (28)

[ṭīkā] Among Pūrvabhādrapadā, Uttarabhādrapadā, Jyeṣṭhā, Anurādhā, Svātī, Revatī and Bharaṇī — whichever of these nakṣatras Saturn occupies, if the vāra is also Saturn's (i.e. Saturday), then that house remains beset by rākṣasas, bhūtas and the like. (28) [Anuṣṭubh metre] [Editorial note: the mūla verse names only six nakṣatras, by their presiding deities; the ṭīkā's list of seven adds Revatī, for which the verse as it stands carries no corresponding deity-name.]

**Dvāra-cakra (the wheel for placing the door)**

**[29]** Counting from the Sun's nakṣatra: with four nakṣatras in the "head", the fruit is Lakṣmī (prosperity); then with the eight corner-nakṣatras, udvasana (the house left uninhabited); then with eight [falling] in the "branches" (śākhā, the doorposts), there is happiness; in the "threshold" (dehalī), with three nakṣatras, the death of the householder; and with the four set in the "middle", happiness. Having examined this cakra (reckoning-wheel), the wise man should set the door auspiciously. (29)

Thus, in the Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi composed by Rāma, son of the illustrious daivajña (astrologer) Ananta, the twelfth section, on Vāstu. (12)

[ṭīkā] According to some, the dvāra-cakra is this: counting from the Sun's nakṣatra up to the Moon's nakṣatra, the first 4 nakṣatras [fall] in the "head" and bring the attainment of Lakṣmī; the next 8, in the four corners, [give] udvasana — no one gets to live in the house; the next 8, in the "branches", happiness; 3, in the "threshold", the death of the householder; and the next 4, in the "middle", happiness. (Other works also give a pañcāṅga reckoning: that Aśvinī, Citrā, Uttarā, Svātī, Revatī and Rohiṇī are auspicious for the doorposts, threshold and so on; and that the tithis (lunar days) 5, 7, 9 and 8 are auspicious, 11, 12, 13[?] and 14 middling, and the remaining tithis inauspicious; the vāra, yoga and the rest should likewise be auspicious.) Having examined this cakra, learned men should ordain the placing of the door. (29)

Thus, in the Hindi ṭīkā made by Mahīdhara on the illustrious Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi, the twelfth section, on Vāstu. (12)

Everything else in this chunk is secure: v.28 scans as an exact anuṣṭubh and v.29 as an exact śārdūlavikrīḍita in all four pādas. Separate, non-OCR textual point recorded in the translation: the mūla names six nakṣatras by deity while the ṭīkā lists seven, adding Revatī.

(152) Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi [Gṛha-praveśa—

**Chapter 13 — Gṛha-praveśa (entry into a house)**

*Purity of time and the rest (kāla-śuddhi)*

**[1]** In the saumya ayana (the northern course of the Sun, uttarāyaṇa); in Jyeṣṭha, Tapas (Māgha), Antya (Phālguna) and Mādhava (Vaiśākha); upon the cessation of a journey; for the king[?], in a new house — the entry[?] should fall in those dvāḥstha (door-governing) nakṣatras (lunar mansions) that are mṛdu (soft) or dhruva (fixed), and when an upacaya house reckoned from the natal ṛkṣa (birth rāśi) and the lagna (ascendant) is rising, or a sthira (fixed) sign. (1)

[ṭīkā] The muhūrta (elected moment) for the re-entry (sa-pūrva praveśa) of a king and others returning from a journey, and for the first-ever entry (apūrva praveśa) into a newly built house and the like: one should enter in the uttarāyaṇa, in the months of Jyeṣṭha, Māgha, Phālguna and Vaiśākha, the time being free of the asta (combustion) and the rest of Venus and Jupiter, and free of the doṣas (afflictions) given in the passage beginning "vāpyārāma…" (Kārttika and Mārgaśīrṣa are also stated, as middling.) The dvāḥstha nakṣatras are those given in the passage beginning "bhāni sthāpyānyabdhidikṣu" — that is, from among the nakṣatras belonging to the direction in which the house's door faces, one takes the mṛdu and dhruva ones; and first entry into a house is auspicious in the upacaya houses — the 3rd, 6th, 10th and 11th from the natal lagna and natal rāśi — and in the sthira (fixed) lagnas. Here too the 21 mahādoṣas (great afflictions) laid down for marriage are excluded. (1)

(30)

*The special rule for entry into an old house*

**[2]** Even in an old house, and even in one damaged by the hazard of fire and the rest, [entry] would be good also in Mārga (Mārgaśīrṣa) and Ūrja (Kārttika), and in Śrāvaṇa; the lineage [prospers] in the nakṣatras of Ambupa (the lord of waters, Varuṇa — Śatabhiṣā), Ijya (Bṛhaspati — Puṣya), Anila (Vāyu — Svātī) and Vāsava (the Vasus — Dhaniṣṭhā); the consideration of asta (combustion) and the rest is not obligatory [here][?]. (2)

[ṭīkā] For entry into an old house — another's, or one built by oneself — and likewise into a house rebuilt after having been destroyed through fire, water, the king and so forth, one should take the months and the rest stated above; and the months of Kārttika, Mārgaśīrṣa and Śrāvaṇa, and the nakṣatras Śatabhiṣā, Puṣya, Svātī and Dhaniṣṭhā, are auspicious as well. Moreover, in such an entry there is no consideration even of the astādi (combustion and the like) of Venus and Jupiter. (2) [Indravajrā metre]

*The Vāstu worship that forms a limb of the house-entry*

**[3]** In the mṛdu, dhruva, kṣipra (swift) and cara (movable) nakṣatras, and in the …[?] nakṣatra, one should have the vāstv-arcana (worship of the Vāstu deity) and the bhūta-bali (offering to the spirits) performed — with benefics placed[?] in the trikoṇa (trines), the kendras (angles), the āya (11th) and the dhana (2nd), and with the malefics gone to the 3rd, 6th and 11th from the lagna. (3)

[ṭīkā] [In] the mṛdu, dhruva, kṣipra and mūla nakṣatras — from the day of entry, the …[?] worship of Vāstu (the bhūta-bali) is to be done, and the bali prescribed in the section on the method of Vāstu worship is also to be performed. As to purity of the lagna, it is said: in the trikoṇa (5th, 9th), the kendras (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th) … [the ṭīkā runs on into the next chunk]

Five flagged readings across vv.1-3, all sense-secured by the ṭīkā despite the corrupt akṣaras. Secure by metre despite the noise: v.2 pādas 1–3 each scan as exact indravajrā, and v.3 pāda 2 as exact indravaṃśā. Note also a mūla/ṭīkā divergence: the verse's 'वासव' is glossed by Mahīdhara as Dhaniṣṭhā (vasu-devatā), not as its usual referent Jyeṣṭhā.
